title: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost, and to the

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost, and to the
Holy Ghost,
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end,
world without end.

title: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost,
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end.

title: Before Jehovah's awful throne
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
His sovereign power, without our aid,
Made us of clay, and formed us men;
And when like wandering sheep we strayed,
He brought us to his fold again.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We are his people, we his care—
Our souls, and all our mortal frame;
What lasting honors shall we rear,
Almighty Maker, to thy name?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We'll crowd thy gates with thankful songs,
High as the heavens our voices raise;
And earth, with her ten thousand tongues,
Shall fill thy courts with sounding praise.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: From all that dwell below the skies
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From all that dwell below the skies
Let the Creator's praise arise;
Let the Redeemer's name be sung,
Through every land, by every tongue.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Your lofty themes, ye mortals, bring,
In songs of praise divinely sing:
The great salvation loud proclaim,
And shout for joy the Savior's name.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Awake, my soul, awake my tongue
author: Anne Steele

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Awake, my soul, awake my tongue,
My God demands the grateful song;
Let all my inmost powers record
The wondrous mercy of the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Divinely free his mercy flows,
Forgives my sins, allays my woes,
And bids approaching death remove,
And crowns me with indulgent love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His mercy, with unchanging rays,
Forever shines, while time decays;
And children's children shall record
The truth and goodness of the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
While all his works his praise proclaim
And men and angels bless his name,
Oh, let my heart, my life, my tongue
Attend, and join the blissful song!

title: Praise God, from whom all blessings flow
author: Thos. Ken

sections.label: Verse 1

title: Lord of all being! throned afar
author: Oliver Wendell Holmes

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord of all being! throned afar,
Thy glory flames from sun and star;
Center and soul of ev'ry sphere,
Yet to each loving heart how near!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sun of our life! thy quick'ning ray
Sheds on our path the glow of day;
Star of our hope! thy softened light
Cheers the long watches of the night.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Grant us thy truth to make us free,
And kindling hearts that burnt for thee,
Till all thy living altars claim
One holy light, one heavenly flame.

title: Come, oh, my soul, in sacred lays
author: Thomas Blacklock

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, oh, my soul, in sacred lays,
Attempt thy great Creator's praise;
But oh! what tongue can speak his fame?
What mortal verse can reach the theme?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Enthroned amidst the radiant spheres,
He glory like a garment wears;
To form a robe of light divine,
Ten thousand suns around him shine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In all our Master's grand designs,
Omnipotence with wisdom shines;
His works, through all this wondrous frame,
Bear the great impress of his name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Raised on Devotion's lofty wing,
Do thou, my soul! his glories sing;
And let his praise employ thy tongue,
Till listening worlds applaud the song.

title: God of my life! through all my days
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of my life! through all my days
My grateful powers shall sound my praise;
The song shall wake with opening light,
And warble to the silent night.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When anxious cares would break my rest,
And griefs would tear my throbbing breast,
Thy tuneful praises, raised on high,
Shall check the murmur and the sigh.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When death o'er nature shall prevail,
And all its powers of language fail,
Joy thro' my swimming eyes shall break,
And mean the thanks I cannot speak.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Soon shall I learn th' exalted strains,
Which echo o'er the heavenly plains,
And emulate, with joy unknown,
The growing seraphs round thy throne.

title: Oh, render thanks to God above
author: Tate-Brady

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, render thanks to God above,
The fountain of eternal love;
Whose mercy firm, through ages past,
Hath stood, and shall forever last.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Who can his mighty deeds express,
Not only vast—but numberless?
What mortal eloquence can raise
His tribute of immortal praise?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Extend to me that favor, Lord,
Thou to thy chosen dost afford;
When thou return'st to set them free.
Let thy salvation visit me.

title: Now to the Lord, a noble song
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now to the Lord, a noble song!
Awake, my soul! awake, my tongue,
Hosanna to th' eternal name,
And all his boundless love proclaim.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
See where it shines in Jesus' face,—
The brightest image of his grace!
God, in the person of his Son,
Has all his mightiest works outdone.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh! may I live to reach the place,
Where he unveils his lovely face,
Where all his beauties you behold,
And sing his name to harps of gold.

title: My God! my King! thy various praise
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God! my King! thy various praise
Shall fill the remnant of my days;
Thy grace employ my humble tongue,
Till death and glory raise the song.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The wings of every hour shall bear
Some thankful tribute to thine ear;
And every setting sun shall see
New works of duty, done for thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But who can speak thy wondrous deeds?
Thy greatness all our thoughts exceeds;
Vast and unsearchable thy ways—
Vast and immortal be thy praise.

title: Oh, come, loud anthems let us sing
author: Nahum Tate

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, come, loud anthems let us sing,
Loud thanks to our Almighty King!
For we our voices high should raise,
When our salvation's Rock we praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Into his presence let us haste,
To thank him for his favors past;
To him address, in joyful songs,
The praise that to his name belongs.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, let us to his courts repair,
And bow with adoration there;
Down on our knees, devoutly, all
Before the Lord, our Maker, fall.

title: Sweet is the work, my God! my King
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet is the work, my God! my King!
To praise thy name, give thanks and sing;
To show thy love by morning light,
And talk of all thy truth at night.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
My heart shall triumph in the Lord,
And bless his works, and bless his word;
Thy works of grace, how bright they shine!
How deep thy counsels! how divine!

title: Hail! great Creator, wise and good
author: Anon

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hail! great Creator, wise and good!
To thee our songs we raise;
Nature, through all her various scenes,
Invites us to thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
At morning, noon, and evening mild,
Fresh wonders strike our view;
And, while we gaze, our hearts exult
With transports ever new.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy glory beams in every star,
Which gilds the gloom of night;
And decks the smiling face of morn
With rays of cheerful light.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And while, in all thy wondrous ways,
Thy varied love we see;
Oh, may our hearts, great God, be led
Through all thy works to thee.

title: My soul shall praise thee, O my God
author: O. Heigenbotham

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My soul shall praise thee, O my God
Through all my mortal days,
And in eternity prolong
Thy vast, thy boundless praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In every smiling, happy hour,
Be this my sweet employ;
Thy praise refines my earthly bliss,
And heightens all my joy.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When anxious grief and gloomy care
Afflict my throbbing breast,
My tongue shall learn to speak thy praise,
And lull each pain to rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Nor shall my tongue alone proclaim
The honors of my God;
My life, with all its active powers,
Shall spread thy praise abroad.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And when these lips shall cease to move,
When death shall close these eyes,
My soul shall then to nobler heights
Of joy and transport rise.

title: Lift up to God the voice of praise
author: Ralph Wardlaw

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lift up to God the voice of praise,
Whose breath our souls inspired;
Loud, and more loud the anthem raise,
With grateful ardor fired.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lift up to God the voice of praise,
Whose goodness, passing thought,
Loads every minute as it flies,
With benefits unsought.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lift up to God the voice of praise
From whom salvation flows,
Who sent his Son, our souls to save
From everlasting woes.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lift up to God the voice of praise,
For hope's transporting ray,
Which lights, through darkest shades of death,
To realms of endless day.

title: Holy, holy, holy! Lord God Almighty
author: Reginald Heber--_alt._

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Holy, holy, holy! Lord God Almighty!
Early in the morning our song shall rise to thee;
Holy, holy, holy! merciful and mighty!
God over all and blest eternally.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Holy, holy, holy! all saints adore thee,
Casting down their golden crowns around the glassy sea;
Cherubim and seraphim falling down before thee,
Who wast, and art, and evermore shall be.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Holy, holy, holy! Lord God Almighty!
All thy works shall praise thy name in earth, and sky, and sea;
Holy, holy, holy, merciful and mighty!
God over all, and blest eternally.

title: Sing to the Lord Jehovah's name
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sing to the Lord Jehovah's name,
And in his strength rejoice;
When his salvation is our theme,
Exalted be our voice.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With thanks approach his awful sight,
And psalms of honor sing;
The Lord's a God of boundless might—
The whole creation's King.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Now is the time—he bends his ear,
And waits for your request;
Come, lest he rouse his wrath, and swear,
"Ye shall not see my rest."

title: Oh, bless the Lord, my soul
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, bless the Lord, my soul!
Let all within me join,
And aid my tongue to bless his name,
Whose favors are divine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, bless the Lord, my soul,
Nor let his mercies lie
Forgotten in unthankfulness,
And without praises die.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis he forgives thy sins—
'Tis he relieves thy pain—
'Tis he that heals thy sicknesses,
And gives thee strength again.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He crowns thy life with love,
When ransomed from the grave;
He who redeemed my soul from hell,
Hath sovereign power to save.

title: Come, sound his praise abroad
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, sound his praise abroad,
And hymns of glory sing;
Jehovah is the sov'reign God,
The universal king.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
To-day attend his voice,
Nor dare provoke his rod;
Come, like the people of his choice,
And own your gracious God.

title: Lift up the Gates of Praise
author: M. E. Servoss

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lift up the Gates of Praise,
That we may enter in,
And o'er salvation's walls proclaim
That Christ redeems from sin.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
The stars may praise the hand
That decks the sky above,
But man alone can tell the pow'r
Of Christ's redeeming love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
God's works reveal his might,
His majesty and grace;
But not the tender Father's love
That saves a dying race.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then let the voice of praise
To heavenly courts ascend,
Till with the songs the angels sing
Our hallelujahs blend.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To him that hath redeemed
Our souls from sin's dark maze;
The Hope and Savior of mankind,
Be everlasting praise.

title: Stand up, and bless the Lord
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Stand up, and bless the Lord,
Ye people of his choice!
Stand up, and bless the Lord, your God,.
With heart, and soul, and voice.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though high above all praise,
Above all blessing high,
Who would not fear his holy name,
And laud and magnify?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, for the living flame
From his own altar brought,
To touch our lips, our minds inspire,
And wing to heaven our thought!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
God is our strength and song,
And his salvation ours;
Then be his love in Christ proclaimed,
With all our ransomed powers.

title: Praise the Lord, ye heavens! adore him
author: John Kempthorne

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Praise the God of our salvation,
Hosts on high! his power proclaim
Heaven and earth, and all creation!
Laud and magnify his name.

title: Thank and praise Jehovah's name
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thank and praise Jehovah's name;
For his mercies, firm and sure,
From eternity the same
To eternity endure.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let the ransomed thus rejoice,
Gathered out of every land;
As the people of his choice,
Plucked from the destroyer's hand.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
For his truth and mercy stand,
Past, and present, and to be,
Like the years of his right hand—
Like his own eternity.

title: Hallelujah! song of gladness
author: Anon

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
sections.text:
Praise ye the Lord! sing Hallelujah!
Praise ye the Lord! sing Hallelujah!
Praise ye the Lord! sing Hallelujah!
Praise ye the Lord!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hallelujah! Church victorious,
Thou mayst lift this joyful strain;
Hallelujah! songs of triumph,
Well befit the ransomed train.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Hallelujah! let our voices
Rise to heav'n with full accord;
Hallelujah! ev'ry moment
Brings us nearer to the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But our earnest supplication,
Holy God, we raise to thee;
Bring us to thy blissful presence.
Let us all thy glory see.

title: Praise to thee, thou great Creator
author: J. W. Fawcett

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Praise to thee, thou great Creator!
Praise to thee from ev'ry tongue;
Join, my soul, with ev'ry creature,
Join the universal song.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Glory to the Father and the Son,
Glory to the Spirit! three in one!
Let us praise him, let us praise him, let us praise him to-day,
And sing his loving kindness on our way.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Father! source of all compassion!
Pure, unbounded grace is thine;
Hail the Lord of our salvation!
Praise him for his love divine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For ten thousand blessings given,
For the hope of future joy,
Sound his praise thro' earth and heaven,
Sound Jehovah's praise on high.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Praise to God, our great Creator!
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost;
Praise him, ev'ry living creature,
Earth and heav'n's united host.

title: O worship the King, all-glorious above
author: Sir Robert Grant

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O worship the King, all-glorious above,
And gratefully sing his wonderful love;
Our Shield and Defender, the Ancient of days,
Pavilioned in splendor and girdled with praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy bountiful care, what tongue can recite?
It breathes in the air, it shines in the light;
It streams from the hills, it descends to the plain,
And sweetly distills in the dew and the rain.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Frail children of dust, and feeble as frail,
In thee do we trust, nor find thee to fail;
Thy mercies, how tender! how firm to the end,
Our Maker, Defender, Redeemer, and Friend!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Our Father and God, how faithful thy love!
While angels delight to hymn thee above,
The humbler creation, though feeble their lays.
With true adoration shall lisp to thy praise.

title: Ye servants of God, your Master proclaim
author: C. Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye servants of God, your Master proclaim,
And publish abroad his wonderful name.
The name, all-victorious, of Jesus extol;
His kingdom is glorious, and rules over all.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
"Salvation to God, who sits on the throne,"
Let all cry aloud, and honor the Son;
Our Savior's high praises the angels proclaim,—
Fall down on their faces, and worship the Lamb.

title: How charming is the place
author: S. Stennett

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How charming is the place
Where my Redeemer God
Unveils the glories of his face,
And sheds his love abroad!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here, on the mercy seat,
With radiant glory crowned,
Our joyful eyes behold him sit,
And smile on all around.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To him their prayers and cries,
Each contrite soul presents;
And while he hears their humble sighs
He grants them all their wants.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Give me, O Lord, a place
Within thy blest abode;
Among the children of thy grace,
The servants of my God.

title: Lord! we come before thee now
author: William Hammond

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Send some message from thy word,
That may joy and peace afford;
Let thy Spirit now impart
Full salvation to each heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Grant that those who seek may find
Thee, a God sincere and kind;
Heal the sick, the captive free,
Let us all rejoice in thee.

title: In thy name, O Lord! assembling
author: Thomas Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
While our days on earth are lengthened,
May we give them, Lord, to thee;
Cheered by hope, and daily strengthened,
May we run, nor weary be,
Till thy glory
Without clouds in heaven we see.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Lord, dismiss us with thy blessing
author: Walter Shirley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
So, whene'er the signal's given,
Us from earth to call away,
Borne on angel's wings to heaven,
Glad the summons to obey,
We shall surely
Reign with Christ in endless day.

title: God of our salvation! hear us
author: Thomas Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
As our steps are drawing nearer
To our everlasting home,
May our view of heaven grow clearer,
Hope more bright of joys to come;
And, when dying,
May thy presence cheer the gloom.

title: Great God! attend while Zion sings
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great God! attend while Zion sings
The joy that from thy presence springs;
To spend one day with thee on earth
Exceeds a thousand days of mirth.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Might I enjoy the meanest place
Within thy house, O God of grace!
Not tents of ease, nor thrones of power,
Should tempt my feet to leave thy door.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
God is our sun, he makes our day;
God is our shield, he guards our way
From all th' assaults of hell and sin,
From foes without and foes within.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
All needful grace will God bestow,
And crown that grace with glory too;
He gives us all things, and withholds
No real good from upright souls.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O God, our King! whose sovereign sway
The glorious hosts of heaven obey,
And devils at thy presence flee;
Blest is the man that trusts in thee!

title: How sweet to leave the world awhile
author: Thomas Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How sweet to leave the world awhile,
And seek the presence of our Lord!
Dear Savior! on thy people smile,
And come, according to thy word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
From busy scenes we now retreat,
That we may here converse with thee:
Ah! Lord! behold us at thy feet;—
Let this the gate of heaven be.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Chief of ten thousand! now appear,
That we by faith may see thy face;
Oh! speak, that we thy voice may hear
And let thy presence fill this place.

title: How pleasant, how divinely fair
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How pleasant, how divinely fair,
O Lord of hosts, thy dwellings are!
With long desire my spirit faints,
To meet the assemblies of thy saints.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Blest are the souls who find a place
Within the temple of thy grace;
There they behold thy gentler rays,
And seek thy face and learn thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blest are the men whose hearts are set
To find the way to Zion's gate;
God is their strength, and through the road
They lean upon their helper, God.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Cheerful they walk with growing strength,
Till all shall meet in heaven at length;
Till all before thy face appear,
And join in nobler worship there.

title: Thy presence, gracious God! afford
author: John Fawcett

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thy presence, gracious God! afford:
Prepare us to receive thy word;
Now let thy voice engage our ear,
And faith be mixed with what we hear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Distracting thoughts and cares remove,
And fix our hearts and hopes above;
With food divine may we be fed
And satisfied with living bread.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To us thy sacred word apply,
With sovereign power and energy;
And may we, in thy faith and fear,
Reduce to practice what we hear.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Command thy blessing from above
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Command thy blessing from above
O God, on all assembled here;
Behold us with a Father's love,
While we look up with filial fear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Command thy blessing, Jesus, Lord!
May we thy true disciples be;
Speak to each heart the mighty word—
Say to the weakest, follow me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Command thy blessing in this hour,
Spirit of truth! and till the place
With wounding and with healing power,
With quickening and confirming grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, thou, our Maker, Savior, Guide,
One true, eternal God confessed;
Whom thou hast joined none may divide,
None dare to curse whom thou hast blest.

title: Again our earthly cares we leave
author: John Newton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Again our earthly cares we leave,
And in thy courts appear;
Again, with joyful feet, we come
To meet our Savior here.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Within those walls let holy peace.
And love, and concord dwell;
Here give the troubled conscience ease—
The wounded spirit heal.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The feeling heart, the melting eye.
The humble mind bestow;
And shine upon us from on high,
To make our graces grow.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
May we in faith receive thy word,
In faith present our prayers;
And in the presence of our Lord,
Unbosom all our cares.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Shew us some token of thy love,
Our fainting hope to raise;
And pour thy blessing from above,
That we may render praise.

title: Oh, thou, whose own vast temple stands
author: William C. Bryant

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, thou, whose own vast temple stands,
Built over earth and sea!
Accept the walls that human hands
Have raised to worship thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord! from thine inmost glory send,
Within these walls t' abide,
The peace that dwelleth without end
Serenely by thy side!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
May erring minds, that worship here,
Be taught the better way;
And they who mourn, and they who fear,
Be strengthened as they pray.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
May faith grow firm, and love grow warm,
And pure devotion rise,
While, round these hallowed walls, the storm
Of earth-born passion dies.

title: How did my heart rejoice to hear
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How did my heart rejoice to hear
My friends devoutly say—
"In Zion let us all appear—
And keep the solemn day!"

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I love her gates, I love the road;
The church, adorned with grace,
Stands like a palace, built for God
To show his milder face.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Up to her courts, with joys unknown,
The holy tribes repair;
The Son of David holds his throne,
And sits in judgment there.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He hears our praises and complaints;
And, while his awful voice
Divides the sinners from the saints,
We tremble and rejoice.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Peace be within this sacred place,
And joy a constant guest!
With holy gifts and heavenly grace
By her attendants blest!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
My soul shall pray for Zion still,
While life or breath remains;
There my best friends, my kindred, dwell,
There God, my Saviour, reigns.

title: Welcome! sweet day of rest
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Welcome! sweet day of rest,
That saw the Lord arise!
Welcome to this reviving breast,
And these rejoicing eyes!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The King himself comes near,
And feasts his saints to-day;
Here we may sit and see him here,
And love, and praise, and pray.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
One day in such a place,
Where thou, my God, art seen,
Is sweeter than ten thousand days
Of pleasurable sin.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My willing soul would stay
In such a frame as this,
And sit and sing herself away
To everlasting bliss.

title: O day of rest and gladness
author: Christopher Wordsworth

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O day of rest and gladness,
O day of joy and light!
O balm of care and sadness,
Most beautiful, most bright!
On thee, the high and lowly,
Before th' eternal throne,
Sing Holy! Holy! Holy!
To the great Three in One.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On thee, at the creation.
The light first had its birth;
On thee for our salvation,
Christ rose from depths of earth.
On thee, our Lord, victorious,
The Spirit sent from heaven,
And thus on thee, most glorious,
A triple light was given.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
New graces ever gaining
From this our day of rest,
We reach the rest remaining
To spirits of the blest;
To Holy Ghost be praises,
To Father and to Son;
The church her voice upraises
To thee, blest Three in One.

title: Come, dearest Lord, and feed thy sheep
author: John Mason

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, dearest Lord, and feed thy sheep,
On this sweet day of rest;
Oh, bless this flock, and make this fold
Enjoy a heavenly rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Welcome, and precious to my soul
Are these sweet days of love;
But what a Sabbath shall I keep
When I shall rest above!

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Those are the sweet and precious days
On which my Lord I've seen;
And oft, when feasting on his word,
In raptures I have been.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Oh, if my soul, when death appears.
In this sweet frame be found,
I'll clasp my Savior in mine arms,
And leave this earthly ground.

title: How sweetly breaks the Sabbath dawn
author: Edwin F. Hatfield

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How sweetly breaks the Sabbath dawn
Along the eastern skies!
So, when the night of time hath gone,
Eternity shall rise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How softly spreads the Sabbath light!
How soon the gloom hath fled!
So o'er the new created sight
Celestial bliss is spread.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
What quiet reigns o'er earth and sea,
Through all the stilly air!
So calm may we this Sabbath be,
And free from worldly care.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thus let thy peace, O Lord! pervade
Our bosoms all our days;
And let each passing hour be made
A herald of thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
This peace of God—how full! how sweet
It flows from Jesus' breast;
It makes our bliss on earth complete,
It brings eternal rest.

title: When the worn spirit wants repose
author: James Edmeston

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When the worn spirit wants repose,
And sighs her God to seek,
How sweet to hail the evening's close
That ends the weary week!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How sweet to hail the early dawn
That opens on the sight,
When first that soul-reviving morn
Sheds forth new rays of light!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sweet day! thine hours too soon will cease;
Yet, while they gently roll,
Breathe, heavenly Spirit, source of peace,
A Sabbath o'er my soul.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When will my pilgrimage be done,
The world's long week be o'er,
That Sabbath dawn which needs no sun,
That day which fades no more?

title: Safely thro' another week
author: John Newton

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
May the gospel's joyful sound
Conquer sinners, comfort saints,
Make the fruits of grace abound,
Bring relief from all complaints;
Thus let all our Sabbaths prove,
Till we join the church above.

title: Welcome, delightful morn
author: Hayward

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Now may the King descend,
And fill his throne of grace;
Thy scepter, Lord, extend,
While saints address thy face!
Let sinners feel thy quickening word,
And learn to know and fear the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Welcome, sacred day of rest
author: William Brown

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Gracious Lord! we love this day,
When we hear thy holy word;
When we sing thy praise, and pray,
Earth can no such joys afford;
But a better rest remains,
Heav'nly Sabbaths, happier days,
Rest from sin, and rest from pains,
Endless joys and endless praise.

title: Softly fades the twilight ray
author: Samuel F. Smith

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Softly fades the twilight ray
Of the holy Sabbath day;
Gently as life's setting sun,
When the Christian's course is run.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Night her solemn mantle spreads
O'er the earth as daylight fades;
All things tell of calm repose
At the holy Sabbath's close.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Peace is on the world abroad;
'Tis the holy peace of God—
Symbol of the peace within,
When the spirit rests from sin.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Savior, may our Sabbaths be
Days of peace and joy in thee,
Till in heav'n our souls repose,
Where the Sabbath ne'er shall close.

title: Awake, my soul, and with the sun
author: Bp. Ken

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Awake, my soul, and with the sun
Thy daily stage of duty run;
Shake off dull sloth, and joyful rise
To pay thy morning sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Awake, lift up thyself, my heart,
And with the angels bear thy part,
Who all night long unwearied sing
High praises to th' eternal King.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Glory to thee, who safe hast kept,
And hast refreshed me when I slept;
Grant, Lord, when I from death shall wake,
I may of endless life partake.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: See how the morning sun
author: T. Scott

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
See how the morning sun
Pursues his shining way;
And wide proclaims his Maker's praise,
With ev'ry bright'ning ray.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thus would my rising soul
Its heavenly Parent sing,
And to its great Original
The humble tribute bring.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Serene I laid me down,
Beneath his guardian care;
I slept, and I awoke, and found
My kind Preserver near.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My life I would anew
Devote, O Lord, to thee;
And in thy service I would spend
A long eternity.

title: Savior, breathe an evening blessing
author: James Edmeston

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Savior, breathe an evening blessing,
E'er repose our spirits seal;
Sin and want we come confessing,
Thou canst save and thou canst heal.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though destruction walk around us,
Though the arrows past us fly;
Angel guards from thee surround us,
We are safe if thou art nigh.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Though the night be dark and dreary,
Darkness cannot hide from thee;
Thou art he who, never weary,
Watchest where thy people be.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Should swift death this night o'ertake us,
And our couch become our tomb,
May the morn in heaven awake us,
Clad in bright and deathless bloom.

title: Sun of my soul, thou Savior dear
author: Rev. J. Keble

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sun of my soul, thou Savior dear,
It is not night if thou be near;
Oh, may no earth-born cloud arise
To hide thee from thy servant's eyes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When the soft dews of kindly sleep
My weary eye-lids gently steep,
Be my last thought, how sweet to rest
Forever on my Savior's breast.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Abide with me from morn till eve,
For without thee I cannot live;
Abide with me when night is nigh,
For without thee I dare not die.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come near and bless us when we wake,
Ere thro' the world our way we take,
Till in the ocean of thy love
We lose ourselves in heaven above.

title: Abide with me: fast falls the eventide
author: Henry Francis Lyte

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Abide with me: fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide!
When other helpers fail, and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, oh, abide with me!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word,
But as thou dwell'st with thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free,
Come, not to sojourn, but abide with me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I need thy presence every passing hour;
What but thy grace can foil the tempter's power?
Who like thyself my guide and stay can be?
Thro' cloud and sunshine, oh, abide with me!

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Savior, again to thy dear name we raise
author: John Ellerton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Savior, again to thy dear name we raise
With one accord our parting hymn of praise;
We rise to bless thee ere our worship cease,
And now, departing, wait thy word of peace.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

title: Softly now the light of day
author: G.W. Doane

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Softly now the light of day
Fades upon my sight away;
Free from care, from labor free,
Lord, I would commune with thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou whose all pervading eye
Naught escapes without, within,
Pardon each infirmity,
Open fault, and secret sin.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Soon, for me, the light of day
Shall forever pass away;
Then, from sin and sorrow free,
Take me, Lord, to dwell with thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou who, sinless, yet hast known
All of man's infirmity;
Then from thine eternal throne,
Jesus, look with pitying eye.

title: Silently the shades of evening
author: C.C. Cox

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Silently the shades of evening
Gather round my lowly door;
Silently they bring before me
Faces I shall see no more.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O the lost, the unforgotten,
Tho' the world be oft forgot!
O the shrouded and the lonely!
In our hearts they perish not.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Living in the silent hours,
Where our spirits only blend—
They, unlinked with earthly trouble;
We, still hoping for its end.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
How such holy memories cluster,
Like the stars when storms are past;
Pointing up to that far heaven
We may hope to gain at last.

title: Fading, still fading, the last beam is shining
author: Selina Huntingdon

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
sections.text:
Father, have mercy,
Father, have mercy,
Father, have mercy, thro' Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: God be with you till we meet again
author: J.E. Rankin D.D

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God be with you till we meet again,
By his counsels guide, uphold you,
With his sheep securely fold you,
God be with you till we meet again

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Till we meet, till we meet,
Till we meet at Jesus' feet;
Till we meet, till we meet,
God be with you till we meet again.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
God be with you till we meet again,
'Neath his wings securely hide you,
Daily manna still provide you,
God be with you till we meet again.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
God be with you till we meet again,
When life's perils thick confound you,
Put his arms unfailing round you,
God be with you till we meet again.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
God be with you till we meet again,
Keep love's banner floating o'er you,
Smite death's threat'ning wave before you,
God be with you till we meet again.

title: Sing them over again to me
author: P.P. Bliss

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sing them over again to me,
Wonderful words of life,
Let me more of their beauty see,
Wonderful words of life,
Words of life and beauty,
Teach me faith and duty.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Beautiful words, wonderful words,
Wonderful words of life,
Beautiful words, wonderful words,
Wonderful words of life.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

title: Give me the Bible, star of gladness gleaming
author: Priscilla J. Owens

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Give me the Bible, star of gladness gleaming,
To cheer the wand'rer lone and tempest-tossed;
No storm can hide that radiance peaceful beaming,
Since Jesus came to seek and save the lost.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Give me the Bible! holy message shining,
Thy light shall guide me in the narrow way.
Precept and promise, law and love combining,
Till night shall vanish in eternal day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Give me the Bible, when my heart is broken,
When sin and grief have filled my soul with fear;
Give me the precious words by Jesus spoken,
Hold up faith's lamp to show my Savior near.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Give me the Bible, all my steps enlighten,
Teach me the danger of these realms below;
That lamp of safety, o'er the gloom shall brighten,
That light alone the path of peace can show.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Give me the Bible, lamp of life immortal,
Hold up that splendor by the open grave;
Show me the light from heaven's shining portal,
Show me the glory gilding Jordan's wave.

title: Behold! the morning sun
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold! the morning sun
Begins his glorious way;
His beams thro' all the nations run,
And life and light convey.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But, where the gospel comes,
It spreads diviner light;
It calls dead sinners from the tombs
And gives the blind their sight.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How perfect is thy word!
And all thy judgments just;
Forever sure thy promise, Lord!
And men securely trust.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My gracious God! how plain
Are thy directions given!
Oh! may I never read in vain,
But find the path to heaven.

title: Holy Bible, book divine
author: John Burton

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Mine to comfort in distress,
Suffering in this wilderness;
Mine to show, by living faith,
Man can triumph over death.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Mine to tell of joys to come,
And the rebel sinner's doom;
O thou holy book divine,
Precious treasure, thou art mine.

title: Lord! I have made thy word my choice
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord! I have made thy word my choice,
My lasting heritage;
There shall my noblest powers rejoice,
My warmest thoughts engage.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I'll read the histories of thy love,
And keep thy laws in sight,
While through the promises I rove,
With ever fresh delight.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis a broad land of wealth unknown
Where springs of life arise;
Seeds of immortal bliss are sown,
And hidden, glory lies.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The best relief that mourners have—
It makes our sorrows blest;
Our fairest hope, beyond the grave,
And our eternal rest.

title: Lord! send thy word, and let it fly
author: Thomas Gibbons

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord! send thy word, and let it fly,
Armed with thy Spirit's power;
Ten thousands shall confess its sway,
And bless the saving hour.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Beneath the influence of its grace,
The barren wastes shall rise,
With sudden flowers and fruits arrayed,—
A blooming paradise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Peace, with her olives crowned, shall stretch
Her wings from shore to shore;
No trump shall rouse the rage of war,
Nor murderous cannon roar.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord! for these days we wait;—these days
Are in thy word foretold;
Fly swifter, sun and stars! and bring
This promised age of gold.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Amen!—with joy divine, let earth's
Unnumbered myriads cry;
Amen!—with joy divine, let heaven's
Unnumbered choirs reply.

title: Father of mercies, in thy word
author: Anne Steele

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father of mercies, in thy word
What endless glory shines!
Forever be thy name adored
For these celestial lines.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here may the wretched sons of want
Exhaustless riches find—
Riches above what earth can grant,
And lasting as the mind.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here the fair tree of knowledge grows,
And yields a free repast;
Sublimer sweets than nature knows
Invite the longing taste.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here the Redeemer's welcome voice
Spreads heavenly peace around;
And life and everlasting joys
Attend the blissful sound.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Oh, may these heavenly pages be
My ever dear delight;
And still new beauties may I see
And still increasing light.

title: How precious is the book divine
author: John Fawcett

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How precious is the book divine,
By inspiration given!
Bright as a lamp its doctrines shine,
To guide our souls to heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Its light, descending from above,
Our gloomy world to cheer,
Displays a Savior's boundless love,
And brings his glories near.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
It sweetly cheers our drooping hearts,
In this dark vale of tears;
Life, light, and joy it still imparts,
And quells our rising fears.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
This lamp, through all the tedious night
Of life, shall guide our way,
Till we behold the clearer light
Of an eternal day.

title: How shall the young secure their hearts
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How shall the young secure their hearts,
And guard their lives from sin?
Thy word the choicest rules imparts
To keep the conscience clean.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis like the sun, a heavenly light,
That guides us all the day;
And, through the dangers of the night,
A lamp to lead our way.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy word is everlasting truth;
How pure is every page!
That holy book shall guide our youth,
And well support our age.

title: Thy law is perfect, Lord of light
author: C. Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Let these, O God, my soul convert,
And make thy servant wise;
Let those be gladness to my ears—
The dayspring to mine eyes.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
So may the words my lips express—
The thoughts that throng my mind—
O Lord, my strength and righteousness,
With thee acceptance find.

title: Begin, my tongue, some heavenly theme
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Begin, my tongue, some heavenly theme,
And speak some boundless thing;
The mighty works or mightier name
Of our eternal King.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Tell of his wondrous faithfulness,
And sound his power abroad;
Sing the sweet promise of his grace,
And the performing God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His very word of grace is strong,
As that which built the skies;
The voice that rolls the stars along,
Speaks all the promises.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, might I hear thy heavenly tongue
But whisper, "Thou art mine!"
Those gentle words should raise my song
To notes almost divine.

title: The Lord, our God, is full of might
author: H. Kirke White

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Lord, our God, is full of might,
The winds obey his will;
He speaks,—and, in his heavenly height,
The rolling sun stands still.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Rebel, ye waves, and o'er the land
With threatening aspect roar;
The Lord uplifts his awful hand,
And chains you to the shore.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Howl, winds of night, your force combine;
Without his high behest,
Ye shall not, in the mountain pine,
Disturb the sparrow's nest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
His voice sublime is heard afar,
In distant peals it dies;
He yokes the whirlwind to his car,
And sweeps the howling skies.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Ye nations bend—in reverence bend;
Ye monarchs, wait his nod,
And bid the choral song ascend
To celebrate your God.

title: Great God! how infinite art thou
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great God! how infinite art thou!
What worthless worms are we!
Let the whole race of creatures bow,
And pay their praise to thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy throne eternal ages stood,
Ere seas or stars were made:
Thou art the ever-living God,
Were all the nations dead.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Eternity, with all its years,
Stands present in thy view;
To thee there's nothing old appears—
Great God! there's nothing new.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Our lives through various scenes are drawn,
And vexed with trifling cares;
While thine eternal thought moves on
Thine undisturbed affairs.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Great God! how infinite art thou!
What worthless worms are we!
Let the whole race of creatures bow.
And pay their praise to thee.

title: Come, thou Almighty King
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, thou Almighty King!
Help us thy name to sing,
Help us to praise;
Father all glorious!
O'er all victorious,
Come and reign over us,
Ancient of days!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Come, thou incarnate Word!
Gird on thy mighty sword;
Our prayer attend:
Come, and thy people bless,
And give thy word success;
Spirit of holiness,
On us descend.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come, holy Comforter!
Thy sacred witness bear
In this glad hour:
Thou who almighty art,
Now rule in every heart,
And ne'er from us depart,
Spirit of power!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To the great One in Three,
The highest praises be,
Hence, evermore!
His sovereign majesty
May we in glory see,
And to eternity
Love and adore.

title: Blest be the Father and his love
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest be the Father and his love,
To whose celestial source we owe
Rivers of endless joy above,
And rills of comfort here below.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Glory to thee, great Son of God!
From whose dear, wounded body rolls
A precious stream of vital blood—
Pardon and life for dying souls

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We give the sacred Spirit praise,
Who, in our hearts of sin and woe,
Makes living springs of grace arise,
And into boundless glory flow.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thus, God, the Father, God, the Son,
And God, the Spirit, we adore;
That sea of life and love unknown,
Without a bottom or a shore.

title: Thy way, O God! is in the sea
author: John Fawcett

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thy way, O God! is in the sea,
Thy paths I cannot trace;
Nor comprehend the mystery
Of thine unbounded grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Here the dark veils of flesh and sense
My captive soul surround;
Mysterious deeps of providence
My wondering thoughts confound.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
As through a glass I dimly see
The wonders of thy love;
How little do I know of thee,
Or of the joys above!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
With rapture I shall soon survey
Thy providence and grace;
And spend an everlasting day
In wonder, love, and praise.

title: O God! our help in ages past
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O God! our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come;
Our shelter from the stormy blast,
And our eternal home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Under the shadow of thy throne,
Still may we dwell secure;
Sufficient is thine arm alone,
And our defense is sure.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Before the hills in order stood,
Or earth received her frame,
From everlasting thou art God,
To endless years the same.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A thousand ages in thy sight
Are like an evening gone;
Short as the watch that ends the night,
Before the rising sun.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The busy tribes of flesh and blood,
With all their cares and fears,
Are carried downward by the flood,
And lost in following years.

title: I sing th' almighty power of God
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I sing th' almighty power of God,
That made the mountains rise,
That spread the flowing seas abroad,
And built the lofty skies.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I sing the wisdom that ordained
The sun to rule the day;
The moon shines full at his command,
And all the stars obey.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I sing the goodness of the Lord,
That filled the earth with food;
He formed the creatures with his word,
And then pronounced them good.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord! how thy wonders are displayed
Where'er I turn mine eye!
If I survey the ground I tread,
Or gaze upon the sky.

title: My God how wonderful thou art
author: Frederick Wm. Faber

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God how wonderful thou art!
Thy majesty how bright!
How beautiful thy mercy seat,
In depths of burning light.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How dread are thine eternal years,
Oh, everlasting Lord!
By prostrate spirits day and night,
Incessantly adored.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, how I fear thee, living God!
With deepest, tenderest fears,
And worship thee with trembling hope,
And penitential tears.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Yet I may love thee, too, O Lord!
Almighty as thou art,
For thou hast stooped to ask of me
The love of this poor heart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
No earthly father loves like thee,
No mother, half so mild,
Bears and forbears as thou hast done
With me, thy sinful child.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Father of Jesus! love's reward!
What rapture will it be,
Prostrate before thy throne to lie,
And gaze and gaze on thee.

title: God moves in a mysterious way
author: William Cowper

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God moves in a mysterious way,
His wonders to perform;
He plants his footsteps in the sea,
And rides upon the storm.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Deep in unfathomable mines
Of never-failing skill,
He treasures up his bright designs,
And works his sovereign will.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ye fearful saints! fresh courage take;
The clouds ye so much dread,
Are big with mercy, and shall break
In blessings on your head.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Judge not the Lord by feeble sense,
But trust him for his grace;
Behind a frowning providence,
He hides a smiling face.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
His purposes will ripen fast,
Unfolding every hour;
The bud may have a bitter taste,
But sweet will be the flower.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Blind unbelief is sure to err,
And scan his work in vain;
God is his own interpreter,
And he will make it plain.

title: The Lord descended from above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Lord descended from above,
And bowed the heavens most high;
And underneath his feet he cast
The darkness of the sky.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On cherub and on cherubim
Full royally he rode;
And on the wings of mighty winds
Came flying all abroad.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He sat serene upon the floods,
Their fury to restrain;
And he, as sovereign Lord and King,
Forevermore shall reign.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text: Thomas Sternhold, d. 1549.

title: Yes, God is good; in earth and sky
author: John H. Gurney

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Yes, God is good; in earth and sky,
From ocean depths and spreading wood,
Ten thousand voices seem to cry,
"God made us all, and God is good."

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The sun that keeps his trackless way,
And downward pours his golden flood,
Night's sparkling hosts all seem to sky,
In accents clear, that God is good.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yes, God is good, all Nature says,
By God's own hand with speech endued;
And man, in louder notes of praise,
Should sing for joy that God is good.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Ere mountains reared their forms sublime
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ere mountains reared their forms sublime,
Or heaven and earth in order stood,
Before the birth of ancient time,
From everlasting thou art God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A thousand ages in their flight
With thee are as a fleeting day;
Past, present, future, to thy sight
At once their various scenes display.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But our brief life's a shadowy dream—
A passing thought, that soon is o'er;
That fades with morning's earliest beam,
And fills the musing mind no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To us, O Lord, the wisdom give,
Each passing moment so to spend,
That we at length with thee may live
Where life and bliss shall never end.

title: There is a God—all nature speaks
author: Anne Steele

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a God—all nature speaks,
Through earth, and air, and sea, and skies;
See, from the clouds his glory breaks,
When earliest beams of morning rise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The rising sun, serenely bright,
Throughout the world's extended frame,
Inscribes in characters of light
His mighty Maker's glorious name.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ye curious minds, who roam abroad,
And trace creation's wonders o'er,
Confess the footsteps of your God—
Bow down before him and adore.

title: The Lord is King; child of the dust
author: Josiah Conder

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The Lord is King! lift up thy voice,
Oh, earth! and all ye heavens! rejoice;
From world to world the joy shall ring—
The Lord omnipotent is King.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Lord is King! who then shall dare
Resist his will, distrust his care,
Or murmur at his wise decrees,
Or doubt his royal promises?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, when his wisdom can mistake,
His might decay, his love forsake,
Then may his children cease to sing—
The Lord omnipotent is King.

title: God is love; his mercy brightens
author: Sir John Bowring

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
E'en the hour the darkest seemeth
Will his changeless goodness prove;
From the gloom his brightness streameth:
God is wisdom, God is love.
He with earthly cares entwineth
Hope and comfort from above;
Everywhere his glory shineth:
God is wisdom, God is love.

title: Lord! thy glory fills the heaven
author: Richard Mant

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Heaven is still with glory ringing,
Earth takes up the angels' cry—
"Holy, holy, holy!" singing,
"Lord of hosts! the Lord most high!"

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ever thus in God's high praises,
Brethren! let our tongues unite;
Chief the heart when duty raises
God-ward at his mystic rite.

title: Eternal Wisdom! thee we praise
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Eternal Wisdom! thee we praise,
Thee the creation sings;
With thy loved name, rocks, hills, and seas,
And heaven's high palace rings.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy hand, how wide it spread the sky!
How glorious to behold!
Tinged with a blue of heavenly dye,
And starred with sparkling gold.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Infinite strength and equal skill
Shine through the worlds abroad;
Our souls with vast amazement fill,
And speak the builder—God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But the sweet beauties of thy grace
Our softer passions move;
Pity divine, in Jesus' face,
We see, adore, and love.

title: Hail! holy, holy, holy, Lord
author: C. Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hail! holy, holy, holy, Lord,
Whom One in Three we know;
By all thy heavenly host adored,
By all thy Church below.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
One undivided Trinity
With triumph we proclaim;
The universe is full of thee,
And speaks thy glorious name.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Hail! holy, holy, holy Lord,
Our heavenly song shall be
Supreme, Essential One, adored
In co-eternal Thee!

title: Come, ye that know and fear the Lord
author: George Burder

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, ye that know and fear the Lord,
And lift your souls above;
Let every heart and voice accord,
To sing that—God is love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
This precious truth his word declares,
And all his mercies prove;
Jesus, the Gift of gifts, appears,
To show that—God is love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Behold his patience lengthened out
To those who from him rove,
And calls effectual reach their hearts,
To teach them—God is love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The work begun is carried on
By power from heaven above;
And every step from first to last,
Declares that—God is love.

title: Jehovah God! thy gracious power
author: John Thompson

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jehovah God! thy gracious power
On every hand we see;
Oh, may the blessings of each hour
Lead all our thoughts to thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy power is in the ocean deeps,
And reaches to the skies;
Thine eye of mercy never sleeps,
Thy goodness never dies.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In all the varying scenes of time,
On thee our hopes depend;
In every age, in every clime,
Our Father and our Friend.

title: Come, let us all unite to sing
author: Anon

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, let us all unite to sing,
God is love;
Let heav'n and earth their praises bring,
God is love;
Let every soul from sin awake,
Each in his heart sweet music make,
And sing with us for Jesus' sake,
For God is love.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
God is love,
God is love.
Come, let us all unite to sing
That God is love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, tell us to earth's remotest bound,
God is love;
In Christ we have redemption found,
God is love;
His blood has washed our sins away,
His Spirit turned our night to day,
And now we can rejoice to say
That God is love.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: It came upon the midnight clear
author: E.H. Sears

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
It came upon the midnight clear,
That glorious song of old,
From angels bending near the earth,
To touch their harps of gold;
"Peace to the earth, good-will to men,
From heaven's all gracious King:"
The earth in solemn stillness lay,
To hear the angels sing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Still through the cloven skies they come,
With peaceful wings unfurled;
And still celestial music floats
O'er all the weary world;
Above its sad and lowly plains
They bend on heavenly wing,
And ever o'er its Babel sounds,
The blessed angels sing.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O ye, beneath life's crushing load,
Whose forms are bending low,
Who toil along the climbing way,
With painful steps and slow;—
Look up! for glad and golden hours
Come swiftly on the wing;
Oh, rest beside the weary road,
And hear the angels sing!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
For lo! the days are hastening on,
By prophet-bards foretold,
When with the ever-circling years
Comes round the age of gold!
When peace shall over all the earth
Its final splendors fling,
And the whole world send back the song
Which now the angels sing!

title: The race that long in darkness pine
author: John Morrison

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The race that long in darkness pine
Have seen a glorious light;
The people dwell in day who dwelt
In death's surrounding night.
To hail thy rise, thou better Sun,
The gathering nations come,
With joy, as when the reapers bear
The harvest treasures home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To us a child of hope is born;
To us a Son is given;
And him shall all the earth obey,
And all the hosts of heaven.
His name shall be the Prince of Peace,
Forevermore adored,
The Wonderful, the Counselor,
The great and mighty Lord.

title: While shepherds watched their flocks by night
author: Nahum Tate

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
While shepherds watched their flocks by night,
All seated on the ground,
The angel of the Lord came down,
And glory shone around.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Fear not," said he,—for mighty dread
Had seized their troubled mind,—
"Glad tidings of great joy I bring
To you and all mankind.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
"To you, in David's town, this day,
Is born of David's line,
The Savior, who is Christ, the Lord;
And this shall be the sign:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"The heavenly babe you there shall find
To human view displayed,
All meanly wrapped in swathing bands,
And in a manger laid."

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thus spake the seraph; and forthwith
Appeared a shining throng
Of angels, praising God, and thus
Addressed their joyful song:

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
"All glory be to God on high,
And to the earth be peace:
Good-will henceforth from heaven to men
Begin and never cease!"

title: Calm on the listening ear of night
author: Edmund H. Sears

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Calm on the listening ear of night
Come heaven's melodious strains,
Where wild Judea stretches far
Her silver-mantled plains.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Celestial choirs, from courts above,
Shed sacred glories there,
And angels, with their sparkling lyres,
Make music on the air.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The answering hills of Palestine
Send back the glad reply,
And greet, from all their holy heights,
The day-spring from on high.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"Glory to God!" the sounding skies
Loud with their anthems ring—
"Peace to the earth, good-will to men,
From heaven's eternal King."

title: Joy to the world! the Lord is come
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Joy to the world! the Lord is come:
Let earth receive her King;
Let every heart prepare him room,
And heaven and nature sing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Joy to the earth! the Savior reigns:
Let men their songs employ;
While fields and floods, rocks, hills, and plains,
Repeat the sounding joy.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
No more let sins and sorrows grow,
Nor thorns infest the ground;
He comes to make his blessings flow,
Far as the curse is found.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He rules the world with truth and grace,
And makes the nations prove
The glories of his righteousness,
And wonders of his love.

title: Hark the glad sound! the Savior comes
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark the glad sound! the Savior comes—
The Savior promised long;
Let every heart prepare a throne,
And every voice a song.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He comes, the prisoners to release,
In Satan's bondage held;
The gates of brass before him burst,
The iron fetters yield.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He comes, the broken heart to bind,
The bleeding soul to cure;
And, with the treasures of his grace,
T' enrich the humble poor.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Our glad hosannas, Prince of Peace,
Thy welcome shall proclaim;
And heaven's eternal arches ring
With thy beloved name.

title: Jesus is God! the glorious bands
author: Frederick Wm. Faber

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus is God! the glorious bands
Of holy angels sing
Songs of adoring praise to him,
Their Maker and their King.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He was true God in Bethlehem's crib,
On Calvary's cross, true God;
He who, in heaven, eternal reigned,
In time, on earth abode.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus is God! there never was
A time when he was not;
Boundless, eternal, merciful,
The Word the Sire begot.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Backward our thoughts through ages stretch,
Onward through endless bliss;
For there are two eternities,
And both alike are his.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus is God! oh, could I now,
But compass land and sea,
To teach and tell this single truth,
How happy should I be!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Oh, had I but an angel's voice,
I would proclaim so loud,
Jesus, the Good, the Beautiful,
Is everlasting God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hark! the herald angels sing,
"Glory to the new-born King!
Peace on earth, and mercy mild,
God and sinners reconciled."
Joyful all ye nations, rise;
Join the triumph of the skies!
With the angelic host proclaim,
Christ is born in Bethlehem.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
See, he lays his glory by,
Born that man no more may die;
Born to raise the sons of earth,
Born to give them second birth.
Veiled in flesh the Godhead see;
Hail the incarnate Deity.
Pleased as man with men to dwell,
Jesus, our Immanuel.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hail the heaven-born Prince of Peace!
Hail the Sun of Righteousness;
Light and life to all he brings,
Risen with healing in his wings.
Let us, then, with angels sing,
"Glory to the new-born King!
Peace on earth, and mercy mild,
God and sinners reconciled."

title: Angels rejoiced and sweetly sung
author: M. E. Servoss

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Angels rejoiced and sweetly sung
At our Redeemer's birth;
Mortals! awake: let every tongue
Proclaim his matchless worth.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Glory to God, who dwells on high,
And sent his only Son
To take a servant's form, and die,
For evils we had done!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Good-will to men; ye fallen race!
Arise, and shout for joy;
He comes, with rich abounding grace
To save and not destroy.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord! send the gracious tidings forth,
And fill the world with light,
That Jew and Gentile, through the earth,
May know thy saving might.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: William Hurn, 1813.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text: 1O3 Salvation Morning, 7s & 6s.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
What means this glorious radiance
Across Judea's plain?
Those white-winged angels singing
In such exultant strain?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
The King of glory cometh,
Earth's broken hearts to bind,
And God's salvation morning
Hath dawned for all mankind.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
What means this wondrous story
The holy angels tell?
Of one who reigned in heaven,
And now on earth would dwell?

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Why bend these Eastern sages
To one of lowly birth?
What means this heav'nly message
Of love and peace on earth?

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
Ye wand'rers in earth's darkness,
On ocean deep and land,
Hail! hail! the joyful tidings,
The morning is at hand.

title: What grace, O Lord! and beauty shone
author: Edward Denny

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What grace, O Lord! and beauty shone
Around thy steps below!
What patient love was seen in all
Thy life and death of woe!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy foes might hate, despise, revile,
Thy friends unfaithful prove;
Unwearied in forgiveness still,
Thy heart could only love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, give us hearts to love like thee;
Like thee, O Lord! to grieve
Far more for others' sins, than all
The wrongs that we receive.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
One with thyself, may every eye,
In us, thy brethren, see
That gentleness and grace that springs
From union, Lord, with thee.

title: We may not climb the heavenly steeps
author: J. G. Whittier

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We may not climb the heavenly steeps
To bring the Lord Christ down;
In vain we search the lowest deeps,
For him no depths can drown.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But warm, sweet, tender, even yet
A present help is he;
And faith has yet its Olivet,
And love its Galilee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The healing of the seamless dress
Is by our beds of pain;
We touch him in life's throng and press,
And we are whole again.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Through him the first fond prayers are said
Our lips of childhood frame;
The last low whispers of our dead
Are burdened with his name.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O Lord and Master of us all,
Whate'er our name or sign,
We own thy sway, we hear thy call,
We test our lives by thine!

title: In stature grows the heavenly Child
author: Anon

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In stature grows the heavenly Child,
With death before his eyes;
A Lamb unblemished, meek and mild,
Prepared for sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The Son of God his glory hides
With parents mean and poor;
And he who made the heavens abides
In dwelling-place obscure.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Those mighty hands that stay the sky
No earthly toil refuse;
And he who set the stars on high
A humble trade pursues.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He before whom the angels stand.
At whose behest they fly,
Now yields himself to man's command,
And lays his glory by.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The Father's name we loudly raise,
The Son we all adore,
The Holy Ghost, One God, we praise,
Both now and evermore.

title: A pilgrim through this lonely world
author: H. Bonar

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A pilgrim through this lonely world,
The blessed Savior passed;
A mourner all his life was he,
A dying Lamb at last

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That tender heart which felt for all,
For us its life-blood gave;
It found on earth no resting-place.
Save only in the grave.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Such was our Lord; and shall we fear
The cross with all its scorn?
Or love a faithless, evil world
That wreathed his brow with thorn?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
No, facing all its frowns or smiles,
Like him obedient still,
We homeward press, through storm or calm,
To Zion's blessed hill.

title: How beauteous were the marks divine
author: Arthur Cleveland Coxe

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How beauteous were the marks divine,
That in thy meekness used to shine;
That lit thy lonely pathway, trod
In wondrous love, O Son of God!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, who, like thee, so calm, so bright,
Thou God of God, thou Light of Light!
Oh, who, like thee, did ever go
So patient through a world of woe?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, who, like thee, so humbly bore
The scorn, the scoffs of men before?
So meek, forgiving, godlike, high,
So glorious in humility?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
E'en death, which sets the prisoner free,
Was pang, and scoff, and scorn to thee;
Yet love, through all thy torture glowed,
And mercy with thy life-blood flowed.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Oh, in thy light, be mine to go,
Illuming all my way of woe!
And give me ever on the road
To trace thy footsteps, Son of God!

title: How sweetly flowed the gospel's sound
author: John Bowring

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How sweetly flowed the gospel's sound
From lips of gentleness and grace,
When listening thousands gathered round,
And joy and reverence filled the place!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
"Come, wanderers, to my Father's home;
Come, all ye weary ones, and rest;"
Yes, sacred Teacher, we will come,
Obey thee, love thee, and be blest.

title: My dear Redeemer and my Lord
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My dear Redeemer and my Lord,
I read my duty in thy Word;
But in thy life the law appears,
Drawn out in living characters.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Such was thy truth, and such thy zeal,
Such deference to thy Father's will,
Such love and meekness so divine,
I would transcribe and make them mine.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Be thou my pattern, make me bear
More of thy gracious image here;
Then God, the Judge, shall own my name
Among the followers of the Lamb.

title: Behold! the blind their sight receive
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Thus doth th' eternal Spirit own
And seal the mission of the Son;
The Father vindicates his cause,
While he hangs bleeding on the cross.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He dies! the heavens in mourning stood;
He rises, the triumphant God!
Behold the Lord ascending high,
No more to bleed, no more to die.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hence, and forever, from my heart,
I bid my doubts and fears depart;
And to those hands my soul resign,
Which bear credentials so divine.

title: Ride on! ride on in majesty
author: Latin

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ride on! ride on in majesty!
Hark! all the tribes Hosanna cry;
O Savior meek, pursue thy road
With palms and scattered garments strowed.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Bide on! ride on in majesty!
In lowly pomp ride on to die;
O Christ, thy triumphs now begin
O'er captive death and conquered sin.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ride on! ride on in majesty!
The angel armies of the sky
Look down with sad and wondering eyes
To see the approaching sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ride on! ride on in majesty!
The last and fiercest strife is nigh;
The Father on his sapphire throne
Awaits his own anointed Son.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Ride on! ride on in majesty!
In lowly pomp, ride on to die;
Bow thy meek head to mortal pain,
Then take, O God, thy power and reign.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text: Henry Hart Milman, 1827.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text: 113 Overberg. L.M.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text: The Transfiguration. (245)

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Oh, wondrous type, oh, vision fair,
Of glory that the church shall share,
Which Christ upon the mountain shows,
Where brighter than the sun he glows!

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
From age to age the tale declare,
How with the three disciples there,
Where Moses and Elias meet,
The Lord holds converse high and sweet.

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
The law and prophets there have place,
Two chosen witnesses of grace;
The Father's voice from out the cloud
Proclaimed his only Son aloud.

sections.label: Verse 12
sections.text:
With shining face and bright array
Christ deigns to manifest to-day,
What glory shall be theirs above
Who joy in God with perfect love.

title: Ever would I fain be reading

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ever would I fain be reading,
In the ancient holy Book,
Of my Savior's gentle pleading,
Truth in ev'ry word and look.
How to all the sick and tearful
Help was ever gladly shown;
How he sought the poor and fearful,
Called them brothers and his own.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How no contrite soul e'er sought him,
And was bidden to depart;
How, with gentle words he taught him,
Took the death from out his heart.
Still I read the ancient story,—
And my joy is ever new,—
How for us he left his glory,
How he still is kind and true.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How the flock he gently leadeth,
Whom his Father gave him here;
How his arms he widely spreadeth,
To his heart to draw us near.
Let me kneel, my Lord! before thee,
Let my heart in tears o'erflow,
Melted by thy love adore thee,
Blessed in thee, mid joy or woe.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ger., Louisa Hensel, 1829.
Tr., Catherine Winkworth, 1858

title: Behold where, in the Friend of man
author: William Endfield

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold where, in the Friend of man,
Appears each grace divine!
The virtues all in Jesus meet,
With mildest radiance shine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To spread the rays of heavenly light,
To give the mourner joy,
To preach glad tidings to the poor,
Was his divine employ.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In the last hour of deep distress,
Before his Father's throne,
With soul resigned, he bowed, and said,
"Thy will, not mine, be done!"

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Be Christ our pattern and our guide,
His image may we bear;
Oh, may we tread his sacred steps,
And his bright glories share.

title: In vain in high and holy lays
author: E.S. Lorenz

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In vain in high and holy lays
My soul her grateful voice would raise;
For who can sing the worthy praise
Of the wonderful love of Jesus?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Wonderful love! wonderful love!
Wonderful love of Jesus!
Wonderful love! wonderful love!
Wonderful love of Jesus!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A joy by day, a peace by night,
In storms a calm, in darkness light;
In pain a balm, in weakness might,
Is the wonderful love of Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My hope for pardon when I call,
My trust for lifting when I fall;
In life, in death, my all in all,
Is the wonderful love of Jesus.

title: 'Tis midnight; and on Olive's brow
author: W.B. Tappan

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
'Tis midnight; and on Olive's brow
The star is dimmed that lately shone;
'Tis midnight; in the garden, now,
The suffering Savior prays alone.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis midnight; and, from all removed,
The Savior wrestles lone with fears;
