E'en that disciple whom he loved
Heeds not his Master's grief and tears.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis midnight; and for others' guilt
The man of sorrows weeps in blood;
Yet he that hath in anguish knelt
Is not forsaken by his God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
'Tis midnight; and from ether plains
Is borne the song that angels know;
Unheard by mortals are the strains
That sweetly soothe the Savior's woe.

title: From Calvary a cry was heard
author: John W. Cunningham

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From Calvary a cry was heard—
A bitter and heart-rending cry;
My Savior! ev'ry mournful word
Bespoke thy soul's deep agony

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A horror of great darkness fell
On thee, thou spotless holy One!
And all the eager hosts of hell
Conspired to tempt God's only Son.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The scourge, the thorns, the deep disgrace,
These thou could'st bear, nor once repine;
But when Jehovah veiled his face,
Unutterable pangs were thine.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: When I survey the wondrous cross
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When I survey the wondrous cross,
On which the Prince of Glory died,
My richest gain I count but loss,
And pour contempt on all my pride.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Forbid it, Lord, that I should boast,
Save in the death of Christ, my God;
All the vain things that charm me most,
I sacrifice them to his blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
See, from his head, his hands, his feet
Sorrow and love flow mingled down;
Did e'er such love and sorrow meet,
Or thorns compose so rich a crown?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Were all the realms of nature mine,
That were a present far too small;
Love so amazing, so divine.
Demands my soul, my life, my all.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O sacred head, now wounded!
With grief and shame weighed down,
Now scornfully surrounded
With thorns, thine only crown;
O sacred head, what glory,
What bliss, till now, was thine!
Yet tho' despised and gory,
I joy to call thee mine.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
The joy can ne'er be spoken,
Above all joys beside,
When in thy body broken,
I thus with safety hide;
My Lord of life! desiring
Thy glory now to see,
Beside thy cross expiring,
I'd breathe my soul to thee.

title: Alas! and did my Savior bleed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Alas! and did my Savior bleed?
And did my Sovereign die?
Would he devote that sacred head
For such a worm as I?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Was it for crimes that I have done
He groaned upon the tree?
Amazing pity! grace unknown!
And love beyond degree!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Well might the sun in darkness hide,
And shut his glories in,
When Christ, the mighty Maker, died
For man, the creature's sin!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thus might I hide my blushing face
While his dear cross appears;
Dissolve my heart in thankfulness,
And melt mine eyes to tears.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text: Isaac Watts, 1709.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Jesus died for you,
And Jesus died for me,
Yes, Jesus died for all mankind;
Bless God, salvation's free.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Help me, dear Savior, thee to own,
And ever faithful be;
And when thou sittest on thy throne.
O Lord, remember me.

title: Great God, when I approach thy throne

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great God, when I approach thy throne
And all thy glory see;
This is my stay, and this alone,
That Jesus died for me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How can a soul condemned to die,
Escape the just decree?
Helpless and full of sin am I,
But Jesus died for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Burdened with sin's oppressive chain,
Oh, how can I get free?
No peace can all my efforts gain,
But Jesus died for me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And, Lord, when I behold thy face,
This must be all my plea;
Save me by thy almighty grace,
For Jesus died for me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: W.B. Bathurst, d. 1877.

title: O Jesus! sweet the tears I shed
author: Ray Palmer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Jesus! sweet the tears I shed,
While at thy cross I kneel,
Gaze on thy wounded, fainting head,
And all thy sorrows feel.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My heart dissolves to see thee bleed,
This heart so hard before;
I hear thee for the guilty plead,
And grief o'erflows the more.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Twas for the sinful thou didst die,
And I a sinner stand;
What love speaks from thy dying eye,
And from each pierced hand!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I know this cleansing blood of thine
Was shed, dear Lord, for me;
For me, for all—oh, grace divine!—
Who look by faith on thee.

title: Oppressed with noon-day's scorching heat
author: H. Bonar

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oppressed with noon-day's scorching heat,
To yonder cross I flee;
Beneath its shelter take my seat:
No shade like this for me!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Beneath that cross clear waters burst,
A fountain sparkling free;
And there I quench my desert thirst:
No spring like this for me!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A stranger here, I pitch my tent
Beneath this spreading tree;
Here shall my pilgrim life be spent:
No home like this for me!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
For burdened ones a resting-place
Beside that cross I see;
Here I cast off my weariness:
No rest like this for me!

title: The cross, the cross, the blood-stained cross
author: J.H. Stockton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The cross, the cross, the blood-stained cross!
The hallowed cross I see;
Reminding me of precious blood
That once was shed for me.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Oh, the blood, the precious blood,
That Jesus shed for me;
Upon the cross, in crimson flood,
Just now by faith I see.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The cross, the cross, that heavy cross,
My Savior bore for me;
It bowed him to the earth with grief
On sad Mount Calvary

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The wounds, the wounds, those painful wounds;
Oh, they were made for me!
His hands and feet, his holy head,
All pierced and torn I see.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The death, the death, the awful death!
That Jesus died for me;
I heard his groans, his prayer, "Forgive,"
His bleeding side I see.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The love, the love, the matchless love,
That bled upon the tree!
It melts my heart, it wins my love,
It brings me, Lord, to thee.

title: Our sins on Christ were laid
author: J. Fawcett

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, we look to thee;—
Where else can sinners go?
Thy boundless love shall set us free
From wretchedness and woe.

title: Are there no wounds for me
author: Mrs. Grace Webster Hinsdale

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Are there no wounds for me?
Hast thou received them all?
How can I, Lord, the anguish see,
Beneath which thou didst fall?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
But yet, I weeping see
The thorns which pierced thy head;
Thou faint'st beneath thy cross for me,
For me to death thou'rt led!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Meekly, with love divine,
Thy holy head is bent,
And streams of blood, for sins of mine,
Flow where thy side is rent.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Beneath this sacred flood
I bow my sinful soul;
Dear Savior, let thy precious blood
Wash me and make me whole.

title: Did Christ o'er sinners weep
author: Benjamin Beddome

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Did Christ o'er sinners weep,
And shall our cheeks be dry?
Let floods of penitential grief
Burst forth from every eye.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The Son of God in tears—
The wondering angels see!
Be thou astonished, O my soul!
He shed those tears for thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He wept—that we might weep—
Each sin demands a tear;
In heaven alone no sin is found,
And there's no weeping there.

title: Rock of ages, cleft for me
author: Let me hide myself in thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rock of ages, cleft for me!
Let me hide myself in thee:
Let the water and the blood,
From thy side a healing flood,
Be of sin the double cure;
Save from wrath and make me pure.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
While I draw this fleeting breath,
When mine eyelids close in death,
When I rise to worlds unknown,
See thee on thy judgment throne—
Rock of Ages cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text: Augustus M. Toplady, 1776.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in thee,

title: By thy birth, and by thy tears
author: Sir Robert Grant

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: In the cross of Christ I glory
author: Sir John Bowring

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In the cross of Christ I glory,
Towering o'er the wrecks of time;
All the light of sacred story
Gathers round its head sublime.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When the woes of life o'ertake me,
Hopes deceive, and fears annoy,
Never shall the cross forsake me;
Lo! it glows with peace and joy.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When the sun of bliss is beaming
Light and love upon my way,
From the cross the radiance streaming
Adds more luster to the day.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Bane and blessing, pain and pleasure
By the cross are sanctified;
Peace is there, that knows no measure,
Joys that through all time abide.

title: Sweet the moments, rich in blessing
author: Altered by Walter Shirley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet the moments, rich in blessing,
Which before the cross I spend,
Life, and health, and peace possessing,
From the sinner's dying Friend!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here I'll sit, forever viewing
Mercy's streams in streams of blood:
Precious drops, my soul bedewing,
Plead, and claim my peace, with God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Truly blessed is this station,
Low before the cross to lie,
While I see divine compassion
Floating in his languid eye.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here it is I find my heaven,
While upon the Lamb I gaze;
Love I much?—I've much forgiven,—
I'm a miracle of grace.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Love and grief my heart dividing,
With my tears his feet I'll bathe;
Constant still in faith abiding,—
Life deriving from his death.

title: When I view my Savior bleeding
author: R. Lee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When I view my Savior bleeding,
For my sins upon the tree;
Oh, how wondrous!—how exceeding
Great his love appears to me!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Floods of deep distress and anguish.
To impede his labors, came;
Yet they all could not extinguish
Love's eternal, burning flame.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Now redemption is completed,
Full salvation is procured;
Death and Satan are defeated,
By the sufferings he endured.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now the gracious Mediator,
Risen to the courts of bliss,
Claims for me, a sinful creature,
Pardon, righteousness, and peace!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Sure, such infinite affection
Lays the highest claims to mine;
All my powers, without exception,
Should in fervent praises join.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: I gave my life for thee
author: Frances R. Havergal

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I gave my life for thee,
My precious blood I shed,
That thou mightst ransomed be,
And quickened from the dead;
I gave, I gave my life for thee,
What hast thou given for me?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My Father's house of light,
My glory-circled throne,
I left for earthly night,
For wand'rings sad and lone;
I left, I left it all for thee,
Hast thou left aught for me?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I suffered much for thee,
More than thy tongue can tell,
Of bitterest agony,
To rescue thee from hell;
I've borne, I've borne it all for thee,
What hast thou borne for me?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And I have brought to thee,
Down from my home above,
Salvation full and free,
My pardon and my love;
I bring, I bring rich gifts to thee,
What hast thou brought to me?

title: Come to the cross, where the Savior died
author: Rev. J.H. Martin

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come to the cross, where the Savior died,
Look to the Lamb that was crucified;
Turn to the mournful and tragic scene,
Gaze on the suffering Nazarene.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Look at the Crucified, look and live!
Look, for eternal life he will give.
Come to the cross, where the Savior died,
Look to the Lamb that was crucified.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Fall at the feet of the dying One,
Trust in the name of the Father's Son;
Wash in the fountain of Jesus' blood,
Seek for thy cure in the healing flood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Fly to the arms of his pard'ning love,
Cherish the hope of a crown above;
Taste of the sweetness of sins forgiven,
Lean on the promise of rest in heaven.

title: Jesus, keep me near the cross
author: Fanny J. Crosby

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, keep me near the cross
There a precious fountain
Free to all—a healing stream,
Flows from Calvary's mountain.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
In the cross, in the cross,
Be my glory ever,
Till my raptured soul shall find
Rest beyond the river.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Near the cross, a trembling soul,
Love and mercy found me;
There the bright and morning star
Shed its beams around me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Near the cross, O Lamb of God,
Bring its scenes before me;
Help me walk from day to day,
With its shadows o'er me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Near the cross I'll watch and wait,
Hoping, trusting ever,
Till I reach the golden strand,
Just beyond the river.

title: Saw ye my Savior, saw ye my Savior

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Saw ye my Savior, saw ye my Savior,
Saw ye my Savior and God?
Oh! he died on Calvary,
To atone for you and me,
And to purchase our pardon with blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Hail, mighty Savior! hail, mighty Savior!
Prince, and the Author of peace!
Oh! he burst the bars of death,
And, triumphant from the earth,
He ascended to mansions of bliss.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
"I will forgive them, I will forgive them
When they repent and believe;
Let them now return to thee,
And be reconciled to me,
And salvation they all shall receive."

title: Deep in our hearts let us record
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Deep in our hearts let us record
The deeper sorrows of our Lord;
Behold the rising billows roll,
To overwhelm his holy soul.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Yet, gracious God, thy power and love
Have made the curse a blessing prove;
Those dreadful sufferings of thy Son
Atoned for sins that we have done.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The pangs of our expiring Lord
The honors of thy law restored;
His sorrows made thy justice known.
And paid for follies not his own.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, for his sake our guilt forgive,
And let the mourning sinner live;
The Lord will hear us in his name,
Nor shall our hope be turned to shame.

title: Beneath thy cross I lay me down
author: Wm. Williams

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Here, Jesus, will I ever stay,
And spend my longing hours away;
Think on thy bleeding wounds and pain,
And contemplate thy woes again.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, unmolested, happy rest!
Where inward fears are all suppressed;
Here I shall love, and live secure,
And patiently my cross endure.

title: O love! who gav'st thy life for me
author: From the German. Author unknown

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O love! who gav'st thy life for me,
And won an everlasting good
Through thy sore anguish on the tree,
I ever think upon thy blood!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O Love! who unto death hast grieved
For this cold heart, unworthy thine,
Whom the cold grave and death received,
I thank thee for that grief divine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I give thee thanks that thou didst die
To win eternal life for me,
To bring salvation from on high:
Oh, draw me up through love to thee!

title: The morning purples all the sky
author: Dr. A. R. Thompson

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The morning purples all the sky,
The air with praises rings;
Defeated hell stands sullen by,
The world exulting sings.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
While he, the King all strong to save,
Rends the dark doors away,
And through the breaches of the grave
Strides forth into the day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Death's captive, in his gloomy prison
Past fettered he has lain;
But he has mastered death, is risen,
And death wears now the chain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The shining angels cry, "Away
With grief; no spices bring;
Not tears, but songs, this joyful day,
Should greet the rising King!"

title: Hosanna to the Prince of Light
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hosanna to the Prince of Light,
Who clothed himself in clay,
Entered the iron gates of death,
And tore the bars away.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Death is no more the king of dread,
Since our Immanuel rose;
He took the tyrant's sting away,
And spoiled our hellish foes.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
See how the conqueror mounts aloft
And to his Father flies,
With scars of honor in his flesh,
And triumph in his eyes.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There our exalted Savior reigns,
And scatters blessings down;
Our Jesus fills the middle seat
Of the celestial throne.

title: Christ, the Lord, is risen to-day
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Christ, the Lord, is risen to-day,
Sons of men and angels say:
Raise your joys and triumphs high;
Sing, ye heavens; thou earth, reply.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Vain the stone, the watch, the seal—
Christ hath burst the gates of hell;
Death in vain forbids his rise—
Christ hath opened paradise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lives again our glorious King:
Where, O death, is now thy sting?
Once he died our souls to save:
Where's thy victory, boasting grave?

title: Angel! roll the rock away
author: Thomas Scott

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis the Savior; angels! raise
Fame's eternal trump of praise:
Let the world's remotest bound
Hear the joy-inspiring sound.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Shout! ye saints! in rapturous song,
Let the strains be sweet and strong;
Shout the Son of God, this morn
From his sepulcher new-born.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Heaven displays her portals wide;
Glorious Hero! through them ride!
King of glory! mount the throne—
Thy great Father's and thine own.

title: '"The Lord is risen indeed!"
author: Thomas Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
'"The Lord is risen indeed!"
The grave hath lost its prey;
With him shall rise the ransomed seed
To reign in endless day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"The Lord is risen indeed!"
He lives to die no more;
He lives his people's cause to plead,
Whose curse and shame he bore.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
"The Lord is risen indeed!"
Attending angels hear;
Up to the courts of heaven with speed,
The joyful tidings bear.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then take your golden lyres,
And strike each cheerful chord;
Join all the bright celestial choirs,
To sing our risen Lord.

title: Now for a tune of lofty praise
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now for a tune of lofty praise
To great Jehovah's equal Son;
Awake, my voice, in heavenly lays,
And tell the wonders he hath done.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sing how he left the worlds of light,
And those bright robes he wore above;
How swift and joyful was his flight,
On wings of everlasting love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Among a thousand harps and songs,
Jesus, the God, exalted reigns;
His sacred name fills all their tongues
And echoes through the heavenly plains.

title: The morning kindles all the sky
author: Latin Tr. by Mrs. E. Charles

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Vainly with rocks his tomb was barred
While Roman guards kept watch and ward;
Majestic from the spoiled tomb,
In pomp of triumph he has come!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When the amazed disciples heard,
Their hearts with speechless joy were stirred;
Their Lord's beloved face to see,
Eager they haste to Galilee.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Hail! morning known among the blest
author: E. Wardlaw

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hail! morning known among the blest,
Morning of hope, and joy, and love,
Of heavenly peace, and holy rest,
Pledge of the endless rest above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Blest be the Father of our Lord,
Who from the dead hath brought his Son;
Hope to the lost was then restored,
And everlasting glory won.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Mercy looked down with smiling eye
When our Immanuel left the dead;
Faith marked his bright ascent on high,
And hope with gladness raised her head.

title: I know that my Redeemer lives
author: Samuel Medley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
He lives, all glory to his name!
He lives, my Savior still the same—
Oh, the sweet joy this sentence gives:
I know that my Redeemer lives.

title: Rise, glorious Conqueror, rise
author: Matthew Bridges

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rise, glorious Conqueror, rise,
Into thy native skies,
Assume thy right;
And where, in many a fold,
The clouds are backward rolled;
Pass thro' these gates of gold,
And reign in light.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Enter, incarnate God!
No feet but thine have trod
The serpent down;
Blow the full trumpets, blow!
Wider your portals throw!
Savior, triumphant, go
And take thy crown.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lion of Judah, hail!
And let thy name prevail
From age to age;
Lord of the rolling years,
Claim for thine own the spheres,
For thou hast bought with tears
Thine heritage.

title: Hark! ten thousand harps and voices
author: Thomas Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Savior! hasten thine appearing;
Bring, oh, bring the glorious day
When, the awful summons hearing,
Heaven and earth shall pass away;—
Then, with golden harps, we'll sing,—
"Glory to our King!"

title: Jesus comes, his conflict over
author: Thomas Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Yonder throne for him erected,
Now becomes the Victor's seat;
Lo, the man on earth rejected!
Angels worship at his feet:
Haste, ye saints! your tribute bring,
Crown him, everlasting King.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Day and night they cry before him,—
"Holy, holy, holy, Lord!"
All the powers of heaven adore him,
All obey his sovereign word;
Haste, ye saints! your tribute bring,
Crown him, everlasting King.

title: See, the Conqueror mounts in triumph
author: Christopher Wordsworth

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
See, the Conqueror mounts in triumph,
See the King in royal state,
Riding on the clouds, his chariot,
To his heavenly palace gate!
Hark! the choirs of angel voices
Joyful hallelujahs sing,
And the portals high are lifted
To receive their heavenly King.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Who is this that comes in glory,
With the trump of jubilee?
Lord of battles, God of armies,
He has gained the victory;
He, who on the cross did suffer,
He, who from the grave arose,
He has vanquished sin and Satan,
He by death has spoiled his foes.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: All hail the power of Jesus' name

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All hail the power of Jesus' name,
Let angels prostrate fall;
Bring forth the royal diadem,
And crown him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Crown him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this earthly ball;
Now hail the strength of Israel's might,
And crown him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ye chosen seed of Israel's race,
Ye ransomed from the fall,
Hail him who saves you by his grace,
And crown him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sinners, whose love can ne'er forget
The wormwood and the gall;
Go, spread your trophies at his feet,
And crown him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Let every kindred, every tribe
On this terrestrial ball,
To him all majesty ascribe,
And crown him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O that with yonder sacred throng
We at his feet may fall!
We'll join the everlasting song,
And crown him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text: Edward Perronet, alt. 1780.

title: Come, let us join in songs of praise
author: Anon

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, let us join in songs of praise
To our ascended Priest;
He entered heaven with all our names
Engraven on his breast.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Below he washed our guilt away,
By his atoning blood;
Now he appears before the throne,
And pleads our cause with God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Clothed with our nature still, he knows
The weakness of our frame,
And how to shield us from the foes
Which he himself o'ercame.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh! may we ne'er forget his grace,
Nor blush to wear his name;
Still may our hearts hold fast his faith,
Our mouths his praise proclaim.

title: The head, that once was crowned with thorns
author: Thomas Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The head, that once was crowned with thorns,
Is crowned with glory now;
A royal diadem adorns
The mighty Victor's brow.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The highest place that heaven affords
Is his—is his by right;
"The King of kings, and Lord of lords,"
And heaven's eternal Light.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The joy of all who dwell above,
The joy of all below,
To whom he manifests his love,
And grants his name to know.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
They suffer with their Lord below,
They reign with him above;
Their profit and their joy—to know
The mystery of his love.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
The cross he bore is life and health—
Though shame and death to him;
His people's hope, his people's wealth,
Their everlasting theme.

title: With joy we meditate the grace
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With joy we meditate the grace
Of our High Priest above;
His heart is made of tenderness,
His bowels melt with love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Touched with a sympathy within,
He knows our feeble frame;
He knows what sore temptations mean,
For he has felt the same.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He, in the days of feeble flesh,
Poured out his cries and tears;
And, in his measure, feels afresh
What every member bears.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then let our humble faith address
His mercy and his power;
We shall obtain delivering grace
In the distressing hour.

title: There's a glorious kingdom waiting in the land beyond the sky
author: D. W. Whittle

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There's a glorious kingdom waiting in the land beyond the sky,
Where the saints have been gath'ring year by year,
And the days are swiftly passing that will bring the kingdom nigh,
For the coming of the kingdom draweth near.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Oh, the coming of the kingdom draweth near;
Oh, the coming of the kingdom draweth near!
Be thou ready, O my soul, for the trumpet soon may roll,
And the King in his glory shall appear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis the hope of yonder kingdom, and the glory there prepared,
And the looking for the Savior to appear,
That delivers us from bondage to the world that once ensnared,
For the coming of the kingdom draweth near.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
With the coming of the kingdom we shall see our blessed Lord,
For the King ere the kingdom must appear;
Hallelujah to his name, who redeemed us by his blood!
Oh, the coming of the kingdom draweth near.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, the world is growing weary, it has waited now so long,
And the hearts of men are failing them for fear;
Let us tell them of the kingdom, let us cheer them with the song,
That the coming of the kingdom draweth near.

title: Come, thou long-expected Jesus
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, thou long-expected Jesus!
Born to set thy people free!
From our fears and sins release us,
Let us find our rest in thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Israel's strength and consolation,
Hope of all the earth thou art;
Dear desire of ev'ry nation,
Joy of ev'ry longing heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
By thine own eternal Spirit
Rule in all our hearts alone;
By thine all-sufficient merit
Raise us to thy glorious throne.

title: Our Lord is now rejected
author: D.W. Whittle

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our Lord is now rejected,
And by the world disowned,
By the many still neglected,
And by the few enthroned,
But soon he'll come in glory,
The hour is drawing nigh,
For the crowning day is coming by and by.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Oh, the crowning day is coming,
Is coming by and by,
When our Lord shall come in "power,"
And "glory" from on high.
Oh, the glorious sight will gladden,
Each waiting, watchful eye,
In the crowning day that's coming by and by.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The heavens shall glow with splendor,
But brighter far than they
The saints shall shine in glory,
As Christ shall them array,
The beauty of the Savior,
Shall dazzle every eye,
In the crowning day that's coming by and by.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Our pain shall then be over,
We'll sin and sigh no more,
Behind us all of sorrow,
And nought but joy before,
A joy in our Redeemer,
As we to him are nigh,
In the crowning day that's coming by and by.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let all that look for, hasten
The coming joyful day,
By earnest consecration,
To walk the narrow way.
By gathering in the lost ones,
For whom our Lord did die,
For the crowning day that's coming by and by.

title: Jesus! thy church, with longing eyes
author: William H. Bathurst

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus! thy church, with longing eyes
For thine expected coming waits;
When will the promised light arise,
And glory beam from Zion's gates?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
E'en now when tempests round us fall,
And wintry clouds o'ercast the sky,
Thy words with pleasure we recall,
And deem that our redemption's nigh.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh! come and reign o'er ev'ry land;
Let Satan from his throne be hurled,
All nations bow to thy command,
And grace revive a dying world.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Teach us, in watchfulness and prayer,
To wait for the appointed hour;
And fit us by thy grace to share,
The triumphs of thy conquering power.

title: Crown his head with endless blessing
author: William Goode

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Crown his head with endless blessing,
Who, in God the Father's name,
With compassions never ceasing,
Comes salvation to proclaim.
Hail, ye saints, who know his favor,
Who within his gates are found;
Hail, ye saints, th' exalted Savior,
Let his courts with praise resound.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lo, Jehovah, we adore thee;
Thee our Savior! thee our God!
From his throne his beams of glory
Shine through all the world abroad.
Jesus, thee our Savior hailing
Thee our God in praise we own;
Highest honors, never failing,
Rise eternal round thy throne.

title: Hail! my ever blessed Jesus
author: John Wingrove

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hail! my ever blessed Jesus!
Only thee I wish to sing.
To my soul, thy name is precious,
Thou, my Prophet, Priest, and King.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh! what mercy flows from heaven!
Oh! what joy and happiness!
Love I much? I've much forgiven;
I'm a miracle of grace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Once with Adam's race in ruin,
Unconcerned in sin I lay;
Swift destruction still pursuing,
Till my Savior passed that way

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Shout, ye bright angelic choir!
Praise the Lamb enthroned above;
Whilst, astonished, I admire
God's free grace, and boundless love.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
That blest moment I received him,
Filled my soul with joy and peace:
Love I much? I've much forgiven;
I'm a miracle of grace.

title: Come, Holy Ghost! in love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Holy Ghost! in love,
Shed on us, from above,
Thine own bright ray:
Divinely good thou art;
Thy sacred gifts impart,
To gladden each sad heart;
Oh! come to-day!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Come, Light serene, and still
Our inmost bosoms fill;
Dwell in each breast:
We know no dawn but thine;
Send forth thy beams divine,
On our dark souls to shine,
And make us blest.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text: Lat. Robert II. of France, 996. Tr., Ray Palmer, 1858.

title: Thou! whose almighty word
author: John Marriott

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou! whose almighty word
Chaos and darkness heard,
And took their flight,
Hear us, we humbly pray,
And, where the gospel's day
Sheds not its glorious ray,
"Let there be light!"

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou! who didst come to bring,
On thy redeeming wing,
Healing and sight,
Health to the sick in mind,
Sight to the inly blind;—
Oh! now to all mankind,
"Let there be light!"

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Spirit of truth and love,
Life-giving holy Dove!
Speed forth thy flight:
Move o'er the water's face,
Bearing the lamp of grace,
And, in earth's darkest place,
"Let there be light!"

title: Come, Holy Spirit, heavenly Dove
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Holy Spirit, heavenly Dove!
With all thy quickening powers,—
Kindle a flame of sacred love,
In these cold hearts of ours.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Look—how we grovel here below,
Fond of these trifling toys!
Our souls, how heavily they go,
To reach eternal joys.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In vain we tune our formal songs,
In vain we strive to rise;
Hosannas languish on our tongues,
And our devotion dies.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Dear Lord! and shall we ever live,
At this poor dying rate?
Our love so faint, so cold to thee,
And thine to us so great?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Come, Holy Spirit, heavenly Dove
With all thy quickening powers;
Come, shed abroad a Savior's love,
And that shall kindle ours.

title: Great Spirit! by whose mighty power
author: Thomas Howels

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great Spirit! by whose mighty power
All creatures live and move,
On us thy benediction shower;
Inspire our souls with love.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Thine inward witness bear, unknown
To all the world beside;
Exalting, then, we feel, and own
Our Jesus glorified.

title: Spirit Divine! attend our prayers
author: Andrew Reed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Spirit Divine! attend our prayers,
And make this house thy home;
Descend with all thy gracious powers,
Oh, come, great Spirit! come.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Come as the light; to us reveal
Our emptiness and woe;
And lead us in those paths of life
Where all the righteous go.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come as the fire; and purge our hearts,
Like sacrificial flame;
Let our whole soul an offering be
To our Redeemer's name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come as the dove; and spread thy wings,
The wings of peaceful love;
And let thy church on earth become
Blessed as the church above.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Come as the wind; with rushing sound
And pentecostal grace;
That all, of woman born, may see
The glory of thy face.

title: Why should the children of a King
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Why should the children of a King
Go mourning all their days?
Great Comforter, descend, and bring
Some tokens of thy grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Dost thou not dwell in all the saints,
And seal the heirs of heaven?
When wilt thou banish my complaints,
And show my sins forgiven?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Assure my conscience of her part
In the Redeemer's blood;
And bear thy witness with my heart,
That I am born of God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou art the earnest of his love,
The pledge of joys to come;
And thy soft wings, celestial Dove,
Will safe convey me home.

title: Eternal Spirit! by whose power
author: Wm. Riley Bathurst

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Eternal Spirit! by whose power
Are burst the bands of death,
On our cold hearts thy blessings shower,
And stir them with thy breath.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis thine to point the heavenly way,
Each rising fear control,
And, with a warm, enlivening ray,
To melt the icy soul.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis thine to cheer us when distressed,
To raise us when we fall;
To calm the doubting, troubled breast,
And aid when sinners call.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
'Tis thine to bring God's sacred word,
And write it on our heart;
There its reviving truths record,
And there its peace impart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Almighty Spirit! visit thus
Our hearts, and guide our ways;
Pour down thy quickening grace on us,
And tune our lips to praise.

title: Holy Spirit, faithful Guide
author: M.M. Wells

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Holy Spirit, faithful Guide,
Ever near the Christian's side;
Gently lead us by the hand,
Pilgrims in a desert land;
Weary souls fore'er rejoice,
While they hear that sweetest voice
Whisper softly, wanderer come!
Follow me, I'll guide thee home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Ever present, truest Friend,
Ever near thine aid to lend,
Leave us not to doubt and fear,
Groping on in darkness drear,
When the storms are raging sore,
Hearts grow faint, and hopes give o'er
Whisper softly, wanderer come!
Follow me, I'll guide thee home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When our days of toil shall cease,
Waiting still for sweet release,
Nothing left but heaven and prayer,
Wondering if our names were there;
Wading deep the dismal flood,
Pleading nought but Jesus' blood,
Whisper softly, wanderer come!
Follow me, I'll guide thee home.

title: Gracious Spirit, love divine
author: John Stocker

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Gracious Spirit, love divine,
Let thy light within me shine;
All my guilty fears remove,
Fill me full of heaven and love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Speak thy pardoning grace to me,
Set the burdened sinner free;
Lead me to the Lamb of God,
Wash me in his precious blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Life and peace to me impart!
Seal salvation on my heart;
Breathe thyself into my breast,
Earnest of immortal rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let me never from thee stray,
Keep me in the narrow way;
Fill my soul with joy divine,
Keep me, Lord, forever thine.

title: Spirit of pow'r, and truth, and love
author: William Lindsay Alexander

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Spirit of pow'r, and truth, and love,
Who sitt'st enthroned in light above!
Descend, and bear us on thy wings,
Far from these low and fleeting things.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis thine the wounded soul to heal,
'Tis thine to make the hardened feel;
Thine to give light to blinded eyes,
And bid the groveling spirit rise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When faith is weak, and courage fails,
When grief or doubt our soul assails,
Who can, like thee, our spirits cheer?
Great Comforter! be ever near.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Come, Holy Spirit, come
author: Joseph Hart

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Holy Spirit, come;
Let thy bright beams arise,
Dispel the sorrow from our minds,
The darkness from our eyes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Revive our drooping faith,
Our doubts and fears remove,
And kindle in our breasts the flame
Of never dying love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis thine to cleanse the heart,
To sanctify the soul,
To pour fresh life in ev'ry part,
And new create the whole.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Dwell, Spirit, in our hearts;
Our minds from bondage free.
Then shall we know, and praise, and love,
The Father, Son, and thee.

title: Hover o'er me, Holy Spirit

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou canst fill me, gracious Spirit,
Tho' I cannot tell thee how;
But I need thee, greatly need thee,
Come, oh, come, and fill me now.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text: E.H. Stokes, D.D.

title: Holy Spirit, Fount of blessing
author: Thomas J. Judkin

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Holy Spirit, Fount of blessing,
Ever watchful, ever kind,
Thy celestial aid possessing,
Prisoned souls deliverance find.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Seal of truth, and Bond of union,
Source of light, and Flame of love,
Symbol of divine communion,
In the olive-bearing dove.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Heavenly Guide from paths of error,
Comforter of minds distressed,
When the billows fill with terror;
Pointing to an ark of rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Promised Pledge, eternal Spirit,
Greater than all gifts below,
May our hearts thy grace inherit;
May our lips thy glories show!

title: Holy Ghost, dispel our sadness
author: Tr. by J.C. Jacobi

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
From the height which knows no measure,
As a gracious shower descend,
Bringing down the richest treasure
Man can wish, or God can send.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Hear, O hear our supplication,
Blessed Spirit, God of peace!
Rest upon this congregation,
With the fullness of thy grace.

title: Ah! how shall fallen man
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ah! how shall fallen man
Be just before his God?
If he contend in righteousness,
We fall beneath his rod.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If he our ways should mark
With strict inquiring eyes,
Could we for one of thousand faults
A just excuse devise?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
All-seeing, powerful God,
Who can with thee contend?
Or who that tries the unequal strife,
Shall prosper in the end?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ah! how shall guilty man
Contend with such a God?
None, none can meet him and escape,
But through the Savior's blood.

title: Astonished and distressed
author: Benjamin Beddome

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Astonished and distressed,
I turn mine eyes within;
My heart with loads of guilt oppressed,
The source of every sin.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What crowds of evil thoughts,
What vile affections there!
Envy and pride, deceit and guile,
Distrust and slavish fear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Almighty King of saints!
These tyrant lusts subdue;
Drive the old serpent from his seat,
And all my powers renew.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
This done,—my cheerful voice
Shall loud hosannas raise;
My heart shall glow with gratitude,
My lips be filled with praise.

title: How heavy is the night
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How heavy is the night
That hangs upon our eyes,
Till Christ with his reviving light
Over our souls arise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our guilty spirits dread
To meet the wrath of heaven;
But, in his righteousness arrayed,
We see our sins forgiven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The powers of hell agree
To hold our souls in vain;
He sets the sons of bondage free,
And breaks the cursed chain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord, we adore thy ways
To bring us near to God,
Thy sovereign power, thy healing grace,
And thine atoning blood.

title: How helpless guilty nature lies
author: Anne Steele

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How helpless guilty nature lies,
Unconscious of its load!
The heart, unchanged, can never rise
To happiness and God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Can aught, beneath a power divine,
The stubborn will subdue?
'Tis thine, almighty Spirit! thine,
To form the heart anew.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis thine, the passions to recall,
And upward bid them rise;
To make the scales of error fall,
From reason's darkened eyes.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh! change these wretched hearts of ours,
And give them life divine;
Then shall our passions and our powers,
Almighty Lord! be thine.

title: How sad our state by nature is
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How sad our state by nature is!
Our sin—how deep it stains!
And Satan binds our captive minds,
Fast in his slavish chains.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But there's a voice of sovereign grace
Sounds from the sacred word;—
"Ho! ye despairing sinners! come
And trust a faithful Lord."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My soul obeys the gracious call
And runs to this relief;
I would believe thy promise, Lord!
Oh! help my unbelief.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To the blest fountain of thy blood,
Incarnate God! I fly;
Here let me wash my spotted soul,
From crimes of deepest dye.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
A guilty, weak, and helpless worm,
On thy kind arms I fall;
Be thou my strength and righteousness
My Jesus, and my all.

title: Sinners, this solemn truth regard
author: John Fawcett

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sinners, this solemn truth regard,
Hear, all ye sons of men;
For Christ, the Savior, hath declared,
"Ye must be born again."

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Whate'er might be your birth or blood,
The sinner's boast is vain;
Thus saith the glorious Son of God,
"Ye must be born again."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
That which is born of flesh is flesh,
And flesh it will remain:
Then marvel not that Jesus saith,
"Ye must be born again."

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Spirit of life, thy grace impart,
And breathe on sinners slain:
Bear witness, Lord, in ev'ry heart,
That we are born again.

title: Buried in shadows of the night
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Buried in shadows of the night
We lie, till Christ restores the light;
Till he descends to heal the blind,
And chase the darkness of the mind.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our guilty souls are drowned in tears,
Till his atoning blood appears;
Then we awake from deep distress,
And sing the Lord our righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus beholds where Satan reigns,
And binds his slaves in heavy chains;
He sets the prisoners free, and breaks
The iron bondage from our necks.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Poor, helpless worms in thee possess
Grace, wisdom, power, and righteousness
Thou art our mighty all, and we
Give our whole selves, O Lord, to thee.

title: Vain are the hopes, the sons of men
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Vain are the hopes, the sons of men
On their own works have built;
Their hearts by nature all unclean,
And all their actions, guilt.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let Jew and Gentile stop their mouths,
Without a murm'ring word;
And the whole race of Adam stand
Guilty before the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In vain we ask God's righteous law
To justify us now,
Since to convince, and to condemn,
Is all the law can do.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus! how glorious is thy grace!
When in thy name we trust,
Our faith receives a righteousness,
That makes the sinner just.

title: There is a fountain filled with blood
author: William Cowper

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a fountain filled with blood,
Drawn from Immanuel's veins,
And sinners plunged beneath that flood,
Lose all their guilty stains.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Oh, glorious fountain!
Here will I stay,
And in thee ever
Wash my sins away.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The dying thief rejoiced to see,
That fountain in his day,
And there may I, though vile as he,
Wash all my sins away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou dying Lamb, thy precious blood,
Shall never lose its power,
Till all the ransomed church of God,
Are saved to sin no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
E'er since by faith I saw the stream
Thy flowing wounds supply,
Redeeming love has been my theme,
And shall be till I die.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And when this feeble, faltering tongue
Lies silent in the grave,
Then in a nobler, sweeter song,
I'll sing thy power to save.

title: When wounded sore, the stricken soul
author: Mrs. Cecil F. Alexander

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When wounded sore, the stricken soul
Lies bleeding and unbound:
One hand alone, a pierced hand,
Can heal the sinner's wound.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When sorrow swells the laden breast,
And tears of anguish flow,
One heart alone, a broken heart,
Can feel the sinner's woe.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis Jesus' blood that washes white,
His hand, that brings relief;
His heart, that's touched with all our joys,
And feeleth for our grief.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lift up thy bleeding hand, O Lord!
Unseal that cleansing tide;
We have no shelter from our sin,
But in thy wounded side.

title: Salvation! oh, the joyful sound
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Salvation! oh, the joyful sound!
What pleasure to our ears;
A sovereign balm for every wound,
A cordial for our fears.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Salvation! let the echo fly
The spacious earth around,
While all the armies of the sky
Conspire to raise the sound.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Salvation! O thou bleeding Lamb!
To Thee the praise belongs:
Salvation shall inspire our hearts,
And dwell upon our tongues.

title: How, vast, how full, how free

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How, vast, how full, how free,
The mercy of our God!
Proclaim the blessed news around,
And spread it all abroad.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I'm glad salvation's free!
I'm glad salvation's free!
Salvation's free for you and me,
I'm glad salvation's free!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How vast! "whoever will"
May drink at mercy's stream,
And know that faith in Jesus brings
Salvation now to him.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How full! it doth remove
The stain of every sin;
And makes the soul as white and pure,
As though no sin had been.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Poor trembling sinner, come!
God waits to comfort thee,
Come, cast thyself upon his love,
So vast, so full, so free.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: Vestry H. & T. Book.

title: Not all the blood of beasts
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Not all the blood of beasts,
On Jewish altars slain,
Could give the guilty conscience peace,
Or wash away the stain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But Christ, the heavenly Lamb,
Takes all our sins away;
A sacrifice of nobler name,
And richer blood than they.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My faith would lay her hand
On that dear head of Thine,
While like a penitent I stand,
And there confess my sin.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My soul looks back to see
The burden thou didst bear;
While hanging on the cursed tree,
And knows her guilt was there.

title: We have heard the joyful sound
author: Priscilla J. Owens

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We have heard the joyful sound,
Jesus saves, Jesus saves!
Spread the tidings all around,
Jesus saves, Jesus saves!
Bear the news to ev'ry land,
Climb the steeps and cross the waves;
Onward! 'tis our Lord's command;
Jesus saves, Jesus saves!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Waft it on the rolling tide,
Jesus saves, Jesus saves!
Tell to sinners far and wide,
Jesus saves, Jesus saves!
Sing, ye islands of the sea,
Echo back, ye ocean caves;
Earth shall keep her jubilee;
Jesus saves, Jesus saves!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sing above the battle strife,
Jesus saves, Jesus saves!
By his death and endless life,
Jesus saves, Jesus saves!
Sing it softly thro' the gloom,
When the heart for mercy craves;
Sing in triumph o'er the tomb,
Jesus saves, Jesus saves!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Give the winds a mighty voice,
Jesus saves, Jesus saves!
Let the nations now rejoice,
Jesus saves, Jesus saves!
Shout salvation full and free,
Highest hills and deepest caves;
This our song of victory,
Jesus saves, Jesus saves!

title: Like Noah's weary dove
author: Wm. A. Muhlenberg

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Like Noah's weary dove
That soared the earth around,
But not a resting place above
The cheerless waters found,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, cease, my wandering soul,
On restless wing to roam;
All the wide world, to either pole,
Has not for thee a home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Behold the ark of God,
Behold the open door;
Hasten to gain that dear abode,
And rove, my soul, no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There safe thou shalt abide,
There sweet shall be thy rest,
And every longing satisfied,
With full salvation blessed.

title: Sinners Jesus will receive
author: Arr. from Neumaster

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sinners Jesus will receive;
Sound this word of grace to all
Who the heavenly pathway leave,
All who linger, all who fall.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Sing it o'er and o'er again;
Christ receiveth sinful men,
Make the message clear and plain:
Christ receiveth sinful men.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Now my heart condemns me not,
Pure before the law I stand;
He who cleansed me from all spot,
Satisfied its last demand.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Christ receiveth sinful men,
Even me with all my sin;
Purged from every spot and stain,
Heaven with him I'll enter in.

title: Depth of mercy! can there be
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Depth of mercy! can there be
Mercy still reserved for me?
Can my God his wrath forbear?
Me, the chief of sinners, spare?

sections.label: Chorus
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Blow ye the trumpet, blow
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blow ye the trumpet, blow!
The gladly solemn sound,
Let all the nations know,
To earth's remotest bound,
The year of jubilee is come,
Return, ye ransomed sinners, home.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Arise, my soul, arise

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
My God is reconciled,
His pard'ning voice I hear,
He owns me for his child,
I can no longer fear;
With confidence I now draw nigh,
And Father, Abba, Father, cry.

title: I hear the Savior say
author: Mrs. Elvina M. Hall

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I hear the Savior say,
Thy strength indeed is small;
Child of weakness, watch and pray,
Find in me thine all in all.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Jesus paid it all,
All to him I owe;
Sin had left a crimson stain,
He washed it white as snow.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord, now indeed I find
Thy power, and thine alone,
Can change the leper's spots,
And melt the heart of stone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For nothing good have I
Whereby thy grace to claim—
I'll wash my garment white
In the blood of Calvary's Lamb.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When from my dying bed
My ransomed soul shall rise,
Then "Jesus paid it all"
Shall rend the vaulted skies.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And when before the throne
I stand in him complete,
I'll lay my trophies down,
All down at Jesus' feet.

title: Come to the blood-stained tree

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The Spirit will apply
His blood to cleanse thy stain;
Oh, burdened soul, draw nigh,
For none can come in vain!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Dark though thy guilt appear,
And deep its crimson stain,
There's boundless mercy here,
Oh, do not still disdain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Look not within for peace,
Within, there's nought to cheer;
Look up, and find release
From sin, and self, and fear.

title: Christ has for sin atonement made
author: E. A. Hoffman

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Christ has for sin atonement made,
What a wonderful Savior!
We are redeem'd, the price is paid,
What a wonderful Savior!

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
What a wonderful Savior is Jesus, my Jesus!
What a wonderful Savior is Jesus, my Lord!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I praise him for the cleansing blood,
What a wonderful Savior!
That reconciled my soul to God,
What a wonderful Savior!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He cleansed my heart from all its sin,
What a wonderful Savior!
And now he reigns and rules therein,
What a wonderful Savior!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He walks beside me in the way,
What a wonderful Savior!
And keeps me faithful day by day,
What a wonderful Savior!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
He gives me overcoming power,
What a wonderful Savior!
And triumph in each conflict hour,
What a wonderful Savior!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
To him I've given all my heart,
What a wonderful Savior!
The world shall never share a part,
What a wonderful Savior!

title: 'Tis grace, 'tis grace, 'tis wonderful grace
author: Rev. W. H. Burrell

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
'Tis grace, 'tis grace, 'tis wonderful grace,
This great salvation brings;
The soul, delivered of its load,
In sweetest rapture sings.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
'Tis grace, 'tis grace,
Wonderful, wonderful, wonderful grace,
'Tis grace, 'tis grace,
Flowing still freely for me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis grace, 'tis grace, 'tis wonderful grace,
Which saves the soul from sin,
The power of rising evil days,
And reigns supreme within.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Jesus, my Savior, to Bethlehem came
author: E. E. Hasty

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, my Savior, to Bethlehem came,
Born in a manger to sorrow and shame;
Oh, it was wonderful, blest be his name,
Seeking for me, for me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus, my Savior, on Calvary's tree
Paid the great debt, and my soul he set free;
Oh, it was wonderful, how could it be?
Dying for me, for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, my Savior, the same as of old,
While I did wander afar from the fold,
Gently and long he hath plead with my soul,
Calling for me, for me.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Behold a stranger at the door
author: Joseph Grigg

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
sections.text:
Oh, let the dear Savior come in,
He'll cleanse the heart from sin,
Oh, keep him no more out at the door,
But let the dear Savior come in.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, lovely attitude—he stands
With melting heart and loaded hands;
Oh, matchless kindness—and he shows
This matchless kindness to his foes.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But will he prove a friend indeed?
He will—the very friend you need;
The Friend of sinners? Yes, 'tis he.
With garments died on Calvary.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Rise, touched with gratitude divine,
Turn out his enemy and thine;
That soul-destroying monster, sin,
And let the heavenly stranger in.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Admit him, ere his anger burn—
His feet, departed, ne'er return;
Admit him, or the hour's at hand
You'll at his door rejected stand.

title: Oh, do not let the word depart

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
To-morrow's sun may never rise
To bless thy long-deluded sight;
This is the time, oh, then be wise!
Thou would'st be saved, why not to-night?

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Sinners, turn; why will ye die
author: Rev. C. Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sinners, turn; why will ye die?
God, your Maker, asks you why?
God, who did your being give,
Made you with himself to live;
He the fatal cause demands;
Asks the work of his own hands,—
Why, ye thankless creatures, why
Will ye cross his love, and die?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sinners, turn; why will ye die?
God, your Savior, asks you why?
He, who did your souls retrieve,
Died himself, that ye might live.
Will ye let him die in vain?
Crucify your Lord again?
Why, ye ransomed sinners, why
Will ye slight his grace and die?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sinners, turn; why will ye die?
God; the Spirit, asks you why?
He who all your lives hath strove,
Urged you to embrace his love.
Will ye not his grace receive?
Will ye still refuse to live?
O ye dying sinners, why,
Why will ye forever die?

title: Hasten, sinner! to be wise
author: Thomas Scott

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hasten, sinner! to be wise,
Stay not for the morrow's sun;
Wisdom, if thou still despise,
Harder is she to be won.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hasten, mercy to implore,
Stay not for the morrow's sun,
Lest thy season should be o'er,
Ere this evening's stage be run.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Hasten, sinner! to return,
Stay not for the morrow's sun,
Lest thy lamp should fail to burn,
Ere salvation's work is done.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hasten, sinner! to be blessed,
Stay not for the morrow's sun,
Lest perdition thee arrest,
Ere the morrow is begun.

title: Come, says Jesus' sacred voice
author: Mrs. Anna L. Barbauld

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou, who, houseless, sole, forlorn,
Long hast borne the proud world's scorn,
Long hast roamed this barren waste,
Weary pilgrim! hither haste.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ye, who, tossed on beds of pain,
Seek for ease, but seek in vain!
Ye, by fiercer anguish torn,
In remorse for guilt who mourn!—

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hither come, for here is found
Balm that flows for every wound,
Peace that ever shall endure,
Rest eternal, sacred, sure.

title: Why do you wait, dear brother
author: George F. Root

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Why do you wait, dear brother,
Oh, why do you tarry so long?
Your Savior is waiting to give you
A place in his sanctified throng.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Why not? why not?
Why not come to him now?
Why not? why not?
Why not come to him now?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What do you hope, dear brother,
To gain by a further delay?
There's no one to save you but Jesus,
There's no other way but his way.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Do you not feel, dear brother,
His Spirit now striving within?
Oh, why not accept his salvation,
And throw off thy burden of sin?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Why do you wait, dear brother,
The harvest is passing away,
Your Savior is longing to bless you,
There's danger and death in delay.

title: From the cross uplifted high
author: T. Haweis

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From the cross uplifted high,
Where the Savior deigns to die,
What melodious sounds we hear,
Bursting on the ravished ear!—
"Love's redeeming' work is done—
Come and welcome, sinner, come!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Sprinkled now with blood the throne—
Why beneath thy burdens groan?
On my pierced body laid,
Justice owns the ransom paid—
Bow the knee, and kiss the Son—
Come and welcome, sinner, come!

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
"Soon the days of life shall end—
Lo, I come—your Savior, Friend!
Safe your spirit to convey
To the realms of endless day,
Up to my eternal home
Come and welcome, sinner, come!"

title: Ye wretched, hungry, starving poor
author: Anne Steele

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye wretched, hungry, starving poor!
Behold a royal feast,
Where mercy spreads her bounteous store,
For every humble guest.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh! come, and with his children taste
The blessings of his love:
While hope attends the sweet repast
Of nobler joys above.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
There, with united heart and voice,
Before th' eternal throne,
Ten thousand thousand souls rejoice,
In ecstasies unknown.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
And yet ten thousand thousand more
Are welcome still to come;
Ye longing souls! the grace adore,
Approach, there yet is room.

title: There is a line by us unseen
author: Joseph Addison Alexander

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a line by us unseen,
That crosses every path,
The hidden boundary between
God's patience and his wrath.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To pass that limit is to die,
To die as if by stealth;
It does not quench the beaming eye,
Nor pale the glow of health.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh! where is this mysterious bourne
By which our path is crossed;
Beyond which God himself hath sworn
That he who goes is lost?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
How far may we go on to sin?
How long will God forbear?
Where does hope end, and where begin
The confines of despair?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
An answer from the skies is sent,—
"Ye that from God depart,
While it is called to-day, repent,
And harden not your heart."

title: Come, humble sinner! in whose breast
author: Edmund Jones

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, humble sinner! in whose breast
A thousand thoughts revolve:
Come, with your guilt and fear oppressed,
And make this last resolve:—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"I'll go to Jesus, though my sin
Like mountains round me close;
I know his courts, I'll enter in
Whatever may oppose.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
"Prostrate I'll lie before his throne,
And there my guilt confess;
I'll tell him I'm a wretch undone,
Without his sovereign grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
"I can but perish if I go,
I am resolved to try;
For, if I stay away, I know
I must forever die."

title: Say, sinner, hath a voice within
author: Mrs. Ann B. Hyde

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Say, sinner, hath a voice within
Oft whispered to thy secret soul,
Urged thee to leave the ways of sin,
And yield thy heart to God's control?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sinner! it was a heavenly voice,—
It was the Spirit's gracious call;
It bade thee make the better choice,
And haste to seek in Christ thine all.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
God's Spirit will not always strive
With hardened self-destroying men;
Ye, who persist his love to grieve,
May never hear his voice again.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Sinner! perhaps this very day
Thy last accepted time may be:
Oh! should'st thou grieve him now away
Then hope may never beam on thee.

title: Just as thou art—without one trace
author: Russell S. Cook

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Just as thou art—without one trace
Of love, or joy, or inward grace,—
Or meekness for the heav'nly place,—
Oh, guilty sinner! come,—now come.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy sins I bore on Calvary's tree;
The stripes, thy due, were laid on me,
That peace and pardon might be free;—
Oh, wretched sinner! come,—now come.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Burdened with guilt, would'st thou be blessed?
Trust not the world; it gives no rest;
I bring relief to hearts oppressed;—
Oh, weary sinner! come,—now come.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come, hither bring thy boding fears,
Thy aching heart, thy bursting tears;
'Tis mercy's voice salutes thine ears;—
Oh, trembling sinner! come,—now come.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
"The Spirit and the Bride say, Come!"
Rejoicing saints re-echo, "Come!"
Who faints, who thirsts, who will, may come;
Thy Savior bids thee come,—now come.

title: Jesus is tenderly calling thee home
author: Fanny J. Crosby

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus is tenderly calling thee home—
Calling to-day, calling to-day;
Why from the sunshine of love wilt thou roam
Farther and farther away?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Calling to-day,
Calling to-day.
Jesus is calling,
Is tenderly calling to-day.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Oh, turn ye, oh, turn ye, for why will ye die
author: Josiah Hopkins

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, turn ye, oh, turn ye, for why will ye die,
When God, in great mercy, is coming so nigh?
Now Jesus invites you, the Spirit says, "Come!"
And angels are waiting to welcome you home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How vain the delusion, that while you delay,
Your hearts may grow better by staying away!
Come wretched, come starving, come just as you be,
While streams of salvation are flowing so free.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And now Christ is ready your souls to receive;
Oh, how can you question, if you will believe?
If sin is your burden, why will you not come?
'Tis you he bids welcome; he bids you come home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Why will you be starving, and feeding on air?
There's mercy in Jesus, enough and to spare;
If still you are doubting, make trial and see.
And prove that his mercy is boundless and free.

title: Delay not, delay not; oh, sinner! draw near
author: Thomas Hastings

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Delay not, delay not; why longer abuse
The love and compassion of Jesus, thy God?
A fountain is opened,—how canst thou refuse
To wash, and be cleansed in his pardoning blood?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Delay not, delay not, oh, sinner! to come,
For mercy still lingers and calls thee to-day;
Her voice is not heard in the vale of the tomb,—
Her message, unheeded, will soon pass away.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Delay not, delay not; the Spirit of grace,
Long grieved and resisted, may take its sad flight;
And leave thee in darkness to finish thy race,—
To sink in the vale of eternity's night.

title: There's a wideness in God's mercy

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There's a wideness in God's mercy,
Like the wideness of the sea;
There's a kindness in his justice,
Which is more than liberty.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
He is calling, "Come to me;"
Lord, I'll gladly haste to thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There's no place where earthly sorrows
Are more felt than up in heaven;
There's no place where earthly failings
Have such kindly judgment given.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For the love of God is broader
Than the measure of man's mind,
And the heart of the Eternal
Is most wonderfully kind.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But we make his love too narrow,
By false limits of our own;
And we magnify his strictness
With a zeal he will not own.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
If our love were but more simple,
We should take him at his word;
And our lives would be all sunshine
In the sweetness of our Lord.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text: Frederick Faber, ab.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Come to Jesus, come to Jesus,
Come to Jesus just now,
Just now come to Jesus,
Come to Jesus just now.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text: He will save you.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text: Oh, believe him.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: He is able.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text: He is willing.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text: He'll receive you.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text: Call upon him.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text: He will hear you.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text: Look unto him.

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text: He'll forgive you.

sections.label: Verse 12
sections.text: Flee to Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 13
sections.text: He will cleanse you.

sections.label: Verse 14
sections.text: He will clothe you.

sections.label: Verse 15
sections.text: Jesus loves you.

sections.label: Verse 16
sections.text: Don't reject him.

sections.label: Verse 17
sections.text: Only trust him.

sections.label: Verse 18
sections.text: Hallelujah. Amen.

title: Who'll be the next to follow Jesus
author: Annie S. Hawks

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Who'll be the next to follow Jesus?
Who'll be the next the cross to bear?
Someone is ready, someone is waiting;
Who'll be the next a crown to wear?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Who'll be the next? Who'll be the next?
Who'll be the next to follow Jesus?
Who'll be the next to follow Jesus now?
Follow Jesus now?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Who'll be the next to follow Jesus—
Follow his weary, bleeding feet?
Who'll be the next to lay ev'ry burden
Down at the Father's mercy-seat?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Who'll be the next to follow Jesus?
Who'll be the next to praise his name?
Who'll swell the chorus of free redemption—
Sing, hallelujah! praise the Lamb?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Who'll be the next to follow Jesus,
Down thro' the Jordan's rolling tide?
Who'll be the next to join with the ransomed,
Singing upon the other side?

title: There's a stranger at the door
author: Rev. J. B. Atchison

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There's a stranger at the door,
Let him in,
He has been there oft before,
Let him in;
Let him in ere he is gone,
Let him in, the Holy One,
Jesus Christ, the Father's Son,
Let him in.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Open now to him your heart,
Let him in,
If you wait he will depart,
Let him in;
Let him in, he is your Friend,
He your soul will sure defend,
He will keep you to the end,
Let him in.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Hear you now his loving voice?
Let him in,
Now, oh, now make him your choice
Let him in;
He is standing at the door,
Joy to you he will restore,
And his name you will adore,
Let him in.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now admit the heavenly Guest,
Let him in,
He will make for you a feast,
Let him in;
He will speak your sins forgiv'n,
And when earth ties all are riven,
He will take you home to heaven,

title: "Almost persuaded" now to believe
author: P. P. Bliss

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
"Almost persuaded," harvest is past!
"Almost persuaded," doom comes at last!
"Almost" cannot avail;
"Almost" is but to fail!
Sad, sad that bitter wail,—
"Almost," but lost!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To-day the Savior calls!
Ye wand'rers, come,
Oh, ye benighted souls,
Why longer roam?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To-day the Savior calls!
Oh, hear him now;
Within these sacred walls
To Jesus bow.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Today the Savior calls!
For refuge fly!
The storm of justice falls,
And death is nigh.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Come, ye sinners, poor and needy

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text: Joseph Hart, 1759.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Turn to the Lord and seek salvation,
Sound the praise of his dear name:
Glory, honor, and salvation,
Christ, the Lord, is come to reign.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I will arise and go to Jesus,
He will embrace me in his arms,
In the arms of my dear Savior,
Oh, there are ten thousand charms!

title: Listen, sinner! mercy hails you
author: Andrew Reed

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
See! the storm of vengeance gathering
O'er the path you dare to tread!
Hark! the awful thunders rolling
Loud and louder o'er your head!
Flee, oh, sinner!
Lest the lightnings strike you dead.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Dropping souls! no longer mourn
author: Thomas Hastings

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
He has pardons full and free,
Drooping souls to gladden;
Still he cries—"Come unto me,
Weary, heavy laden!"
Tho' your sins, like mountains high,
Rise, and reach to heaven,
Soon as you on him rely,
All shall be forgiven.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Soon the evening shadows falling
author: J. W. Slaughenhaupt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Soon the evening shadows falling
Close the day of mortal life;
Soon the hand of death appalling
Draws thee from its weary strife.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Are you ready? are you ready?
'Tis the Spirit calling, why delay?
Are you ready? are you ready?
Do not linger longer, come to-day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Soon the awful trumpet sounding
Calls thee to the judgment throne;
Now prepare, for love abounding
Yet has left thee not alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, how fatal 'tis to linger!
Art thou ready—ready now?
Ready should Death's icy finger
Lay its chill upon thy brow?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Priceless love and free salvation
Freely still are offered thee;
Yield no longer to temptation,
But from sin and sorrow flee.

title: Broad is the road that leads to death
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Broad is the road that leads to death,
And thousands walk together there;
But wisdom shows a narrow path,
With here and there a traveler.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Deny thyself and take thy cross,"
Is the Redeemer's great command;
Nature must count her gold but dross,
If she would gain this heavenly land.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The fearful soul that tires and faints,
And walks the ways of God no more,
Is but esteemed almost a saint.
And makes his own destruction sure.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord, let not all my hopes be vain;
Create my heart entirely new—
Which hypocrites could ne'er attain,
Which false apostates never knew.

title: Oh, where shall rest be found
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, where shall rest be found—
Rest for the weary soul?
'Twere vain the ocean depths to sound,
Or pierce to either pole.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The world can never give
The bliss for which we sigh;
'Tis not the whole of life to live,
Nor all of death to die.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Beyond this vale of tears
There is a life above,
Unmeasured by the flight of years;
And all that life is love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There is a death, whose pang
Outlasts the fleeting breath;
Oh, what eternal horrors hang
Around the second death!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord God of truth and grace,
Teach us that death to shun,
Lest we be banished from thy face,
And evermore undone.

title: How sad would it be, if when thou didst call
author: W. O. Cushing

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How sad would it be, if when thou didst call,
All hopeless and unforgiven,
The angel that stands at the beautiful gate,
Should answer, No room in heaven.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Sad, sad, sad would it be!
No room in heaven for thee!
No room, no room,
No room in heaven for thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How sad it would be, the harvest all past,
The bright summer days all over;
To know that the reapers had gathered the grain,
And left thee alone forever.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, haste thee, and fly, while mercy is near,
Remember the love that he gave you;
The love that has sought thee is seeking thee still,
