And Jesus now waits to save you.

title: Called to the feast by the King are we
author: J.E. Landor

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Called to the feast by the King are we,
Sitting, perhaps, where his people be,
How will it fare, friend, with thee and me,
When the King comes in?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
When the King comes in, brother,
When the King comes in!
How will it fare with thee and me
When the King comes in?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Crowns on the head where the thorns have been,
Glorified he who once died for men,
Splendid the vision before us then,
When the King comes in.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Like lightning's flash will that instant show
Things hidden long from both friend and foe,
Just what we are will each neighbor know,
When the King comes in.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Joyful his eye shall on each one rest
Who is in white wedding garments dressed,
Ah, well for us if we stand the test,
When the King comes in.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Endless the separation then,
Bitter the cry of deluded men,
Awful that moment beyond all ken,
When the King comes in.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Lord, grant us all, we implore thee, grace,
So to await thee each in his place,
That we may fear not to see thy face
When thou comest in.

title: The door of salvation is open wide
author: M. E. Servoss

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The door of salvation is open wide,
And Jesus invites you to come;
While mercy and pardon await within,
Oh, enter while yet there is room.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
When the door once is shut,
To entreat will be vain;
'Twill never, no, never
Be opened again.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Dear friends, if you ever should stand without,
And plead for admittance in vain,
You'd think of the Savior's entreating voice,
And long for this moment again.

title: Oh, that my load of sin were gone
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, that my load of sin were gone;
Oh, that I could at last submit
At Jesus' feet to lay it down—
To lay my soul at Jesus' feet.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Rest for my soul I long to find;
Savior of all, if mine thou art,
Give me the meek and lowly mind,
And stamp thine image on my heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Break off the yoke of inbred sin,
And fully set my spirit free;
I cannot rest till pure within—
Till I am wholly lost in thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Show pity, Lord, O Lord, forgive
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
My crimes, though great, cannot surpass
The power and glory of thy grace;
Great God, thy nature hath no bound,
So let thy pard'ning love be found.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, wash my soul from every sin,
And make my guilty conscience clean;
Here, on my heart, the burden lies
And past offenses pain mine eyes.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My lips with shame my sins confess,
Against thy law, against thy grace;
Lord, should thy judgment grow severe,
I am condemned, but thou art clear.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Yet save a trembling sinner, Lord,
Whose hope, still hovering round thy word,
Would light on some sweet promise there,
Some sure support against despair.

title: Stay, thou insulted Spirit, stay
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Stay, thou insulted Spirit, stay,
Though I have done thee such despite,
Nor cast the sinner quite away,
Nor take thine everlasting flight.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though I have steeled my stubborn heart,
And still shook off my guilty fears;
And vexed and urged, thee to depart,
For many long rebellious years.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Now, Lord, my weary soul release,
Upraise me with thy gracious hand,
And guide into thy perfect peace,
And bring me to the promised land.

title: Just as I am, without one plea
author: Charlotte Elliott

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Just as I am, without one plea,
But that thy blood was shed for me,
And that thou bidd'st me come to thee,
O Lamb of God, I come! I come!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Just as I am, and waiting not
To rid my soul of one dark blot,
To thee whose blood can cleanse each spot,
O Lamb of God, I come! I come!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Just as I am, tho' tossed about
With many a conflict, many a doubt,
Fightings within, and fears without,
O Lamb of God, I come! I come!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Just as I am—poor, wretched, blind;
Sight, riches, healing of the mind,
Yea, all I need, in thee to find,
O Lamb of God, I come! I come!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Just as I am—thou wilt receive,
Wilt welcome, pardon, cleanse, relieve;
Because thy promise I believe,
O Lamb of God, I come! I come!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Just as I am—thy love unknown
Hath broken every barrier down;
Now to be thine, yea, thine alone,
O Lamb of God, I come! I come!

title: And can I yet delay
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And can I yet delay
My little all to give?
To tear my soul from earth away,
For Jesus to receive?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Nay, but I yield, I yield,
I can hold out no more:
I sink, by dying love compelled,
And own thee conqueror.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Tho' late, I all forsake,
My friends, my all resign;
Gracious Redeemer, take, oh, take,
And seal me ever thine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come and possess me whole,
Nor hence again remove;
Settle and fix my wav'ring soul
With all thy weight of love.

title: Do you hear the Savior calling
author: W. S. Marshall

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Do you hear the Savior calling,
By the wooings of his voice?
Do you hear the accents falling?
Will you make the precious choice?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I am list'ning; oh, I'm list'ning
Just to hear the accents fall!
I am list'ning; oh, I'm list'ning
To the Savior's gentle call!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
By his Spirit he is wooing,
Softly drawing us to him,
Thro' the day and night pursuing,
With his gentle voice to win.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By the Word of Truth he's speaking
To the wand'ring, erring ones;
List! the voice the stillness breaking!
Hear the sweet and solemn tones!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
In his providential dealings,
Even in his stern decrees,
In the loudest thunders pealing,
Or the murm'ring of the breeze.

title: Father, I stretch my hand to thee
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, I stretch my hand to thee;
No other help I know:
If thou withdraw thyself from me,
Ah! whither shall I go?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I do believe, I now believe
That Jesus died for me;
And thro' his blood, his precious blood,
I shall from sin be free.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What did thine only Son endure.
Before I drew my breath?
What pain, what labor, to secure
My soul from endless death!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Jesus, could I this believe,
I now should feel thy power;
And all my wants thou would'st relieve,
In this accepted hour.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Author of faith! to thee I lift
My weary, longing eyes;
Oh, let me now receive that gift—
My soul without it dies.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Surely thou canst not let me die;
Oh, speak, and I shall live,
And here I will unwearied lie,
Till thou thy Spirit give.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
How would my fainting soul rejoice,
Could I but see thy face;
Now let me hear thy quick'ning voice,
And taste thy pard'ning grace.

title: Jesus! thou art the sinner's Friend
author: Richard Burnham

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Remember thy pure word of grace,—
Remember Calvary;
Remember all thy dying groans,
And, then, remember me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou wondrous Advocate with God!
I yield myself to thee;
While thou art sitting on thy throne,
Dear Lord! remember me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord! I am guilty—I am vile,
But thy salvation's free;
Then, in thine all abounding grace,
Dear Lord! remember me.

title: Approach, my soul, the mercy-seat
author: John Newton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Approach, my soul, the mercy-seat,
Where Jesus answers prayer;
There humbly fall before his feet,
For none can perish there.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy promise is my only plea,
With this I venture nigh;
Thou call'st the burdened souls to thee,
And such, O Lord, am I.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Bowed down beneath a load of sin,
By Satan sorely pressed;
By wars without and fears within,
I come to thee for rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, wondrous love! to bleed and die,
To bear the cross and shame;
That guilty sinners, such as I,
Might plead thy gracious name.

title: Jesus, my Lord, to thee I cry
author: Eliza H. Hamilton

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
sections.text:
Take me as I am,
Take me as I am;
Oh, bring thy free salvation nigh,
And take me as I am.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Helpless I am, and full of guilt,
But yet for me thy blood was spilt,
And thou canst make me as thou wilt,
But take me as I am.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I thirst, I long to know thy love,
Thy full salvation I would prove;
But since to thee I cannot move
Oh, take me as I am.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
If thou hast work for me to do,
Inspire my will, my heart renew,
And work both in and by me, too,
But take me as I am.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And when at last the work is done.
The battle o'er, the victory won,
Still, still my cry shall be alone,
Oh, take me as I am.

title: Would you lose your load of sin
author: D. W. Whittle

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Would you lose your load of sin?
Fix your eyes upon Jesus;
Would you know God's peace within?
Fix your eyes upon Jesus.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Jesus who on the cross did die,
Jesus who lives and reigns on high,
He alone can justify;
Fix your eyes upon Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Would you calmly walk the wave?
Fix your eyes upon Jesus;
Would you know his pow'r to save?
Fix your eyes upon Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Would you have your cares grow light?
Fix your eyes upon Jesus;
Would you songs have in the night?
Fix your eyes upon Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Grieving, would you comfort know?
Fix your eyes upon Jesus;
Humble be when blessings flow?
Fix your eyes upon Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Would you strength in weakness have?
Fix your eyes upon Jesus;
See a light beyond the grave?
Fix your eyes upon Jesus.

title: I stand; but not as once I did
author: Unknown

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I stand; but not as once I did,
Beneath my load of guilt;
The blessed Jesus bore it all—
For me his blood was spilt.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I stand; but not on Calvary's Mount,
With arms around the cross;
I have been there, and left behind
Earth's pleasures, joys, and dross.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I stand e'en now where he appears,
In union with my Lord;
In him I'm saved, oh, wondrous thought.
I read it in his word.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, bless the Lord! in him alone—
In him we are complete;
We live by faith! but soon in sight
Our coming Christ we'll greet.

title: Oh, wondrous, deep, unbounded love
author: Fanny Crosby

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, wondrous, deep, unbounded love,
My Savior, can it be
That thou hast borne the crown of thorns
And suffered death for me?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
At the cross, at the cross, where I first saw the light
And, the burden of my heart rolled away—
It was there by faith I received my sight,
And now I am happy all the day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I kneel, repenting, at thy feet,
I give myself to thee;
I plead thy merits, thine alone,
For thou hast died for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, let me plunge beneath the tide,
For sinners flowing free,
Then rise, renewed by grace divine,
And shout salvation free.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And when I reach thy place above,
My sweetest notes will be,
Redemption through a Savior's name,
Who bled and died for me.

title: I have found redemption in the Savior's blood

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I have found redemption in the Savior's blood,
I am saved by faith in his blood, in his blood;
I am sweetly trusting in the word of God
I am saved by faith in his blood.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I am saved, yes, sweetly saved,
I am saved by faith in the blood he shed for me,
I am saved, yes, sweetly saved,
I am saved by faith in his blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, how sweet the story of his wondrous grace,
I am saved by faith in his blood, in his blood;
I will trust in Jesus while I run my race,
I am saved by faith in his blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I will sing of Jesus while the days go by,
I am saved by faith in his blood, in his blood;
I will trust his promise, on his strength rely,
I am saved by faith in his blood.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I will keep on singing as I march along,
I am saved by faith in his blood, in his blood;
In my home in glory this shall be my song,
I am saved by faith in his blood.

title: Come, ev'ry soul by sin oppressed
author: J. H. Stockton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, ev'ry soul by sin oppressed,
There's mercy with the Lord;
And he will surely give you rest
By trusting in his word.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Only trust him, only trust him,
Only trust him now;
He will save you, he will save you,
He will save you now.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For Jesus shed his precious blood
Rich blessings to bestow;
Plunge now into the crimson flood
That washes white as snow.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yes, Jesus is the Truth, the Way,
That leads you into rest;
Believe in him without delay,
And you are fully blest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come, then, and join this holy band,
And on to glory go,
To dwell in that celestial land,
Where joys immortal flow.

title: Lord, I care not for riches
author: Mrs. Mary A. Kidder

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, I care not for riches,
Neither silver nor gold;
I would make sure of heaven,
I would enter the fold.
In the book of thy kingdom,
With its pages so fair,
Tell me, Jesus, my Savior,
Is my name written there?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Is my name written there?
On the page white and fair?
In the book of thy kingdom,
Is my name written there?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord, my sins, they are many,
Like the sands of the sea,
But thy blood, oh, my Savior,
Is sufficient for me;
For thy promise is written,
In bright letters that glow,
"Tho' your sins be as scarlet,
I will make them like snow."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, that beautiful city,
With its mansions of light,
With its glorified beings,
In pure garments of white;
Where no evil thing cometh
To despoil what is fair;
Where the angels are watching,
Yes, my name's written there.

title: Oh, how happy are they
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, how happy are they
Who their Savior obey,
And have laid up their treasures above;
Tongue cannot express
The sweet comfort and peace
Of a soul in its earliest love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That sweet comfort was mine,
When the favor divine
I first found in the blood of the Lamb;
When my heart it believed,
What a joy I received,
What a heaven in Jesus' name.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Twas a heaven below
My Redeemer to know,
And the angels could do nothing more
Than to fall at his feet,
And the story repeat,
And the Lover of sinners adore.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, all the day long,
Was my joy and my song;
O that all his salvation might see!
He hath loved me, I cried,
He hath suffered and died
To redeem such a rebel as me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
On the wings of his love
I was carried above
All sin and temptation and pain,
And I could not believe
That I ever should grieve—
That I ever should suffer again.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
I then rode on the sky,
Freely justified I,
Nor did envy Elijah his seat;
My soul mounted higher,
In a chariot of tire,
And the moon it was under my feet.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O the rapturous height
Of that holy delight
Which I felt in the life-giving blood,
Of my Savior possessed,
I was perfectly blest,
As if filled with the fullness of God.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Never more will I stray
From my Savior away,
But I'll follow the Lamb till I die;
I will take up my cross,
And count all things but loss,
Till I meet with my Lord in the sky.

title: There is a spot to me more dear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a spot to me more dear
Than native vale or mountain;
A spot to which affection's tear
Springs grateful from its fountain;
'Tis not where kindred souls abound—
Tho' that is almost heaven—
But where I first my Savior found,
And felt my sins forgiven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hard was my toil to reach the shore,
Long tossed upon the ocean,
Above me was the thunder's roar,
Beneath, the wave's commotion.
Darkly the pall of night was thrown
Around me, faint with terror;
In that dark hour how did my groans
Ascend for years of error.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sinking and panting as for breath,
I knew not help was nigh me,
And cried, O save me, Lord, from death—
Immortal Jesus, hear me.
Then, quick as thought, I felt him mine—
My Savior stood before me;
I saw his brightness round me shine,
And shouted glory, glory.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O sacred hour, O hallowed spot!
Where love divine first found me;
Wherever falls my distant lot,
My heart shall linger round thee:
And as from earth I rise, to soar
Up to my home in heaven,
Down will I cast my eyes once more,
Where I was first forgiven.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: William Hunter, D. D.

title: How solemn are the words
author: Anon

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How solemn are the words,
And yet to faith how plain,
Which Jesus uttered while on earth—
"Ye must be born again!"

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Ye must be born again!"
For so hath God decreed;
No reformation will suffice—
'Tis life poor sinners need.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
"Ye must be born again!"
And life in Christ must have;
In vain the soul may elsewhere go—
'Tis he alone can save.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"Ye must be born again!"
Or never enter heaven;
'Tis only blood-washed ones are there—
The ransomed and forgiven.

title: When peace, like a river, attendeth my way
author: H.G. Spafford

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When peace, like a river, attendeth my way,
When sorrows, like sea-billows, roll;
Whatever my lot, thou hast taught me to say,
It is well, it is well with my soul.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
It is well with my soul,
It is well, it is well with my soul.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Tho' Satan should buffet, tho' trials should come,
Let this blest assurance control,
That Christ hath regarded my helpless estate,
And hath shed his own blood for my soul.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My sin—oh, the bliss of this glorious tho't—
My sin—not in part but the whole,
Is nailed to his cross and I bear it no more,
Praise the Lord, praise the Lord, oh, my soul!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And, Lord, haste the day when the faith shall be sight,
The clouds be rolled back as a scroll,
The trump shall resound, and the Lord shall descend,
"Even so"—it is well with my soul.

title: 'Tis the promise of God, full salvation to give

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
'Tis the promise of God, full salvation to give
Unto him who on Jesus, his Son, will believe

sections.label: Chorus
Verse 2
sections.text:
Tho' the pathway be lonely, and dangerous, too,
Surely Jesus is able to carry me through.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Many loved ones have I in yon heavenly throng;
They are safe now in glory, and this is their song:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Little children I see standing close by their King,
And he smiles as their song of salvation they sing.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
There are prophets and kings in that throng I behold,
And they sing as they march thro' the streets of pure gold,

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
There's a part in that chorus for you and for me,
And the theme of our praises forever will be.

title: Lord! I know thy grace is nigh me
author: H.D. Ganse

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
While I sit in weary blindness,
Longing for the blessed light,
Many taste thy loving kindness;
"Lord! I would receive my sight."

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Ah! what touch is this that thrills me?
What this burst of strange delight?
Lo! the rapturous vision fills me!
This is Jesus! this is sight!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Room, ye saints that throng behind him!
Let me follow in the way;
I will teach the blind to find him
Who can turn their night to day.

title: "Mercy, oh, thou Son of David!"
author: John Newton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
"Mercy, oh, thou Son of David!"
Thus blind Bartimeus prayed;
"Others by thy word are saved,
Now to me afford thine aid."

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Many for his crying chid him,—
But he called the louder still;
Till the gracious Savior bade him,—
"Come, and ask me what you will."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Money was not what he wanted,
Though by begging used to live;
But he asked, and Jesus granted,
Alms which none but he could give.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"Lord! remove this grievous blindness,
Let mine eyes behold the day!"
Straight he saw, and, won by kindness,
Followed Jesus in the way.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Oh! methinks I hear him praising,
Publishing to all around,
"Friends! is not my case amazing?
What a Savior I have found!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
"Oh! that all the blind but knew him,
And would be advised by me!
Surely would they hasten to him,
He would cause them all to see."

title: Oh, the peace that fills my soul
author: Priscilla J. Owens

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, the peace that fills my soul,
Sitting at the feet of Jesus;
Cleansed from sin, made free and whole,
Sitting at the feet of Jesus.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
This is my abiding place,
Clothed with his abounding grace,
Looking upward to his face,
Sitting at the feet of Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Christ is mine in storm and calm,
Sitting at the feet of Jesus;
All my wounds are filled with balm,
Sitting at the feet of Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here I rest from toil and strife,
Sitting at the feet of Jesus;
Safe beneath the Tree of Life,
Sitting at the feet of Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come ye guilty and be healed,
Sitting at the feet of Jesus;
Freely is God's love revealed,
Sitting at the feet of Jesus.

title: Forever here my rest shall be
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Forever here my rest shall be,
Close to thy bleeding side;
'Tis all my hope and all my plea,
"For me the Savior died."

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My dying Savior and my God,
Fountain for guilt and sin,
Sprinkle me ever with thy blood,
And cleanse and keep me clean.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Wash me and make me thus thine own,
Wash me, and mine thou art!
Wash me, but not my feet alone,
My hands, my head, my heart!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Th' atonement of thy blood apply
Till faith to sight improve,
Till hope in full fruition die,
And all my soul be love.

title: Lord, I believe a rest remains
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, I believe a rest remains
To all thy people known;
A rest where pure enjoyment reigns,
And thou art loved alone.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A rest where all our soul's desire
Is fixed on things above;
Where fear, and sin, and grief expire,
Cast out by perfect love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, that I now the rest might know,
Believe and enter in:
Now, Savior, now the power bestow,
And let me cease from sin.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Remove this hardness from my heart;
This unbelief remove:
To me the rest of faith impart—
The Sabbath of thy love.

title: Oh! could I find from day to day
author: Benjamin Cleveland

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh! could I find from day to day,
A nearness to my God;
Then should my hours glide sweet away,
And live upon thy word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord! I desire with thee to live.
Anew from day to day,
In joys the world can never give,
Nor ever take away.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Thus, till my last expiring breath,
Thy goodness I'll adore;
And, when my flesh dissolves in death,
My soul shall love thee more.

title: Welcome, O Savior! to my heart
author: Hugh Bourne

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The world and Satan I forsake,—
To thee I all resign;
My longing heart, O Jesus! take,
And make it all divine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh! may I never turn aside,
Nor from thy bosom flee;
Let nothing here my heart divide—
I give it all to thee.

title: My God, I know, I feel thee mine
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God, I know, I feel thee mine,
And will not quit my claim
Till all I have is lost in thine,
And all renewed I am.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I hold thee with a trembling hand,
And will not let thee go,
Till steadfastly by faith I stand
And all thy goodness know.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, thine all-victorious love
Shed in my heart abroad:
Then shall my feet no longer rove,
Rooted and fixed in God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Refining fire, go through my heart,
Illuminate my soul;
Scatter thy life through every part,
And sanctify the whole.

title: My God! accept my heart this day
author: Matthew Bridges

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God! accept my heart this day,
And make it always thine,
That I from thee no more may stray,
No more from thee decline.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
May the dear blood, once shed for me,
My blest atonement prove,
That I, from first to last, may be
The purchase of thy love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let every thought, and work, and word,
To thee be ever given;
Then life shall be thy service, Lord!
And death the gate of heaven.

title: My gracious Lord! I own thy right
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My gracious Lord! I own thy right
To every service I can pay,
And call it my supreme delight,
To hear thy dictates and obey.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What is my being, but for thee,
Its sure support, its noblest end?
Thine ever-smiling face to see,
And serve the cause of such a Friend.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I would not breathe for worldly joy,
Or to increase my worldly good;
Nor future days or powers employ,
To spread a sounding name abroad.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
'Tis to my Savior I would live,
To him, who for my ransom died;
Nor could all worldly honor give
Such bliss as crowns me at his side.

title: He wills that I should holy be
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
See, Lord, the travail of thy soul
Accomplished in the change of mine;
And plunge me, every whit made whole,
In all the depths of love divine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
On thee, O God, my soul is stayed,
And waits to prove thine utmost will;
The promise by thy mercy made,
Thou canst, thou wilt in me fulfill.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
No more I stagger at thy power,
Or doubt thy truth, which cannot move;
Hasten the long-expected hour,
And bless me with thy perfect love.

title: Jesus, my all, to heav'n is gone
author: John Cennick

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
This is the way I long have sought,
And mourned because I found it not;
My grief a burden long has been,
Because I was not saved from sin.
The more I strove against its power,
I felt its weight and guilt the more;
Till late I heard my Savior say,
"Come hither, soul, I am the way."

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Lord, I am thine, entirely thine
author: Rev. Samuel Davies

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, I am thine, entirely thine,
Purchased and saved by blood divine,
With full consent thine I would be,
And own thy sovereign right in me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Grant one poor sinner more a place
Among the children of thy grace;
A wretched sinner, lost to God,
But ransomed by Immanuel's blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Here at that cross where flows the blood,
That bought my guilty soul for God,
Thee, my new Master now I call,
And consecrate to thee my all.

title: Jesus, I my cross have taken
author: Henry Francis Lyte

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, I my cross have taken,
All to leave and follow thee;
Naked, poor, despised, forsaken,
Thou, from hence, my all shalt be!
Perish, every fond ambition,
All I've sought, or hoped, or known,
Yet how rich is my condition,
God and heaven are still my own!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let the world despise and leave me—
They have left my Savior too;
Human hearts and looks deceive me—
Thou art not, like them, untrue.
And while thou shalt smile upon me,
God of wisdom, love, and might,
Foes may hate and friends disown me,
Show thy face and all is bright.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Go, then, earthly fame and treasure;
Come, disaster, scorn, and pain!
In thy service pain is pleasure,
With thy favor, loss is gain.
I have called thee, Abba, Father,
I have set my heart on thee;
Storms may howl, and clouds may gather—
All must work for good to thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Haste thee on from grace to glory,
Armed by faith, and winged by prayer;
Heaven's eternal day's before thee,
God's own hand shall guide thee there.
Soon shall close thy earthly mission,
Soon shall pass thy pilgrim days;
Hope shall change to glad fruition,
Faith to sight, and prayer to praise.

title: Love divine, all love excelling
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Carry on thy new creation;
Pure and holy may we be;
Let us see our whole salvation
Perfectly secured by thee:
Change from glory into glory,
Till in heaven we take our place,
Till we cast our crowns before thee,
Lost in wonder, love, and praise.

title: In thy service will I ever
author: P. Spitta

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In thy service will I ever,
Jesus, my Redeemer, stay;
Nothing me from thee shall sever,
Gladly would I go thy way.
Yes, Lord Jesus, I am ever
Thine in sorrow and in joy;
Death the union shall not sever,
Nor eternity destroy.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let thy light on me be shining
When the day is almost gone,
When the evening is declining,
And the night is drawing on:
Bless me, oh, my Savior! laying
Thy hands on my weary head;
"Here thy day is ended," saying,
"Yonder live the faithful dead."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Stay beside me, when the stillness
And the icy touch of death
Fill my trembling soul with chillness,
Like the morning's frosty breath;
As my failing eyes grow dimmer,
Let my spirit grow more bright,
As I see the first faint glimmer
Of the everlasting light.

title: Lord! I hear of showers of blessing
author: Elizabeth Coduer

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
sections.text:
Even me, even me,
Let their fullness fall on me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Pass me not, oh, gracious Father!
Sinful, though my heart may be;
Thou might'st curse me, but the rather
Let thy mercy fall on me.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Pass me not, oh, mighty Spirit!
Thou canst make the blind to see;
Witnesser of Jesus' merit,
Speak the word of power to me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Have I long in sin been sleeping,
Long been slighting, grieving thee?
Has the world my heart been keeping?
Oh! forgive and rescue me.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Love of God, so pure and changeless,—
Blood of God, so rich and free,—
Grace of God, so strong and boundless,—
Magnify them all in me.

title: Take me, oh, my Father! take me
author: Ray Palmer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Take me, oh, my Father! take me,
Take me, save me, through thy Son;
That which thou would'st have me, make me,
Let thy will in me be done.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Long from thee my footsteps straying,
Thorny proved the way I trod;
Weary come I now, and praying—
Take me to thy love, my God!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Fruitless years with grief recalling,
Humbly I confess my sin;
At thy feet, O Father! falling,
To thy household take me in.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Freely now to thee I proffer
This relenting heart of mine;
Freely, life and soul I offer—
Gift unworthy love like thine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Once the world's Redeemer dying,
Bore our sins upon the tree;
On that sacrifice relying,
Now I look in hope to thee.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Father! take me; all forgiving,
Fold me to thy loving breast;
In thy hope forever living,
I must be forever blest!

title: O Jesus! full of grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Jesus! full of grace,
To thee I make my moan:
Let me again behold thy face—
Call home thy banished one.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Again my pardon seal,
Again my soul restore,
And freely my backslidings heal,
And bid me sin no more.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: I cannot do without thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I cannot do without thee,
O Savior of the lost!
Whose precious blood redeemed me
At such tremendous cost.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I cannot, would not,
Dare not, could not,
Will not do without thee.
I have no strength or goodness,
No wisdom of my own.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I cannot do without thee,
I cannot stand alone;
I have no strength or goodness,
No wisdom of my own.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I cannot do without thee,
I do not know the way;
Thou knowest and thou leadest,
And wilt not let me stray.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I cannot do without thee,
For years are fleeting fast,
And soon, in solemn loneliness,
The river must be passed.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: Frances H. Havergal, Alt.

title: Mine eyes and my desire
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Mine eyes and my desire
Are ever to the Lord;
I love to plead his promises,
And rest upon his word.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
When shall the sov'reign grace
Of my forgiving God
Restore me from those dangerous ways
My wand'ring feet have trod?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, keep my soul from death,
Nor put my hope to shame;
For I have placed my only trust
In my Redeemer's name.

title: I am coming to the cross
author: Wm. McDonald

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Here I give my all to thee—
Friends, and time, and earthly store;
Soul and body thine to be—
Wholly thine—forevermore.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus comes! he fills my soul!
Perfected in love I am!
I am ev'ry whit made whole;
Glory! glory to the Lamb!

title: My life, my love I give to thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My life, my love I give to thee,
Thou Lamb of God, who died for me;
Oh, may I ever faithful be
My Savior and my God.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I'll live for him who died for me,
How happy, then, my life shall be!
I'll live for him who died for me,
My Savior and my God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I now believe thou dost receive,
For thou hast died that I might live;
And now henceforth I'll trust in thee,
My Savior and my God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, thou who died on Calvary,
To save my soul and make me free,
I consecrate my life to thee,
My Savior and my God.

title: Take my heart, dear Jesus
author: Baltzell

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Take my heart, dear Jesus,
Make it all thine own,
Let thy Holy Spirit
Break this heart of stone,
And make me all thine own.

sections.label: Chorus
Verse 2
sections.text:
Take my heart, dear Jesus,
Make it pure and clean;
Let thy blood, still flowing,
Wash away my sin,
And make me pure and clean.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Take my heart, dear Jesus,
Make it white as snow;
May the cleansing fountain,
May the precious flow,
Still keep me white as snow.

title: Take my life, and let it be
author: Frances Ridley Havergal

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Take my life, and let it be
Consecrated, Lord, to thee;
Take my hands and let them move
At the impulse of thy love.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Wash me in the Savior's precious blood, the precious blood,
Cleanse me in its purifying flood, the healing flood,
Lord, I give to thee my life and all, to be
Thine, henceforth, eternally.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Take my feet, and let them be
Swift and beautiful for thee;
Take my voice, and let me sing
Always, only for my King

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Take my lips, and let them be
Filled with messages for thee;
Take my silver and my gold—
Not a mite would I withhold.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Take my moments and my days,
Let them flow in endless praise;
Take my intellect, and use
Ev'ry pow'r as thou shalt choose.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Take my love,—my Lord, I pour
At thy feet its treasure-store!
Take myself, and I will be
Ever, only, all for thee!

title: Lord, weak and impotent I stand
author: M.A.W. Cook

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, weak and impotent I stand,
As fettered by an unseen hand;
Break thou the strong and subtle band,
And draw me close to thee.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Draw me close to thee, Savior,
Draw me close to thee;
Beneath thy wing do thou me hide,
And draw me close to thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, bring me nearer, nearer still,
That thine own peace my soul may fill,
And I may rest in thy sweet will;
Lord, draw me close to thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here, Lord, I would forever bide,
And never wander from thy side;
Beneath thy wing do thou me hide,
And draw me close to thee.

title: O holy Savior! Friend unseen
author: Charlotte Elliott

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O holy Savior! Friend unseen,
Since on thine arm thou bid'st me lean,
Help me, throughout life's changing scene,
By faith to cling to thee!

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Help me cling to thee, Savior,
Help me cling to thee!
Help me, throughout life's changing scene,
By faith to cling to thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Without a murmur I dismiss
My former dreams of earthly bliss;
My joy, my recompense be this,
Each hour to cling to thee!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Though faith and hope are often tried,
I ask not, need not, aught beside;
So safe, so calm, so satisfied,
The soul that clings to thee!

title: I am thine, O Lord, I have heard thy voice
author: Fanny J. Crosby

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I am thine, O Lord, I have heard thy voice,
And it told thy love to me;
But I long to rise in the arms of faith,
And be closer drawn to thee.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Draw me nearer, nearer, blessed Lord,
To the cross where thou hast died;
Draw me nearer, nearer, nearer, blessed Lord,
To thy precious, bleeding side.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Consecrate me now to thy service, Lord,
By the pow'r of grace divine;
Let my soul look up with a steadfast hope,
And my will be lost in thine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O the pure delight of a single hour
That before thy throne I spend,
When I kneel in pray'r, and with thee, my God,
I commune as friend with friend.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There are depths of love that I cannot know
Till I cross the narrow sea,
There are heights of joy that I may not reach
Till I rest in peace with thee.

title: Lord Jesus, I long to be perfectly whole
author: James Nicholson

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
sections.text:
Whiter than snow, yes, whiter than snow;
Now wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord Jesus, look down from thy throne in the skies,
And help me to make a complete sacrifice;
I give up myself and whatever I know—
Now wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord Jesus, for this I most humbly entreat;
I wait, blessed Lord, at thy crucified feet,
By faith for my cleansing, I see thy blood flow—
Now wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Have you been to Jesus for the cleansing pow'r
author: E.A. Hoffman

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Have you been to Jesus for the cleansing pow'r?
Are you washed in the blood of the Lamb?
Are you fully trusting in his grace this hour?
Are you washed in the blood of the Lamb?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Are you washed in the blood,
In the soul-cleansing blood of the Lamb?
Are your garments spotless, are they white as snow?
Are you washed in the blood of the Lamb?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Are you walking daily by the Savior's side?
Are you washed in the blood of the Lamb?
Do you rest each moment in the Crucified?
Are you washed in the blood of the Lamb?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When the Bridegroom cometh will your robes be white,
Pure and white in the blood of the Lamb?
Will your soul be ready for the mansions bright?
And be washed in the blood of the Lamb?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lay aside the garments that are stained with sin,
And be washed in the blood of the Lamb;
There's a fountain flowing for the soul unclean,
Oh, be washed in the blood of the Lamb.

title: Oh, now I see the crimson wave
author: Mrs. Phoebe Palmer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, now I see the crimson wave,
The fountain deep and wide;
Jesus, my Lord, mighty to save,
Points to his wounded side.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
The cleansing stream I see! I see!
I plunge, and oh, it cleanseth me;
Oh, praise the Lord! it cleanseth me,
It cleanseth me, yes, cleanseth me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I rise to walk in heaven's own light,
Above the world and sin,
With heart made pure, and garments white,
And Christ enthroned within.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Amazing grace! 'tis heaven below
To feel the blood applied;
And Jesus, only Jesus know,
My Jesus crucified.

title: I've reached the land of corn and wine
author: Edgar Page Stites

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I've reached the land of corn and wine.
And all its riches freely mine;
Here shines undimmed one blissful day,
For all my night has passed away.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
O Beulah land, sweet Beulah land,
As on thy highest mount I stand,
I look away across the sea,
Where mansions are prepared for me,
And view the shining glory shore,
My heaven, my home forevermore.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The Savior comes and walks with me,
And sweet communion here have we;
He gently leads me with his hand,
For this is heaven's border land.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A sweet perfume upon the breeze,
Is borne from ever vernal trees,
And flowers that never fading grow
Where streams of life forever flow.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The zephyrs seem to float to me,
Sweet sounds of heaven's melody,
As angels, with the white-robed throng,
Join in the sweet redemption song.

title: I am dwelling on the mountain
author: Rev. Wm. Hunter

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I am dwelling on the mountain,
Where the golden sunlight gleams
O'er a land whose wondrous beauty
Far exceeds my fondest dreams;
Where the air is pure ethereal,
Laden with the breath of flow'rs,
They are blooming by the fountain,
'Neath the amaranthine bow'rs.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Is not this land of Beulah,
Blessed, blessed land of light?
Where the flowers bloom forever,
And the sun is always bright.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I can see far down the mountains,
Where I wandered weary years,
Often hindered in my journey
By the ghosts of doubts and fears;
Broken vows and disappointments,
Thickly sprinkled all the way,
But the Spirit led unerring,
To the land I hold to-day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I am drinking at the fountain,
Where I ever would abide;
For I've tasted life's pure river,
And my soul is satisfied;
There's no thirsting for life's pleasures,
Nor adorning, rich and gay,
For I've found a richer treasure.
One that fadeth not away.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Tell me not of heavy crosses,
Nor the burdens hard to bear,
For I've found this great salvation
Makes each burden light appear;
And I love to follow Jesus,
Gladly counting all but dross,
Worldly honors all forsaking
For the glory of the cross.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Oh, the cross has wondrous glory!
Oft I've proved this to be true;
When I'm in the way so narrow
I can see a pathway thro';
And how sweetly Jesus whispers:
Take the cross, thou need'st not fear,
For I've tried this way before thee.
And the glory lingers near.

title: Majestic sweetness sits enthroned
author: Samuel Stennett

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Majestic sweetness sits enthroned
Upon the Savior's brow;
His head with radiant glories crowned,
His lips with grace o'erflow.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
No mortal can with him compare
Among the sons of men;
Fairer is he, than all the fair
Who fill the heavenly train.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He saw me plunged in deep distress,
And flew to my relief;
For me he bore the shameful cross,
And carried all my grief.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To heaven, the place of his abode,
He brings my weary feet;
Shows me the glories of my God,
And makes my joys complete.

title: I've found the pearl of greatest price
author: John Mason

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I've found the pearl of greatest price!
My heart doth sing for joy;
And sing I must, for Christ is mine!
Christ shall my song employ.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Christ is my Prophet, Priest, and King;
My Prophet full of light,
My great High Priest before the throne,
My King of heavenly might.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Christ is my peace; he died for me,
For me he gave his blood;
And, as my wondrous Sacrifice,
Offered himself to God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Christ Jesus is my All in All,—
My Comfort, and my Love;
My Life below, and he shall be
My Joy and Crown above.

title: Oh, for a thousand tongues, to sing
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, for a thousand tongues, to sing
My great Redeemer's praise,
The glories of my God and King
The triumphs of his grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My gracious Master, and my God,
Assist me to proclaim—
To spread, through all the earth abroad,
The honors of thy name.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus! the name that charms our fears,
That bids our sorrows cease;
'Tis music in the sinner's ears,
'Tis life, and health, and peace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He breaks the power of canceled sin,
He sets the pris'ner free:
His blood can make the foulest clean—
His blood availed for me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
He speaks—and, list'ning to his voice
New life the dead receive;
The mournful, broken hearts rejoice,
The humble poor believe.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Come, let us all unite to praise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, let us all unite to praise
The Savior of mankind;
Our thankful hearts in solemn lays
Be with our voices joined.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O Lord! we cannot silent be;
By love we are constrained
To offer our best thanks to thee,
Our Savior, and our Friend.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let every tongue thy goodness show,
And spread abroad thy fame;
Let every heart with praise o'erflow,
And bless thy sacred name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Worship and honor, thanks and love,
Be to our Jesus given,
By men below, by hosts above,
By all in earth and heaven.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: Martin Madan (?), 1760.

title: Awake, awake, the sacred song
author: Anne Steele

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Awake, awake, the sacred song,
To our incarnate Lord;
Let every heart and every tongue
Adore th' eternal Word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That awful Word, that sovereign Power,
By whom the worlds were made;
Oh, happy morn—illustrious hour—
Was once in flesh arrayed.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To dwell with misery here below,
The Savior left the skies,
And sunk to wretchedness and woe,
That worthless man might rise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Adoring angels tuned their songs,
To hail the joyful day;
With rapture, then, let human tongues
Their grateful worship pay.

title: Jesus, the very tho't of thee
author: Bernard of Clairvaux

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, the very tho't of thee
With sweetness fills my breast;
But sweeter far thy face to see,
And in thy presence rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Nor voice can sing, nor heart can frame,
Nor can the mem'ry find
A sweeter sound than thy blest name,
O Savior of mankind!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, hope of ev'ry contrite heart!
Oh, joy of all the meek!
To those who fall, how kind thou art!
How good to those who seek.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And those who find thee, find a bliss
Nor tongue nor pen can show;
The love of Jesus, what it is
None but his loved ones know.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus! our only joy be thou,
As thou our prize wilt be;
Jesus! be thou our glory now,
And through eternity.

title: O Jesus, Jesus, dearest Lord
author: Frederick Wm. Faber

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Jesus, Jesus, dearest Lord!
Forgive me, if I say,
For very love, thy sacred name
A thousand times a day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I love thee so, I know not how
My transports to control;
Thy love is like a burning fire
Within my very soul.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, wonderful! that thou should'st let
So vile a heart as mine
Love thee with such a love as this,
And make so free with thine!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O Light in darkness, Joy in grief!
O Heaven begun on earth!
Jesus my Love, my Treasure! who
Can tell what thou art worth?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O Jesus, Jesus, sweetest Lord!
What art thou not to me?
Each hour brings joys before unknown,
Each day new liberty.

title: Do not I love thee, oh, my Lord
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Do not I love thee, oh, my Lord?
Behold my heart, and see;
And turn each worthless idol out,
That dares to rival thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Do not I love thee, from my soul?
Then let me nothing love;
Dead be my heart to every joy,
Which thou dost not approve.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Is not thy name melodious still,
To mine attentive ear?
Doth not each pulse with pleasure thrill
My Savior's voice to hear?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou know'st I love thee, dearest Lord!
But, oh! I long to soar
Far from the sphere of mortal joys,
And learn to love thee more.

title: There is a name I love to hear
author: Frederick Whitfield

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a name I love to hear,
I love to sing its worth;
It sounds like music in mine ear,
The sweetest name on earth.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Oh, how I love Jesus,
Oh, how I love Jesus,
Oh, how I love Jesus,
Because he first loved me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It tells me of a Savior's love,
Who died to set me free;
It tells me of his precious blood,
The sinner's perfect plea.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
It tells me what my Father hath
In store for every day,
And, though I tread a darksome path,
Yields sunshine all the way.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
It tells of One, whose loving heart
Can feel my deepest woe,
Who in each sorrow bears a part,
That none can bear below.

title: How sweet the name of Jesus sounds
author: John Newton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How sweet the name of Jesus sounds
In a believer's ear;
It soothes his sorrow, heals his wounds,
And drives away his fear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It makes the wounded spirit whole,
And calms the troubled breast;
'Tis manna to the hungry soul,
And to the weary, rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Dear Name, the rock on which I build,
My shield and hiding-place;
My never-failing treasure, filled
With boundless stores of grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, my Shepherd, Savior, Friend,
My Prophet, Priest, and King,
My Lord, my Life, my Way, my End,
Accept the praise I bring.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I would thy boundless love proclaim
With every fleeting breath,
So shall the music of thy name
Refresh my soul in death.

title: Oh, when shall I see Jesus
author: Anon

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, when shall I see Jesus,
And reign with him above?
And drink the flowing fountain
Of everlasting love?
When shall I be delivered
From this vain world of sin?
And with my blessed Jesus
Drink endless pleasures in?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But now I am a soldier,
My Captain's gone before;
He's given me my orders,
And tells me not to fear;
And if I hold out faithful,
A crown of life he'll give,
And all his valiant soldiers
Eternal life shall have.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Through grace I am determined
To conquer, though I die,
And then away to Jesus
On wings of love I'll fly!
Farewell to sin and sorrow,
I bid them all adieu;
And you, my friends, prove faithful,
And on your way pursue.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh! do not be discouraged,
For Jesus is your friend;
And if you lack for knowledge,
He'll not forget to lend:
Neither will he upbraid you,
Though often you request;
He'll give you grace to conquer,
And take you home to rest.

title: To thee, my God and Savior
author: Thomas Haweis

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To thee, my God and Savior!
My heart exulting sings,
Rejoicing in thy favor,
Almighty King of kings!
I'll celebrate thy glory,
With all thy saints above,
And tell the joyful story
Of thy redeeming love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Soon as the morn with roses
Bedecks the dewy east,
And when the sun reposes
Upon the ocean's breast;
My voice, in supplication,
Well-pleased thou shalt hear:
Oh! grant me thy salvation,
And to my soul draw near.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By thee, through life supported,
I pass the dangerous road,
With heavenly hosts escorted,
Up to their bright abode;
There, cast my crown before thee.—
Now, all my conflicts o'er,—
And day and night adore thee:—
What can an angel more?

title: Children of the heavenly King
author: John Cennick

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Children of the heavenly King,
As we journey let us sing;
Sing our Savior's worthy praise,
Glorious in his works and ways.
We are trav'ling home to God,
In the way our fathers trod;
They are happy now, and we
Soon their happiness shall see.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Fear not, brethren; joyful stand
On the borders of our land;
Jesus Christ, our Father's Son,
Bids us undismayed go on.
Lord! obediently we'll go,
Gladly leaving all below:
Only thou our Leader be,
And we still will follow thee.

title: Earth has nothing sweet or fair
author: Tr. Frances Elizabeth Cox

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Earth has nothing sweet or fair,
Lovely forms or beauties rare,
But before my eyes they bring
Christ, of beauty Source and Spring.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When the morning paints the skies,
When the golden sunbeams rise,
Then my Savior's form I find
Brightly imaged on my mind.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When the day-beams pierce the night,
Oft I think on Jesus' light,—
Think,—how bright that light will be,
Shining through eternity.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When, as moonlight softly steals,
Heaven its thousand eyes reveals,
Then I think;—who made their light
Is a thousand times more bright.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When I see, in spring-tide gay,
Fields their varied tints display,
Wakes the thrilling thought in me,
What must their Creator be?

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Lord of all that's fair to see!
Come, reveal thyself to me;
Let me, 'mid thy radiant light,
See thine unveiled glories bright.

title: Crown him with many crowns
author: Matthew Bridges

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Crown him with many crowns,
The Lamb upon his throne;
Hark! how the heavenly anthem drowns
All music but its own!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Awake, my soul! and sing
Of him who died for thee;
And hail him as thy matchless King,
Through all eternity.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Crown him, the Lord of love!
Behold his hands and side,
Rich wounds, yet visible above
In beauty glorified.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Crown him, the Lord of peace!
Whose power a scepter sways,
From pole to pole, that wars may cease,
Absorbed in prayer and praise.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Crown him, the Lord of years!
The Potentate of time;
Creator of the rolling spheres,
Ineffably sublime!

title: Awake, and sing the song
author: Altered by Martin Madan

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Awake, and sing the song
Of Moses and the Lamb;
Wake, every heart, and every tongue!
To praise the Savior's name.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Sing on your heavenly way,
Ye ransomed sinners! sing;
Sing on, rejoicing, every day,
In Christ, th' eternal King.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Soon shall ye hear him say,
"Ye blessed children! come;"
Soon will he call you hence away,
And take his wanderers home.

title: Bless'd be thy love, dear Lord
author: John Austin

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Bless'd be thy love, dear Lord!
That taught us this sweet way,
Only to love thee for thyself,
And for that love obey.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, thou, our soul's chief Hope!
We to thy mercy fly;
Where'er we are, thou canst protect,
Whate'er we need, supply.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Whether we sleep or wake,
To thee we both resign;
By night we see, as well as day,
If thy light on us shine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Whether we live or die,
Both we submit to thee;
In death we live, as well as life,
If thine in death we be.

title: Oh, could I speak the matchless worth
author: Samuel Medley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, could I speak the matchless worth,
Oh! could I sound the glories forth,
Which in my Savior shine!
I'd soar and touch the heav'nly strings,
And vie with Gabriel while he sings,
In notes almost divine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I'd sing the precious blood he spilt,
My ransom from the dreadful guilt,
Of sin and wrath divine;
I'd sing his glorious righteousness,
In which all-perfect heav'nly dress
My soul shall ever shine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I'd sing the characters he bears,
And all the forms of love he wears,
Exalted on his throne;
In loftiest songs of sweetest praise,
I would to everlasting days,
Make all his glories known.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Well—the delightful day will come,
When he, dear Lord! will bring me home,
And I shall see his face:
There, with my Savior, brother, friend,
A blessed eternity I'll spend,
Triumphant in his grace.

title: Jesus! and shall it ever be
author: Joseph Grigg

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus! and shall it ever be,
A mortal man ashamed of thee!
Ashamed of thee, whom angels praise,
Whose glories shine thro' endless days.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Ashamed of Jesus! sooner far
Let evening blush to own a star;
He sheds the beams of light divine
O'er this benighted soul of mine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ashamed of Jesus! that dear Friend
On whom my hopes of heaven depend!
No; when I blush, be this my shame,
That I no more revere his name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ashamed of Jesus! yes, I may,
When I've no guilt to wash away;
No tear to wipe, no good to crave,
No fears to quell, no soul to save.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Till then—nor is my boasting vain—
Till then, I boast a Savior slain!
And, oh, may this my glory be
That Christ is not ashamed of me!

title: Jesus! my heart within me burns
author: Ray Palmer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus! my heart within me burns,
To tell thee all its conscious love;
And from earth's low delight it turns,
To taste a joy like that above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When thou to me dost condescend,
In love divine, thou blessed One,
The moments that with thee I spend,
Seem e'en as Heaven itself begun.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Though oft these lips my love have told,
They still the story would repeat;
To me the rapture ne'er grows old,
That thrills me, bending at thy feet.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Come, let us sing the song of songs
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, let us sing the song of songs,
With hearts and voices swell the strain;
The homage which to Christ belongs;—
"Worthy the Lamb, for he was slain!"

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Slain to redeem us by his blood,
To cleanse from every sinful stain;
And make us kings and priests to God:
"Worthy the Lamb, for he was slain!"

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To him who suffered on the tree,
Our souls, at his soul's price, to gain,
Blessing, and praise, and glory be!—
"Worthy the Lamb, for he was slain!"

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come, Holy Spirit! from on high,
Our faith, our hope, our love sustain,
Living to sing, and dying cry,—
"Worthy the Lamb, for he was slain!"

title: My faith looks up to thee
author: Ray Palmer

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
May thy rich grace impart
Strength to my fainting heart;
My zeal inspire;
As thou hast died for me,
Oh! may my love to thee
Pure, warm, and changeless be,
A living fire!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While life's dark maze I tread,
And griefs around me spread,
Be thou my Guide;
Bid darkness turn to day,
Wipe sorrow's tears away,
Nor let me ever stray
From thee aside.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When ends life's transient dream,
When death's cold, sullen stream
Shall o'er me roll,
Blest Savior! then, in love,
Fear and distrust remove;
Oh! bear me safe above,
A ransomed soul!

title: Jesus, thy name I love
author: J.G. Deck

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, thy name I love,
All other names above,
Jesus, my Lord!
Oh, thou art all to me!
Nothing to please I see,
Nothing apart from thee,
Jesus, my Lord!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When unto thee I flee,
Thou wilt my refuge be,
Jesus, my Lord!
What need I now to fear?
What earthly grief or care,
Since thou art ever near,
Jesus, my Lord!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Soon thou wilt come again!
I shall be happy then,
Jesus, my Lord!
Then thine own face I'll see,
Then I shall like thee be,
Then evermore with thee,
Jesus, my Lord!

title: Savior, more than life to me
author: Fanny J. Crosby

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Savior, more than life to me,
I am clinging, clinging close to thee;
Let thy precious blood applied,
Keep me ever, ever near thy side.

sections.label: Chorus
Verse 2
sections.text:
Thro' this changing world below,
Lead me gently, gently as I go;
Trusting thee, I cannot stray,
I can never, never lose my way.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let me love thee more and more,
Till this fleeting, fleeting life is o'er;
Till my soul is lost in love,
In a brighter, brighter world above.

title: More love to thee, O Christ
author: Mrs. E.P. Prentiss

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
More love to thee, O Christ,
More love to thee!
Hear thou the prayer I make
On bended knee:
This is my earnest plea—
More love, O Christ, to thee!
More love to thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Once earthly joy I craved—
Sought peace and rest;
Now thee alone I seek:
Give what is best.
This all my prayer shall be—
More love, O Christ, to thee;
More love to thee!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then shall my latest breath
Whisper thy praise;
This be the parting cry
My heart shall raise—
This still its prayer shall be,
More love, O Christ, to thee!
More love to thee!

title: Nearer, my God, to thee
author: Mrs. Sarah Flower Adams

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Nearer, my God, to thee,
Nearer to thee;
E'en though it be a cross
That raiseth me.
Still all my song shall be
Nearer, my God, to thee,—
Nearer to thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though like the wanderer
The sun gone down,
Darkness be over me,
My rest a stone,
Yet, in my dreams, I'd be
Nearer, my God! to thee,—
Nearer to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There let the way appear,
Steps unto heaven;
All that thou send'st to me,
In mercy given;
Angels to beckon me
Nearer, my God! to thee,—
Nearer to thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Or if, on joyful wing,
Cleaving the sky,
Sun, moon, and stars forgot,
Upward I fly,
Still all my song shall be,
Nearer, my God! to thee,—
Nearer to thee.

title: Fade, fade, each earthly joy
author: Mrs. Horatius Bonar

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Fade, fade, each earthly joy,
Jesus is mine:
Break ev'ry mortal tie;
Jesus is mine.
Dark is the wilderness,
Distant the resting-place;
Jesus alone can bless,
Jesus is mine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Tempt not my soul away:
Jesus is mine:
Here would I ever stay;
Jesus is mine:
Perishing things of clay,
Born but for one brief day!
Pass from my heart away,
Jesus is mine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Farewell, ye dreams of night!
Jesus is mine:
Mine is a dawning bright,
Jesus is mine:
All that my soul has tried,
Left but a dismal void;
Jesus has satisfied;
Jesus is mine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Farewell, mortality!
Jesus is mine:
Welcome, eternity!
Jesus is mine:
Welcome, ye scenes of rest!
Welcome, ye mansions blest!
Welcome a Savior's breast;

title: Ask ye what great thing I know
author: Rev. B. H. Kennedy

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ask ye what great thing I know
That delights and stirs me so?
What the high reward I win?
Whose the name I glory in?
Jesus Christ, the crucified.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What is faith's foundation strong?
What awakes my lips to song?
He who bore my sinful load,
Purchased for me peace with God;
Jesus Christ, the crucified.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Who is life in life to me?
Who the death of death will be?
Who will place me on his right
With the countless hosts of light?
Jesus Christ, the crucified.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Oh, that I could forever dwell
author: Andrew Reed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, that I could forever dwell
Delighted at the Savior's feet,
Behold the form I love so well,
And all his tender words repeat.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The world shut out from all my soul,
And heaven brought in with all its bliss,
Oh! is there aught, from pole to pole,
One moment to compare with this?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
This is the hidden life I prize,
A life of penitential love,
When most my follies I despise,
And raise my highest thoughts above.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When all I am I clearly see,
And freely own with deepest shame;
When the Redeemer's love to me
Kindles within a deathless flame.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thus would I live till nature fail
And all my former sins forsake;
Then rise to God within the veil,
And of eternal joys partake.

title: We praise thee, O God! for the Son of thy love
author: Wm. P. Mackay

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We praise thee, O God! for the Son of thy love,
For Jesus who died, and is now gone above.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Hallelujah! thine the glory,
Hallelujah! Amen.
Hallelujah! thine the glory,
Revive us again.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We praise thee, O God! for thy Spirit of light,
Who has shown us our Savior, and scattered our night.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
All glory and praise to the Lamb that was slain,
Who has borne all our sins, and has cleansed ev'ry stain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
All glory and praise to the God of all grace,
Who has bought us, and sought us, and guided our ways.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Revive us again; fill each heart with thy love;
May each soul be rekindled with fire from above.

title: Rejoice and be glad the Redeemer has come
author: H. Bonar

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rejoice and be glad the Redeemer has come!
Go look on his cradle, his cross and his tomb.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Sound his praises, tell the story,
Of him who was slain,
Sound his praises, tell with gladness,
He liveth again.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Rejoice and be glad: for the blood has been shed;
Redemption is finished, the price has been paid.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Rejoice and be glad: for the Lamb that was slain,
O'er death is triumphant, and liveth again.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Rejoice and be glad: for our King is on high;
He pleadeth for us on his throne in the sky.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Rejoice and be glad: for he cometh again—
He cometh in glory, the Lamb that was slain.

title: I hear thy welcome voice
author: Rev. L. Hartsough

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I hear thy welcome voice
That calls me, Lord, to thee
For cleansing in thy precious blood
That flowed on Calvary.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I am coming, Lord!
Coming now to thee!
Wash me, cleanse me, in the blood
That flowed on Calvary.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Tho' coming weak and vile,
Thou dost my strength assure;
Thou dost my vileness fully cleanse,
Till spotless all and pure.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis Jesus calls me on
To perfect faith and love,
To perfect hope, and peace, and trust,
For earth and heaven above.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
'Tis Jesus who confirms
The blessed work within,
By adding grace to welcomed grace,
Where reigned the power of sin.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And he the witness gives
To loyal hearts and free,
That every promise is fulfilled,
If faith but brings the plea.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
All hail, atoning blood!
All hail, redeeming grace!
All hail, the gift of Christ, our Lord,
Our strength and righteousness!

title: Jesus, my truth, my way
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, my truth, my way,
My sure, unerring light,
On thee my feeble steps I stay,
Which thou wilt guide aright.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My wisdom and my guide,
My counselor thou art;
Oh, never let me leave thy side,
Or from thy paths depart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Never will I remove
Out of thy hands my cause;
But rest in thy redeeming love,
And hang upon thy cross.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, make me all like thee,
Before I hence remove;
Settle, confirm, and 'stablish me—
And build me up in love.

title: Awake, my soul, to joyful lays
author: S. Medley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Awake, my soul, to joyful lays,
And sing thy great Redeemer's praise;
He justly claims a song from me,
His loving kindness, oh, how free!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He saw me ruined in the fall,
Yet loved me notwithstanding all;
He saved me from my lost estate—
His loving kindness, oh, how great!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Though numerous hosts of mighty foes—
Though earth and hell my way oppose;
He safely leads my soul along—
His loving kindness, oh, how strong!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When trouble, like a gloomy cloud,
Has gathered thick and thundered loud,
He near my soul has always stood—
His loving kindness, oh, how good!

title: Of him who did salvation bring

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Ask but his grace, and lo, 'tis given!
Ask, and he turns your hell to heaven;
Though sin and sorrow wound my soul,
Jesus, thy balm will make me whole.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis thee I love, for thee alone,
I shed my tears, and make my moan!
Where'er I am, where'er I move,
I meet the object of my love.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Bernard of Clairvaux,
tr. by A.W. Boehm, 1712

title: My hope is built on nothing less
author: Rev. Edward Mote

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My hope is built on nothing less
Than Jesus' blood and righteousness;
I dare not trust the sweetest frame,
But wholly lean on Jesus' name.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
On Christ, the Solid Rock, I stand,
All other ground is sinking sand.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When darkness veils his lovely face,
I rest on his unchanging grace;
In every high and stormy gale,
My anchor holds within the vail.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His oath, his covenant, his blood,
Support me in the whelming flood;
When all around my soul gives way,
He then is all my hope and stay.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When he shall come with trumpet sound.
O, may I then in him be found;
Dressed in his righteousness alone,
Faultless to stand before the throne.

title: So tender, so precious

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
So tender, so precious.
My Savior to me;
So true, and so gracious,
I've found him to be.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
How can I but love him?
But love him, but love him?
There's no friend above him,
Poor sinner, for thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
So patient, so kindly
Toward all of my ways;
I blunder so blindly,
He love still repays.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Of all friends the fairest
And truest is he;
His love is the rarest,
That ever can be.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
His beauty, tho' bleeding
And circled with thorns,
Is then most exceeding;
For grief him adorns.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: J.E. Rankin, D.D.

title: O thou, in whose presence my soul takes delight
author: Jos. Swain

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou, in whose presence my soul takes delight,
On whom in affliction I call;
My comfort by day, and my song in the night,
My hope, my salvation, my all.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Where dost thou at noon-tide resort with thy sheep,
To feed in the pastures of love?
And why in the valley of death should I weep,
Or alone in the wilderness rove?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, why should I wander an alien from thee,
Or cry in the desert for bread?
Thy foes will rejoice when my sorrows they see,
And smile at the tears I have shed.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He looks, and ten thousands of angels rejoice,
And myriads wait for his word;
He speaks, and eternity, fill'd with his voice,
Re-echoes the praise of the Lord.

title: How tedious and tasteless the hours
author: John Newton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How tedious and tasteless the hours
When Jesus no longer I see!
Sweet prospects, sweet birds, and sweet flowers
Have lost all their sweetness to me:
The midsummer sun shines but dim;
The fields strive in vain to look gay;
But when I am happy in him,
December's as pleasant as May.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Content with beholding his face,
My all to his pleasure resigned,
No changes of season or place
Would make any change in my mind:
While blest with a sense of his love,
A palace a toy would appear;
And prisons would palaces prove,
If Jesus would dwell with me there.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Dear Lord, if indeed I am thine,
If thou art my sun and my song,
Say, why do I languish and pine?
And why are my winters so long?
O, drive these dark clouds from my sky;
Thy soul-cheering presence restore;
Or take me unto thee on high,
Where winter and clouds are no more.

title: My Savior, whom absent I love
author: W. Cowper

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My Savior, whom absent I love,
Whom, not having seen, I adore
Whose name is exalted above
All glory, dominion, and power,—
Dissolve thou these bands that detain
My soul from her portion in thee;
Ah! strike off this adamant chain,
And make me eternally free!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When that happy era begins,
When arrayed in thy glories I shine,
Nor grieve any more, by my sins,
The bosom on which I recline,
Oh! then shall the veil be removed,
And round me thy brightness be poured!
I shall meet him, whom absent I loved,
I shall see, whom unseen I adored.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And then, nevermore shall the fears,
The trials, temptations, and woes,
Which darken this valley of tears,
Intrude on my blissful repose;
To Jesus, the crown of my hope,
My soul is in haste to be gone;
Oh! bear me, ye cherubim, up,
And waft me away to his throne!

title: I need thee ev'ry hour
author: Annie S. Hawks

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I need thee ev'ry hour,
Most gracious Lord;
No tender voice like thine
Can peace afford.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I need thee, oh, I need thee,
Ev'ry hour I need thee;
Oh, bless me now, my Savior
I come to thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
I need thee ev'ry hour,
In joy or pain;
Come quickly and abide,
Or life is vain.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
I need thee ev'ry hour,
Most Holy One;
Oh, make me thine indeed,
Thou blessed Son.

title: My gracious Redeemer I love
author: B. Francis

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My gracious Redeemer I love,
His praises aloud I'll proclaim:
And join with the armies above,
To shout his adorable name.
To gaze on his glories divine
Shall be my eternal employ;
To see them incessantly shine,
My boundless, ineffable joy.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He freely redeemed with his blood
My soul from the confines of hell,
To live on the smiles of my God,
And in his sweet presence to dwell:—
To shine with the angels in light,
With saints and with seraphs to sing,
To view, with eternal delight,
My Jesus, my Savior, my King!

title: I have found a friend in Jesus, he's everything to me

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
