I have found a friend in Jesus, he's everything to me,
He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul;
The Lily of the Valley, in him alone I see
All I need to cleanse and make me fully whole.
In sorrow he's my comfort, in trouble he's my stay,
He tells me ev'ry care on him to roll.
He's the Lily of the Valley, the bright and Morning Star,
He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He all my griefs has taken, and all my sorrows borne;
In temptation he's my strong and mighty tower;
I have all for him forsaken, and all my idols torn
From my heart, and now he keeps me by his power.
Tho' all the world forsake me, and Satan tempt me sore,
Thro' Jesus I shall safely reach the goal.
He's the Lily of the Valley, the bright and Morning Star,
He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He will never, never leave me, nor yet forsake me here,
While I live by faith and do his blessed will;
A wall of fire about me, I've nothing now to fear,
With his manna he my hungry soul shall fill.
Then sweeping up to glory to see his blessed face,
Where rivers of delight shall ever roll.
He's the Lily of the Valley, the bright and Morning Star,
He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul.

title: Down at the cross where my Savior died
author: Rev. E.A. Hoffman

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
sections.text:
Glory to his name,
Glory to his name,
There to my heart was the blood applied,
Glory to his name.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Oh, for a closer walk with God
author: W. Cowper

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, for a closer walk with God!
A calm and heavenly frame!
A light to shine upon the road
That leads me to the Lamb!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Where is the blessedness I knew
When first I saw the Lord?
Where is the soul-refreshing view
Of Jesus and his word?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
What peaceful hours I then enjoyed!
How sweet their memory still!
But now I find an aching void
The world can never fill.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Return, oh, holy Dove, return,
Sweet messenger of rest;
I hate the sins that made thee mourn,
And drove thee from, my breast.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The dearest idol I have known,
Whatever that idol be,
Help me to tear it from thy throne,
And worship only thee.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
So shall my walk be close with God,
Calm and serene my frame;
So purer light shall mark the road
That leads me to the Lamb.

title: Oh, for a heart to praise my God
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, for a heart to praise my God,
A heart from sin set free—
A heart that always feels thy blood,
So freely spilt for me;—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A heart resigned, submissive, meek,
My great Redeemer's throne,
Where only Christ is heard to speak,
Where Jesus reigns alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, for a lowly, contrite heart,
Believing, true, and clean,
Which neither life nor death can part
From him that dwells within;—

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A heart in every thought renewed,
And full of love divine;
Perfect, and right, and pure, and good,
A copy, Lord, of thine.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Amazing grace! how sweet the sound

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Amazing grace! how sweet the sound,
That saved a wretch like me!
I once was lost, but now am found,
Was blind, but now I see.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Twas grace that taught my heart to fear,
And grace my fears relieved:
How precious did that grace appear,
The hour I first believed!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Through many dangers, toils, and snares
I have already come;
'Tis grace has brought me safe thus far,
And grace will lead me home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The Lord has promised good to me,
His word my hope secures;
He will my shield and portion be,
As long as life endures.

title: We bless thee for thy peace, O God
author: Anon

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We bless thee for thy peace, O God
Deep as the soundless sea,
Which falls like sunshine on the road
Of those who trust in thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That peace which suffers and is strong,
Trusts where it cannot see,
Deems not the trial way too long,
But leaves the end with thee;—

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
That peace which flows serene and deep,
A river in the soul,
Whose banks a living verdure keep;
God's sunshine o'er the whole.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Such, Father! give our hearts such peace,
Whate'er the outward be,
Till all life's discipline shall cease,
And we go home to thee.

title: I heard the voice of Jesus say
author: Horatius Bonar

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I heard the voice of Jesus say,
"Come unto me and rest;
Lay down, thou weary one, lay down
Thy head upon my breast."

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I came to Jesus as I was,
Weary, and worn, and sad;
I found in him a resting-place,
And he has made me glad.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I heard the voice of Jesus say
"Behold! I freely give
The living water; thirsty one!
Stoop down, and drink, and live."

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I came to Jesus, and I drank
Of that life-giving stream;
My thirst was quenched, my soul revived,
And now I live in him.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I heard the voice of Jesus say,
"I am this dark world's Light;
Look unto me; thy morn shall rise,
And all thy day be bright."

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
I looked to Jesus, and I found,
In him my Star, my Sun;
And, in that light of life, I'll walk
Till traveling days are done.

title: How gentle God's commands
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How gentle God's commands!
How kind his precepts are!
Come, cast your burdens on the Lord,
And trust his constant care.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Why should this anxious load
Press down your weary mind?
Oh, seek your heavenly Father's throne,
And peace and comfort find.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
His Goodness Stands approved,
Unchanged from day to day;
I'll drop my burden at his feet,
And bear a song away.

title: Grace! 'tis a charming sound
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Grace! 'tis a charming sound
Harmonious to the ear!
Heaven with the echo shall resound,
And all the earth shall hear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Grace first contrived a way
To save rebellious man;
And all the steps that grace display,
Which drew the wondrous plan.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Grace led my roving feet
To tread the heavenly road;
And new supplies each hour I meet
While pressing on to God.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Behold what wondrous grace
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold what wondrous grace
The Father has bestowed
On sinners of a mortal race,
To call them sons of God!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Nor doth it yet appear
How great we must be made;
But when we see our Savior there,
We shall be like our Head.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A hope so much divine
May trials well endure,
May purge our souls from sense and sin,
As Christ the Lord is pure.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
If in my Father's love
I share a filial part,
Send down thy Spirit, like a dove,
To rest upon my heart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
We would no longer lie
Like slaves beneath the throne;
Our faith shall Abba, Father! cry
And thou the kindred own.

title: Come, thou Fount of ev'ry blessing
author: Robert Robinson

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, thou Fount of ev'ry blessing,
Tune my heart to sing thy grace;
Streams of mercy never ceasing,
Call for songs of loudest praise.
Teach me some melodious sonnet,
Sung by flaming tongues above;
Praise the mount—I'm fixed upon it,
Mount of thy redeeming love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here I'll raise mine Ebenezer,
Hither by thy help I'm come;
And I hope by thy good pleasure,
Safely to arrive at home.
Jesus sought me when a stranger,
Wand'ring from the fold of God,
He, to rescue me from danger,
Interposed his precious blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh! to grace how great a debtor
Daily I'm constrained to be!
Let thy goodness, like a fetter,
Bind my wand'ring heart to thee.
Prone to wander, Lord, I feel it;
Prone to leave the God I love—
Here's my heart, oh, take and seal it;
Seal it for thy courts above.

title: The pity of the Lord
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The pity of the Lord,
To those that fear his name,
Is such as tender parents feel;
He knows our feeble frame.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He knows we are but dust,
Scattered with ev'ry breath;
His anger, like a rising wind,
Can send us swift to death.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Our days are as the grass,
Or like the morning flow'r;
If one sharp blast sweep o'er the field,
It withers in an hour.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But thy compassions, Lord,
To endless years endure;
And children's children ever find
Thy words of promise sure.

title: Jesus, Lover of my soul
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, Lover of my soul,
Let me to thy bosom fly,
While the nearer waters roll,
While the tempest still is high!
Hide me, O my Savior, hide,
Till the storm of life is past;
Safe into the haven guide,
O receive my soul at last!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Other refuge have I none;
Hangs my helpless soul on thee:
Leave, O, leave me not alone,
Still support and comfort me:
All my trust on thee is stayed,
All my help from thee I bring;
Cover my defenseless head
With the shadow of thy wing!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou, O Christ, art all I want;
More than all in thee I find;
Raise the fallen, cheer the faint,
Heal the sick, and lead the blind.
Just and holy is thy name,
I am all unrighteousness:
False and full of sin I am,
Thou art full of truth and grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Plenteous grace with thee is found,
Grace to cover all my sin:
Let the healing streams abound:
Make and keep me pure within.
Thou of life the fountain art,
Freely let me take of thee:
Spring thou up within my heart,
Rise to all eternity.

title: Jesus, Savior, pilot me
author: Rev. Edward Hopper

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
As a mother stills her child,
Thou canst hush the ocean wild;
Boist'rous waves obey thy will,
When thou say'st to them "Be still!"
Wondrous Sov'reign of the sea,
Jesus, Savior, pilot me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When at last I near the shore,
And the fearful breakers roar
'Twixt me and the peaceful rest,
Then, while leaning on thy breast,
May I hear thee say to me,
"Fear not, I will pilot thee!"

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Savior! teach me, day by day,
Love's sweet lesson to obey;
Sweeter lesson cannot be,
Loving him who first loved me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
With a child-like heart of love,
At thy bidding may I move;
Prompt to serve and follow thee,
Loving him who first loved me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Teach me all thy steps to trace,
Strong to follow in thy grace;
Learning how to love from thee,
Loving him who first loved me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Love in loving finds employ—
In obedience all her joy;
Ever new that joy will be,
Loving him who first loved me.

title: O Lord, how full of sweet content
author: Mad. Guyon

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Lord, how full of sweet content
Our years of pilgrimage are spent!
Where'er we dwell, we dwell with thee,
In heaven, in earth, or on the sea.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To us remains nor place nor time;
Our country is in every clime:
We can be calm and free from care
On any shore, since God is there.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While place we seek, or place we shun,
The soul finds happiness in none;
But with our God to guide our way,
'Tis equal joy to go or stay.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Could we be cast where thou art not,
That were indeed a dreadful lot;
But regions none remote we call,
Secure of finding God in all.

title: Complete in thee! no work of mine
author: A.R.W

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Complete in thee! no work of mine
May take, dear Lord, the place of thine;
Thy blood has pardon bought for me,
And I am now complete in thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Complete in thee—no more shall sin
Thy grace has conquered, reign within;
Thy voice will bid the tempter flee,
And I shall stand complete in thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Complete in thee—each want supplied,
And no good thing to me denied,
Since thou my portion, Lord, wilt be,
I ask no more—complete in thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Dear Savior! when before thy bar
All tribes and tongues assembled are.
Among thy chosen may I be
At thy right hand—complete in thee.

title: In heavenly love abiding
author: Anna Letitia Waring

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In heavenly love abiding,
No change my heart shall fear,
And safe is such confiding,
For nothing changes here,
The storm may roar without me,
My heart may low be laid,
But God is round about me,—
And can I be dismayed?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Wherever he may guide me,
No want shall turn me back:
My Shepherd is beside me,
And nothing can I lack;
His wisdom ever waketh,
His sight is never dim,
He knows the way he taketh,
And I will walk with him.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Sometimes a light surprises
author: Wm. Cowper

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sometimes a light surprises
The Christian while he sings:
It is the Lord who rises
With healing on his wings;
When comforts are declining,
He grants the soul again
A season of clear shining,
To cheer it after rain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In holy contemplation,
We sweetly then pursue
The theme of God's salvation,
And find it ever new:
Set free from present sorrow,
We cheerfully can say,
Let the unknown to-morrow
Bring with it what it may.

title: "There shall be showers of blessing;"
author: D.W. Whittle

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
"There shall be showers of blessing;"
This is the promise of love;
There shall be seasons refreshing,
Sent from the Savior above.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Showers, showers of blessing,
Showers of blessing we need;
Mercy-drops round us are falling,
But for the showers we plead.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"There shall be showers of blessing;"—
Precious reviving again;
Over the hills and the valleys,
Sound of abundance of rain.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
"There shall be showers of blessing;"
Send them upon us, O Lord!
Grant to us now a refreshing,
Come, and now honor thy Word.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"There shall be showers of blessing;"
Oh, that to-day they might fall,
Now as to God we're confessing,
Now as on Jesus we call!

title: Oh, bliss of the purified! bliss of the free
author: Rev. F. Bottome

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, bliss of the purified! bliss of the free!
I plunge in the crimson tide opened for me!
O'er sin and uncleanness exulting I stand,
And point to the print of the nails in his hand.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Oh, sing of his mighty love,
Sing of his mighty love,
Sing of his mighty love, mighty to save.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, bliss of the purified! Jesus is mine!
No longer in dread condemnation I pine:
In conscious salvation I sing of his grace,
Who lifteth upon me the smiles of his face.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, Jesus, the crucified! thee will I sing!
My blessed Redeemer! my God and my King;
My soul, filled with rapture, shall shout o'er the grave,
And triumph in death in the mighty to save.

title: As pants the hart for cooling streams
author: Henry F. Lyte

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
As pants the hart for cooling streams,
When heated in the chase,
So pants my soul, O Lord, for thee,
And thy refreshing grace.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
As pants the hart for cooling streams,
So pants my soul, O Lord, for thee;
As pants the hart for cooling streams,
So pants my soul, O Lord, for thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For thee, my God, the living God,
My thirsty soul doth pine;
Oh, when shall I behold thy face,
Thou Majesty divine?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I sigh to think of happier days,
When thou, O Lord, wast nigh,
When ev'ry heart was tuned to praise,
And none more blest than I.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Why restless, why cast down, my soul?
Trust God, and thou shalt sing
His praise again, and find him still
Thy health's eternal spring.

title: In thy cleft, O Rock of Ages
author: Fannie J. Crosby

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In thy cleft, O Rock of Ages,
Hide thou me;
When the fitful tempest rages,
Hide thou me;
Where no mortal arm can sever
From my heart thy love forever,
Hide me, O thou Rock of Ages,
Safe in thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
From, the snare of sinful pleasure
Hide thou me;
Thou, my soul's eternal treasure,
Hide thou me;
When the world its power is wielding,
And my heart is almost yielding,
Hide me, O thou Rock of Ages,
Safe in thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In the lonely night of sorrow,
Hide thou me;
Till in glory dawns the morrow,
Hide thou me;
In the sight of Jordan's billow,
Let thy bosom be my pillow,
Hide me, O thou Rock of Ages,

title: Walk in the light! so shalt thou know
author: Bernard Barton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Walk in the light! so shalt thou know
That fellowship of love,
His Spirit only can bestow,
Who reigns in light above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Walk in the light! and thou shalt find
Thy heart made truly his,
Who dwells in cloudless light enshrined,
In whom no darkness is.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Walk in the light! and ev'n the tomb
No fearful shade shall wear;
Glory shall chase away its gloom,
For Christ hath conquered there.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Walk in the light! and thou shalt see
Thy path, though thorny, bright,
For God by grace shall dwell in thee,
And God himself is light.

title: My Father is rich in houses and lands
author: Hattie E. Buell. Arr

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My Father is rich in houses and lands.
He holdeth the wealth of the world in his hands!
Of rubies and diamonds, of silver and gold,
His coffers are full, he has riches untold.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I'm the child of a King,
The child of a King,
With Jesus, my Savior,
I'm the child of a King.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My Father's own Son, the Savior so fair,
Once wandered on earth human sorrow to share:
But now he is reigning forever on high,
He'll give us a home in the sweet by and by.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I once was an outcast stranger on earth,
A sinner by choice and an "alien" by birth!
But I've been "adopted," my name's written down:
An heir to a mansion, a robe, and a crown.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A tent or a cottage, why should I care?
They're building a palace for me over there!
Tho' exiled from home, yet my glad heart can sing:
All glory to God, I'm the child of a King.

title: Amid the trials which I meet
author: E.S. Lorenz

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Amid the trials which I meet,
Amid the thorns that pierce my feet,
One thought remains supremely sweet,
Thou thinkest, Lord, of me!

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Thou thinkest, Lord, of me,
Thou thinkest, Lord, of me,
What need I fear when thou art near,
And thinkest, Lord, of me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The cares of life come thronging fast
Upon my soul their shadow cast;
Their gloom reminds my heart at last,
Thou thinkest, Lord, of me!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let shadows come, let shadows go,
Let life be bright or dark with woe,
I am content, for this I know,
Thou thinkest, Lord, of me!

title: O thou, the contrite sinner's Friend
author: Charlotte Elliott

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou, the contrite sinner's Friend,
Who loving, lov'st them to the end,
On this alone my hopes depend
That thou wilt plead for me.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
O Savior, plead for me,
O Savior, plead for me,
On this alone my hopes depend
That thou wilt plead for me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When weary in the Christian race,
Far off appears my resting place,
And, fainting, I mistrust thy grace,
Then, Savior, plead for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When I have erred and gone astray,
Afar from thine and wisdom's way,
And see no glimmering, guiding ray,
Still, Savior, plead for me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When Satan, by my sins made bold,
Strives from thy cross to loose my hold,
Then with thy pitying arms enfold,
And plead, oh, plead for me!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And when my dying hour draws near,
Darkened with anguish, guilt and fear,
Then to my fainting sight appear,

title: I cannot always trace the way
author: Anon

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I cannot always trace the way
Where thou, Almighty One, dost move;
But I can always, always say,
That God is love, that God is love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When fear her chilling mantle flings
O'er earth, my soul to heaven above,
As to her native home, upsprings,
For God is love, for God is love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When mystery clouds my darkened path,
I'll check my dread, my doubts reprove;
In this my soul sweet comfort hath,
That God is love, that God is love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Yes, God is love;—a thought like this
Can every gloomy thought remove,
And turn all tears, all woes, to bliss,
For God is love, for God is love.

title: God is the refuge of his saints
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God is the refuge of his saints,
When storms of sharp distress invade.
Ere we can offer our complaints,
Behold him present with his aid.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let mountains from their seats be hurled
Down to the deep, and buried there;
Convulsions shake the solid world;—
Our faith shall never yield to fear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There is a stream whose gentle flow
Supplies the city of our God;
Life, love, and joy still gliding through,
And watering our divine abode:—

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
That sacred stream, thy holy word,—
That all our raging fear controls:
Sweet peace thy promises afford,
And give new strength to fainting souls.

title: Faith is a living pow'r from heaven
author: Anon.

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Faith is a living pow'r from heaven
Which grasps the promise God has given;
Securely fixed on Christ alone,
A trust that cannot be o'erthrown.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Faith finds in Christ whate'er we need
To save and strengthen, guide and feed;
Strong in his grace, it joys to share
His cross, in hope his crown to wear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Faith to the conscience whispers peace,
And bids the mourner's sighing cease;
By faith the children's right we claim,
And call upon our Father's name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Such faith in us, O God, implant,
And to our prayers thy favor grant;
In Jesus Christ, thy saving Son,
Who is our fount of health alone.

title: My God, my Father, while I stray
author: Charlotte Elliott

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God, my Father, while I stray
Far from my home, in life's rough way,
Oh, teach me from my heart to say,
"Thy will be done!"

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If thou should'st call me to resign
What most I prize—it ne'er was mine—
I only yield thee what was thine—
"Thy will be done!"

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If but my fainting heart be blest
With thy sweet Spirit for its guest,
My God! to thee I leave the rest—
"Thy will be done!"

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Renew my will from day to day;
Blend it with thine, and take away
All that now makes it hard to say,
"Thy will be done!"

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then, when on earth I breathe no more
The pray'r, oft mixed with tears before,
I'll sing upon a happier shore,
"Thy will be done!"

title: Oh! what, if we are Christ's
author: Henry W. Baker

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh! what, if we are Christ's,
Is earthly shame or loss?
Bright shall the crown of glory be
When we have borne the cross.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Keen was the trial once,
Bitter the cup of woe,
When martyred saints, baptized in blood,
Christ's sufferings shared below.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Bright is their glory now,
Boundless their joy above,
Where, on the bosom of their God,
They rest in perfect love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord! may that grace be ours,
Like them, in faith, to bear
All that of sorrow, grief, or pain
May be our portion here.

title: The Lord my Shepherd is
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Lord my Shepherd is;
I shall be well supplied:
Since he is mine, and I am his,
What can I want beside?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He leads me to the place
Where heavenly pasture grows,
Where living waters gently pass,
And full salvation flows.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If e'er I go astray,
He doth my soul reclaim,
And guides me, in his own right way,
For his most holy name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
While he affords his aid,
I cannot yield to fear;
Tho' I should walk thro' death's dark shade,
My Shepherd's with me there.

title: Here I can firmly rest
author: Tr. by Miss C. Winkworth

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Here I can firmly rest;
I dare to boast of this,
That God, the highest and the best,
My Friend and Father is.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Naught have I of my own,
Naught in the life I lead;
What Christ hath given, that alone
I dare in faith to plead.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I rest upon the ground
Of Jesus and his blood;
It is through him that I have found
My soul's eternal good.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
At cost of all I have,
At cost of life and limb,
I cling to God who yet shall save;
I will not turn from him.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
His Spirit in me dwells,
O'er all my mind he reigns;
My care and sadness he dispels,
And soothes away my pains.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
He prospers day by day
His work within my heart,
Till I have strength and faith to say,
Thou, God, my Father art!

title: Guide me, oh thou great Jehovah
author: William Williams

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Open now thy crystal fountain,
Whence the healing streams do flow,
Let the fiery, cloudy pillar,
Lead me all my journey thro';
Strong deliverer,
Be thou still my strength and shield.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Give to the winds thy fears

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Through waves, and clouds, and storms,
He gently clears the way;
Wait thou his time; so shall this night
Soon end in joyous day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
What, though thou rulest not?
Yet heaven, and earth, and hell
Proclaim,—God sitteth on the throne,
And ruleth all things well.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Leave to his sovereign sway
To choose and to command;
So shalt thou wondering own, his way
How wise, how strong his hand!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: Ger., Paul Gerhardt, 1666. Tr. John Wesley, 1739.

title: Oh! for a faith that will not shrink
author: William H. Bathurst

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh! for a faith that will not shrink,
Though pressed by every foe;
That will not tremble on the brink
Of any earthly woe!—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That will not murmur nor complain,
Beneath the chastening rod,
But, in the hour of grief or pain,
Will lean upon its God;—

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A faith that shines more bright and clear
When tempests rage without;
That, when in danger, knows no fear,
In darkness, feels no doubt;—

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A faith that keeps the narrow way
Till life's last hour is fled,
And, with a pure and heavenly ray,
Lights up a dying bed!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord! give us such a faith as this;
And then, whate'er may come,
We'll taste, ev'n here, the hallowed bliss
Of an eternal home.

title: Father! whate'er of earthly bliss
author: Anne Steele

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father! whate'er of earthly bliss
Thy sovereign hand denies,
Accepted at thy throne of grace,
Let this petition rise:—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Give me a calm, a thankful heart,
From every murmur free;
The blessings of thy grace impart,
And let me live to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
"Let the sweet hope that thou art mine
My path of life attend;
Thy presence through my journey shine,
And bless its happy end."

title: Cast thy burden on the Lord
author: Rowland Hill

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Cast thy burden on the Lord,
Only lean upon his word;
Thou wilt soon have cause to bless
His eternal faithfulness.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He sustains thee by his hand,
He enables thee to stand;
Those whom Jesus once hath loved,
From his grace are never moved.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Heaven and earth may pass away,
God's free grace shall not decay;
He hath promised to fulfill
All the pleasure of his will.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus! Guardian of thy flock,
Be thyself our constant Rock;
Make us, by thy powerful hand,
Strong as Zion's mountain stand.

title: In some way or other
author: Mrs. M.A.W. Cook

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In some way or other
The Lord will provide;
It may not be my way,
It may not be thy way,
And yet in his own way,
The Lord will provide.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
At some time or other
The Lord will provide;
It may not be my time,
It may not be thy time,
And yet in his own time,
The Lord will provide.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Despond then no longer,
The Lord will provide;
And this be the token—
No word he hath spoken,
Was ever yet broken,
The Lord will provide.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
March on, then, right boldly
The sea shall divide;
The pathway made glorious
With shoutings victorious,
We'll join in the chorus,
The Lord will provide.

title: Oh, eyes that are weary, and hearts that are sore

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, eyes that are weary, and hearts that are sore!
Look off unto Jesus, now sorrow no more!
The light of his countenance shineth so bright,
That here, as in heaven, there need be no night.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Still looking to Jesus, O, may I be found,
When Jordan's dark waters encompass me round!
They bear me away in his presence to be;
I see him still nearer whom always I see.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then, then shall I know the full beauty and grace
Of Jesus, my Lord, when I stand face to face;
Shall know how his love went before me each day,
And wonder that ever my eyes turned away.

title: How firm a foundation, ye saints of the Lord
author: Geo. Keith

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How firm a foundation, ye saints of the Lord,
Is laid for your faith in his excellent word:
What more can he say than to you he has said,
You who unto Jesus for refuge have fled?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In every condition—in sickness, in health,
In poverty's vale, or abounding in wealth,
At home and abroad, on the land, on the sea—
As your days may demand, so your succor shall be.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
When through the deep waters I cause you to go,
The rivers of sorrow shall not you o'erflow;
For I will be with you, your troubles to bless,
And sanctify to you your deepest distress.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When through fiery trials your pathway shall lie,
My grace, all-sufficient, shall be your supply;
The flame shall not hurt you; I only design
Your dross to consume, and your gold to refine.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
E'en down to old age all my people shall prove
My sovereign, eternal, unchangeable love;
And when hoary hairs shall their temples adorn,
Like lambs they shall still in my bosom be borne.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
The soul that on Jesus hath leaned for repose,
I will not, I cannot desert to his foes;
That soul, though all hell should endeavor to shake,
I'll never, no never, no never forsake.

title: Safe in the arms of Jesus
author: Fanny J. Crosby

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Safe in the arms of Jesus,
Safe on his gentle breast,
There by his love o'ershaded,
Sweetly my soul shall rest.
Hark! 'tis the voice of angels,
Borne in a song to me,
Over the fields of glory,
Over the jasper sea.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Safe in the arms of Jesus,
Safe on his gentle breast,
There by his love o'ershaded,
Sweetly my soul shall rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Safe in the arms of Jesus,
Safe from corroding care,
Safe from the world's temptations
Sin cannot harm me there.
Free from the blight of sorrow,
Free from my doubts and fears;
Only a few more trials,
Only a few more tears!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, my heart's dear refuge,
Jesus has died for me;
Firm on the Rock of Ages
Ever my trust shall be.
Here let me wait with patience,
Wait till the night is o'er;
Wait till I see the morning
Break on the golden shore.

title: He leadeth me! oh! blessed tho't
author: Rev. Jos. H. Gilmore

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
He leadeth me! oh! blessed tho't,
Oh! words with heav'nly comfort fraught;
Whate'er I do, where'er I be,
Still 'tis God's hand that leadeth me.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
He leadeth me! he leadeth me!
By his own hand he leadeth me;
His faithful follower I would be,
For by his hand he leadeth me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sometimes 'mid scenes of deepest gloom,
Sometimes where Eden's bowers bloom,
By waters still, o'er troubled sea—
Still 'tis his hand that leadeth me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, I would clasp thy hand in mine.
Nor ever murmur or repine—
Content, whatever lot I see,
Since 'tis my God that leadeth me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And when my task on earth is done,
When by thy grace, the vict'ry's won,
E'en death's cold wave I will not flee,
Since God thro' Jordan leadeth me.

title: My Jesus, as thou wilt
author: Benjamin Schmolke

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My Jesus, as thou wilt—
O may thy will be mine!
Into thy hand of love
I would my all resign;
Through sorrow, or through joy,
Conduct me as thine own,
And help me still to say,
My Lord, thy will be done!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My Jesus, as thou wilt—
If needy here and poor,
Give me thy people's bread,
Their portion rich and sure;
The manna of thy word,
Let my soul feed upon,
And, if all else should fail,
My Lord, thy will be done!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My Jesus, as thou wilt—
If among thorns I go,
Still sometimes here and there
Let a few roses blow.
But thou, on earth, along
The thorny path hast gone:
Then lead me after thee;
My Lord, thy will be done!

title: I have found repose for my weary soul
author: Rev. H.B. Hartzler

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I have found repose for my weary soul,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior;
And a harbor safe when the billows roll,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior.
I will fear no foe in the deadly strife,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior;
I will bear my lot in the toil of life,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Resting on his mighty arm forever,
Never from his loving heart to sever,
I will rest by grace in his strong embrace,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I will sing my song as the days go by,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior;
And rejoice in hope, while I live or die,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior.
I can smile at grief and abide in pain,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior;
And the loss of all shall be highest gain,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, the peace and joy of the life I live,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior;
Oh, the strength and grace only God can give,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior.
Whosoever will may be saved to-day,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior;
And begin to walk in the holy way,
Trusting in the promise of the Savior.

title: Come, ye disconsolate, where'er ye languish
author: Vs. 3 by Thos. Hastings

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Joy of the desolate, light of the straying,
Hope when all others die, fadeless and pure—
Here speaks the Comforter, in God's name saying,
Earth has no sorrow that heaven cannot cure.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here see the bread of life; see waters flowing
Forth from the throne of God, boundless in love;
Come to the feast prepared, come, ever knowing
Earth has no sorrow but heaven can remove.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text: Vs. 1, 2, by Thomas Moore, 1816.

title: Down in the valley with my Savior I would go
author: W.O. Cushing

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Down in the valley with my Savior I would go,
Where the flowers are blooming and the sweet waters flow;
Ev'rywhere he leads me I would follow, follow on,
Walking in his footsteps till the crown be won.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Follow! follow! I would follow Jesus!
Anywhere, everywhere I would follow on!
Follow! follow! I would follow Jesus!
Ev'rywhere he leads me I will follow on!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Down in the valley with my Savior I would go,
Where the storms are sweeping and the dark waters flow;
With his hand to lead me I will never, never fear,
Dangers cannot frighten me if my Lord is near.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Down in the valley, or upon the mountain steep,
Close beside my Savior would my soul ever keep;
He will lead me safely, in the path that he has trod,
Up to where they gather on the hills of God.

title: Simply trusting ev'ry day
author: E.P. Stites

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Simply trusting ev'ry day,
Trusting thro' a stormy way;
Even when my faith is small,
Trusting Jesus, that is all.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Trusting as the moments fly,
Trusting as the days go by;
Trusting him whate'er befall,
Trusting Jesus, that is all.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Brightly doth his Spirit shine
Into this poor heart of mine;
While he leads I cannot fall,
Trusting Jesus, that is all.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Trusting him while life shall last,
Trusting him till earth is past;
Till within the jasper wall,
Trusting Jesus, that is all.

title: The Lord's our Rock, in him we hide

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Lord's our Rock, in him we hide,
A shelter in the time of storm;
Secure whatever ill betide,
A shelter in the time of storm.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Oh, Jesus is a Rock in a weary land,
A weary land, a weary land,
Oh, Jesus is a Rock in a weary land,
A shelter in the time of storm.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A shade by day, defense by night,
A shelter in the time of storm;
No foes alarm, no fears affright,
A shelter in the time of storm.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The raging storms may round us beat,
A shelter in the time of storm;
We'll never leave our safe retreat,
A shelter in the time of storm.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O Rock divine, O Refuge dear,
A shelter in the time of storm;
Be thou our helper, ever near,
A shelter in the time of storm.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: Anon, Arranged.

title: In God I have found a retreat
author: James Nicholson

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
sections.text:
Oh, what comfort it brings,
As my soul sweetly sings,
I am safe from all danger
While under his wings.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I dread not the terror by night,
No arrow can harm me by day;
His shadow has covered me quite,
My fears he has driven away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The pestilence walking about,
When darkness has settled abroad,
Can never compel me to doubt
The presence and power of God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The wasting destruction at noon
No fearful foreboding can bring;
With Jesus my soul doth commune,
His perfect salvation I sing.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
A thousand may fall at my side,
And ten thousand at my right hand;
Above me his wings are spread wide,
Beneath them in safety I stand.

title: He knows the bitter, weary way
author: Unknown

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
He knows the bitter, weary way,
The endless striving day by day,
The souls that weep, the souls that pray—
He knows it all.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
He knows it all,
The bitter, weary way;
O souls that weep, O souls that pray,
He knows it all.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He knows how hard the fight has been,
The clouds that come our lives between,
The wounds the world has never seen—
He knows it all.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He knows, when, faint and worn, we sink,
How deep the pain, how near the brink
Of dark despair we pause and shrink—
He knows it all.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He knows! oh, thought so full of bliss!
For though on earth our joys we miss.
We still can bear it, feeling this—

title: Cast thy burden on the Lord

sections.label: Verse 1

title: Lead, kindly Light, amid th' encircling gloom
author: Cardinal J.H. Newman

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lead, kindly Light, amid th' encircling gloom,
Lead thou me on,
The night is dark, and I am far from home,
Lead thou me on;
Keep thou my feet; I do not ask to see
The distant scene; one step enough for me.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

title: Oh, weary pilgrim, lift your head
author: M.M. Weinland

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, weary pilgrim, lift your head,
For joy cometh in the morning;
For God, in his own Word, hath said
That joy cometh in the morning.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Joy cometh in the morning,
Joy cometh in the morning;
Weeping may endure for a night,
But joy cometh in the morning.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Ye trembling saints, dismiss your fears,
For joy cometh in the morning;
Oh, weeping mourner, dry your tears,
For joy cometh in the morning.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let ev'ry burdened soul look up,
For joy cometh in the morning;
And ev'ry trembling sinner hope,
For joy cometh in the morning.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Our God shall wipe all tears away,
For joy cometh in the morning;
Sorrow and sighing flee away,
For joy cometh in the morning.

title: How tender is thy hand
author: Thomas Hastings

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How tender is thy hand,
Oh, thou beloved Lord!
Afflictions come at thy command,
And leave us at thy word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How gentle was the rod
That chastened us for sin!
How soon we found a smiling God,
Where deep distress had been!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A Father's hand we felt,
A Father's heart we knew;
With tears of penitence we knelt,
And found his word was true.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We told him all our grief,
We thought of Jesus' love;
A sense of pardon brought relief,
And bade our pains remove.

title: From every stormy wind that blows
author: Hugh Stowell

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From every stormy wind that blows,
From every swelling tide of woes,
There is a calm, a sure retreat;—
'Tis found before the mercy-seat.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There is a place where Jesus sheds
The oil of gladness on our heads,—
A place, than all besides, more sweet;
It is the blood-bought mercy-seat.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There is a spot where spirits blend,
Where friend holds fellowship with friend;
Though sundered far, by faith they meet
Around one common mercy-seat.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There, there, on eagle's wings we soar,
And time, and sense seem all no more;
And heaven comes down our souls to greet,
And glory crowns the mercy-seat!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Oh! may my hand forget her skill,
My tongue be silent, cold, and still,
This bounding heart forget to beat,
If I forget the mercy-seat!

title: Prayer is appointed to convey
author: Joseph Hart. _D._ 1768

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Prayer is appointed to convey
The blessings God designs to give:
Long as they live should Christians pray;
They learn to pray when first they live.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis prayer supports the soul that's weak,
Tho' thought be broken, language lame,
Pray, if thou canst or canst not speak,
But pray with faith in Jesus' name.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: My God, is any hour so sweet
author: Charlotte Elliott

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God, is any hour so sweet
From blush of morn to evening star,
As that which calls me to thy feet,
The calm and holy hour of prayer?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Blest is the tranquil break of morn,
And blest the hush of solemn eve,
When on the wings of prayer up-borne,
This fair, but transient, world I leave.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
No words can tell what sweet relief,
There for my every want I find;
What strength for warfare, balm for grief,
What deep and cheerful peace of mind.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord, till I reach the blissful shore,
No privilege so dear shall be,
As thus my inmost soul to pour
In faithful, filial prayer to thee!

title: Sweet hour of prayer! sweet hour of prayer
author: Rev. W.W. Walford

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet hour of prayer! sweet hour of prayer!
That calls me from a world of care,
And bids me at my Father's throne
Make all my wants and wishes known:
In seasons of distress and grief,
My soul has often found relief;
And oft escaped the tempter's snare,
By thy return, sweet hour of prayer!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sweet hour of prayer! sweet hour of prayer!
Thy wings shall my petition bear
To him whose truth and faithfulness
Engage the waiting soul to bless.
And since he bids he seek his face,
Believe his word, and trust his grace,
I'll cast on him my ev'ry care
And wait for thee, sweet hour of prayer!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sweet hour of prayer! sweet hour of prayer!
May I thy consolation share,
Till, from Mount Pisgah's lofty height,
I view my home and take my flight:
This robe of flesh I'll drop and rise
To seize the everlasting prize;
And shout, while passing thro' the air,
Farewell, farewell, sweet hour of prayer!

title: I love to steal awhile away
author: Mrs. Phoebe H. Brown

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I love to steal awhile away
From ev'ry cumb'ring care,
And spend the hours of setting day
In humble, grateful prayer.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I love in solitude to shed
The penitential tear,
And all his promises to plead,
Where none but God can hear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I love to think on mercies past,
And future good implore,
And all my cares and sorrows cast
On him whom I adore.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I love by faith to take a view
Of brighter scenes in heaven;
The prospect doth my strength renew,
While here by tempests driven.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thus, when life's toilsome day is o'er,
May its departing ray
Be calm as this impressive hour,
And lead to endless day!

title: Lord! teach us how to pray aright
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord! teach us how to pray aright,
With reverence and with fear;
Though dust and ashes in thy sight,
We may, we must draw near.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
God of all grace, we come to thee,
With broken, contrite hearts,
Give, what thine eye delights to see,
Truth in the inward parts;

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Patience, to watch, and wait, and weep,
Though mercy long delay;
Courage, our fainting souls to keep,
And trust thee though thou slay.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Give these, and then—thy will be done—
Thus strengthened with all might,
We by the Spirit and thy Son,
Shall pray, and pray aright.

title: The Savior bids thee watch and pray
author: T. Hastings

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Savior bids thee watch and pray
Through life's momentous hour;
And grants the Spirit's quickening ray
To those who seek his power.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
The Savior bids thee watch and pray,
For soon the hour will come
That calls thee from the earth away
To thy eternal home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The Savior bids thee watch and pray
Oh, hearken to his voice,
And follow where he leads the way,
To heaven's eternal joys.

title: Prayer is the soul's sincere desire
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
Uttered or unexpressed;
The motion of a hidden fire,
That trembles in the breast.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Prayer is the burden of a sigh,
The falling of a tear,
The upward glancing of an eye,
When none but God is near.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Prayer is the simplest form of speech,
That infant lips can try;
Prayer, the sublimest strains that reach
The Majesty on high.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Prayer is the Christian's vital breath,
The Christian's native air:
His watchword at the gates of death;
He enters heaven with prayer.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Oh, Thou, by whom we come to God,—
The Life, the Truth, the Way!
The path of prayer thyself hast trod;
Lord! teach us how to pray.

title: A throne of grace! then let us go
author: Corbin

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A throne of grace! then let us go
And offer up our prayer;
A gracious God will mercy show
To all that worship there.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A throne of grace! oh, at that throne
Our knees have often bent,
And God has showered his blessings down
As often as we went.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A throne of grace! rejoice, ye saints!
That throne is open still;
To God unbosom your complaints,
And then inquire his will.

title: Talk with us, Lord, thyself reveal
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Talk with us, Lord, thyself reveal,
While here o'er earth we rove;
Speak to our hearts, and let us feel
The kindling of thy love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With thee conversing, we forget
All time, and toil, and care:
Labor is rest, and pain is sweet,
If thou, my God! art here.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here, then, my God, vouchsafe to stay,
And bid my heart rejoice:
My bounding heart shall own thy sway,
And echo to thy voice.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou callest me to seek thy face—
'Tis all I wish to seek;
T' attend the whisperings of thy grace,
And hear thee only speak.

title: Come, my soul! thy suit prepare
author: John Newton

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou art coming to a King,
Large petitions with thee bring;
For his grace and power are such,
None can ever ask too much.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord! I come to thee for rest,
Take possession of my breast;
There thy blood-bought right maintain,
And without a rival reign.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
While I am a pilgrim here,
Let thy love my spirit cheer;
As my Guide, my Guard, my Friend,
Lead me to my journey's end.

title: What a friend we have in Jesus
author: Unknown

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What a friend we have in Jesus,
All our sins and griefs to bear;
What a privilege to carry
Ev'rything to God in prayer!
O what peace we often forfeit,
O what needless pain we bear,
All because we do not carry
Ev'rything to God in prayer!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Have we trials and temptations?
Is there trouble anywhere?
We should never be discouraged,
Take it to the Lord in prayer.
Can we find a friend so faithful,
Who will all our sorrows share?
Jesus knows our ev'ry weakness,
Take it to the Lord in prayer!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Are we weak and heavy laden,
Cumbered with a load of care?—
Precious Savior, still our refuge,—
Take it to the Lord in prayer.
Do thy friends despise, forsake thee?
Take it to the Lord in prayer;
In his firms he'll take and shield thee,
Thou wilt find a solace there.

title: Our Father who art in heaven, | Hallowed | be thy | name, ||

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our Father who art in heaven, | Hallowed | be thy | name, ||
Thy kingdom come; thy will be done in | earth, as it | is in | heaven,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Give us this | day our | daily bread, ||
And forgive us our debts, as | we for- | give our | debtors.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lead us not into temptation, but de- | liver | us from | evil; ||
For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for | ever. | A- | men.

title: Come at the morning hour
author: Anon

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come at the morning hour,
Come, let us kneel and pray;
Pray'r is the Christian pilgrim's staff
To walk with God all day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
At noon beneath the Rock
Of Ages, rest and pray;
Sweet is that shelter from the sun
In weary heat of day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
At evening, in thy home,
Around its altar, pray;
And finding there the house of God,
With heaven then close the day.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When midnight veils our eyes,
Oh, it is sweet to say,
I sleep, but my heart waketh, Lord!
With thee to watch and pray.

title: Behold the throne of grace
author: John Newton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold the throne of grace!
The promise calls me near;
There Jesus shows a smiling face,
And waits to answer prayer.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That rich atoning blood,
Which sprinkled round I see,
Provides, for those who come to God,
An all-prevailing plea.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Thine, image, Lord! bestow,
Thy presence and thy love;
I ask to serve thee here below,
And reign with thee above.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Are you weary, are you heavy-hearted

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Are you weary, are you heavy-hearted?
Tell it to Jesus.
Are you grieving over joys departed?
Tell it to Jesus alone.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Tell it to Jesus, tell it to Jesus,
He is a Friend that's well known;
You have no other such a friend or brother!
Tell it to Jesus alone.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Do the tears flow down your cheeks unbidden?
Tell it to Jesus.
Have you sins that to man's eye are hidden?
Tell it to Jesus alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Do you fear the gath'ring clouds of sorrow?
Tell it to Jesus.
Are you anxious what shall be to-morrow?
Tell it to Jesus alone.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Are you troubled at the tho't of dying?
Tell it to Jesus.
For Christ's coming kingdom are you sighing?
Tell it to Jesus alone.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: J. E. Rankin, D. D.

title: Must Jesus bear the cross alone
author: V. 1. Thomas Shepherd

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Must Jesus bear the cross alone,
And all the world go free?
No, there's a cross for every one,
And there's a cross for me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How happy are the saints above,
Who once went mourning here!
But now they taste unmingled love,
And joy without a tear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
This consecrated cross I'll bear,
Till death shall set me free,
And then go home my crown to wear,
For there's a crown for me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Upon the crystal pavement, down
At Jesus' pierced feet,
Joyful, I'll cast my golden crown,
And his dear name repeat.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And palms shall wave, and harps shall ring
Beneath heaven's arches high;
The Lord, that lives, the ransomed sing,
That lives no more to die.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Oh! precious cross! oh! glorious crown!
Oh! resurrection day!
Ye angels! from the skies come down,
And bear my soul away.

title: Awake, my soul—stretch every nerve
author: P. Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Awake, my soul—stretch every nerve,
And press with vigor on;
A heavenly race demands thy zeal,
A bright, immortal crown.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis God's all-animating voice
That calls thee from on high:
'Tis his own hand presents the prize
To thine aspiring eye.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A cloud of witnesses around,
Hold thee in full survey:
Forget the steps already trod,
And onward urge thy way.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blest Savior, introduced by thee
Have we our race begun;
And, crowned with vict'ry, at thy feet
We'll lay our laurels down.

title: Blest is the man, whose softening heart
author: Mrs. Anna L. Barbauld

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest is the man, whose softening heart
Feels all another's pain;
To whom the supplicating eye
Was never raised in vain;—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Whose breast expands with generous warmth,
A stranger's woes to feel,
And bleeds in pity o'er the wound
He wants the power to heal.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He spreads his kind supporting arms
To every child of grief;
Hie secret bounty largely flows,
And brings unasked relief.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To gentle offices of love,
His feet are never slow;
He views, through mercy's melting eye,
A brother in a foe.

title: A charge to keep I have
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A charge to keep I have,
A God to glorify;
A never-dying-soul to save,
And fit it for the sky:—-

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To serve the present age,
My calling to fulfill,—
Oh! may it all my powers engage—
To do my Master's will.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Arm me with jealous care,
As in thy sight to live;
And, oh, thy servant, Lord! prepare
A strict account to give.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Help me to watch and pray,
And on thyself rely;
Assured, if I my trust betray,
I shall forever die.

title: Sow in the morn thy seed
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
And duly shall appear,
In verdure, beauty, strength,
The tender blade, the stalk, the ear,
And the full corn at length.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou canst not toil in vain;
Cold, heat, and moist, and dry,
Shall foster and mature the grain,
For garners in the sky.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thence, when the glorious end,
The day of God, shall come,
The angel-reapers shall descend,
And heaven cry "Harvest-home!"

title: We give thee but thine own
author: William Walsham How

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We give thee but thine own,
Whate'er the gift may be:
All that we have is thine alone,
A trust, O Lord! from thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, hearts are bruised and dead,
And homes are bare and cold,
And lambs, for whom the Shepherd bled,
Are straying from the fold.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To comfort and to bless,
To find a balm for woe,
To tend the lone and fatherless
Is angels' work below.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The captive to release,
To God the lost to bring,
To teach the way of life and peace,
It is a Christ-like thing.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And we believe thy word,
Though dim our faith may be:
Whate'er for thine we do, O Lord,
We do it unto thee.

title: Go, labor on; spend, and be spent
author: Horatius Bonar

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Go, labor on; enough, while here,
If he shall praise thee, if he deign
Thy willing heart to mark and cheer,
No toil for him shall be in vain.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: So let our lips and lives express
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
So let our lips and lives express
The holy gospel we profess;
So let our works and virtues shine
To prove the doctrine all divine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thus shall we best proclaim abroad
The honors of our Savior God;
When his salvation reigns within,
And grace subdues the power of sin.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Religion bears our spirits up,
While we expect that blessed hope,—
The bright appearance of the Lord;
And faith stands leaning on his word.

title: We are living, we are dwelling
author: Bp. Arthur Cleveland Coxe

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We are living, we are dwelling,
In a grand and awful time,
In an age on ages telling;
To be living is sublime.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hark the onset! will ye fold your
Faith-clad arms in lazy lock?
Up! O up! thou drowsy soldier;
Worlds are charging to the shock.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
On! let all the soul within you
For the truth's sake go abroad;
Strike! let ev'ry nerve and sinew
Tell on ages—tell for God.

title: Go, labor on, while it is day
author: H. Bonar

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Men die in darkness at your side,
Without a hope to cheer the tomb;
Take up the torch and wave it wide—
The torch that lights time's thickest gloom.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Blest is the man whose heart doth move
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest is the man whose heart doth move,
And melt with pity to the poor;
Whose soul, by sympathizing love,
Feels what his fellow-saints endure.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
His heart contrives, for their relief,
More good than his own hands can do;
He, in the time of general grief,
Shall find the Lord has pity too.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His soul shall live secure on earth,
With secret blessings on his head,
When drought, and pestilence, and dearth
Around him multiply their dead.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Or, if he languish on his couch,
God will pronounce his sins forgiven,
Will save him with a healing touch,
Or take his willing soul to heaven.

title: Rescue the perishing
author: Fanny J. Crosby

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rescue the perishing,
Care for the dying,
Snatch them in pity from sin and the grave;
Weep o'er the erring one,
Lift up the fallen,
Tell them of Jesus, the mighty to save.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Rescue the perishing,
Care for the dying;
Jesus is merciful,
Jesus will save.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Tho' they are slighting him,
Still he is waiting,
Waiting the penitent child to receive.
Plead with them earnestly,
Plead with them gently,
He will forgive if they only believe.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Down in the human heart,
Crushed by the tempter,
Feelings lie buried which grace can restore.
Touched by a loving heart,
Wakened by kindness,
Cords that were broken will vibrate once more.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: There are lonely hearts to cherish
author: George Cooper

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There are lonely hearts to cherish,
While the days are going by;
There are weary souls who perish,
While the days are going by;
If a smile we can renew,
As our journey we pursue,
Oh, the good we all may do,
While the days are going by.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Going by, going by,
Going by, going by,
Oh, the good we all may do,
While the days are going by.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
All the loving links that bind us,
While the days are going by;
One by one we leave behind us,
While the days are going by;
But the seeds of good we sow
Both in shade and shine will grow,
And will keep our hearts aglow,
While the days are going by.

title: I want to be a worker for the Lord
author: Isaiah Baltzell

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I want to be a worker for the Lord,
I want to love and trust his holy word;
I want to sing and pray, and be busy ev'ry day
In the vineyard of the Lord.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I will work, I will pray,
In the vineyard, in the vineyard of the Lord;
I will work, I will pray, I will labor ev'ry day
In the vineyard of the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I want to be a worker ev'ry day,
I want to lead the erring in the way
That leads to heav'n above, where all is peace and love,
In the kingdom of the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I want to be a worker strong and brave,
I want to trust in Jesus' power to save;
All who will truly come, shall find a happy home
In the kingdom of the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I want to be a worker; help me, Lord,
To lead the lost and erring to thy word
That points to joys on high, where pleasures never die,
In the kingdom of the Lord.

title: Oh, scatter seeds of loving deeds
author: Jessie H. Brown

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, scatter seeds of loving deeds,
Along the fertile field,
For grain will grow from what you sow,
And fruitful harvest yield.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Then day by day along your way,
The seeds of promise cast,
That ripened grain from hill and plain,
Be gathered home at last.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Tho' sown in tears the weary years,
The seed will surely live;
Tho' great the cost it is not lost,
For God will fruitage give.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The harvest home of God will come;
And after toil and care,
With joy untold your sheaves of gold
Will all be garnered there.

title: Come, we that love the Lord
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, we that love the Lord,
And let our joys be known,
Join in a song with sweet accord,
And thus surround the throne.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
We're marching to Zion,
Beautiful, beautiful Zion,
We're marching upward to Zion,
The beautiful city of God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let those refuse to sing
Who never knew our God;
But children of the heavenly King
May speak their joys abroad.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The hill of Zion yields
A thousand sacred sweets,
Before we reach the heavenly fields,
Or walk the golden streets.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then let our songs abound,
And ev'ry tear be dry;
We're marching thro' Immanuel's ground
To fairer worlds on high.

title: Work, for the night is coming
author: Annie L. Walker

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3

title: Sowing in the morning, sowing seeds of kindness
author: Knowles Shaw

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sowing in the morning, sowing seeds of kindness,
Sowing in the noontide and the dewy eve;
Waiting for the harvest, and the time of reaping,
We shall come, rejoicing, bringing in the sheaves.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Bringing in the sheaves, bringing in the sheaves,
We shall come, rejoicing, bringing in the sheaves;
Bringing in the sheaves, bringing in the sheaves,
We shall come, rejoicing, bringing in the sheaves.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sowing in the sunshine, sowing in the shadows,
Fearing neither clouds nor winter's chilling breeze;
By and by the harvest and the labor ended,
We shall come, rejoicing, bringing in the sheaves.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Light after darkness
author: Frances R. Havergal

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Light after darkness,
Gain after loss,
Strength after weariness,
Crown after cross,
Sweet after bitter,
Song after sigh,
Home after wandering,
Praise after cry.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Now comes the weeping,
Then the glad reaping;
Now comes the labor hard,
Then the reward.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sheaves after sowing,
Sun after rain,
Sight after mystery,
Peace after pain,
Joy after sorrow,
Calm after blast,
Rest after weariness,
Sweet rest at last.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Near after distant,
Gleam after gloom,
Love after loneliness,
Life after tomb.
After long agony,
Rapture of bliss;
Right was the pathway
Leading to this.

title: I love to tell the story
author: Miss Kate Hankey

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I love to tell the story
Of unseen things above,
Of Jesus and his glory,
Of Jesus and his love!
I love to tell the story,
Because I know it's true;
It satisfies my longings,
As nothing else would do.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I love to tell the story!
'Twill be my theme in glory,
To tell the old, old story
Of Jesus and his love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I love to tell the story!
More wonderful it seems,
Than all the golden fancies
Of all our golden dreams.
I love to tell the story!
It did so much for me!
And that is just the reason,
I tell it now to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I love to tell the story!
'Tis pleasant to repeat
What seems, each time, I tell it,
More wonderfully sweet.
I love to tell the story!
For some have never heard
The message of salvation
From God's own Holy Word.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I love to tell the story!
For those who know it best
Seem hungering and thirsting
To hear it like the rest.
And when, in scenes of glory,
I sing the new, new song,
'Twill be—the old, old story
That I have loved so long.

title: Only a word for Jesus
author: E. S. Lorenz

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Only a word for Jesus,
Spoken in fear with sense of need;
Yet, with the Master's blessing,
Thousands that word may feed.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Give me a word for thee, Master!
Give me a word for thee!
To speak thy praise,
Some soul to raise,
Oh, give me a word for thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Only a word for Jesus,
Gentle and low with falt'ring breath;
Yet, with the Spirit's thrilling,
Winning a soul from death.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Only a word for Jesus,
Only a wav'ring soul to hear;
Yet, thro' increasing ages,
Widen its help and cheer.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Only a word for Jesus,
Feeble the love and praise appear:
Angels their songs are ceasing,
Glad this new note to hear.

title: Are you Christ's light bearer
author: Priscilla J. Owens

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Are you Christ's light bearer?
Of his joy a sharer?
Is this dark world fairer
For your cheering ray?
Is your beacon lighted,
Guiding souls benighted
To the land of perfect day?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Oh, brother, is your lamp trimmed and burning?
Is the world made brighter by its cheering ray?
Are you ever waiting
For your Lord's returning?
Are you watching day by day?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Is your heart warm glowing,
With his love o'erflowing,
And his goodness showing
More and more each day?
Are you pressing onward,
With Christ's faithful vanguard,
In the safe and narrow way?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Keep your altars burning,
Wait your Lord's returning,
While your heart's deep yearning
Draws him ever near;
With his radiance splendid
Shall your light be blended
When his glory shall appear?

title: When Jesus comes to reward his servants
author: Fanny J. Crosby

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When Jesus comes to reward his servants,
Whether it be noon or night,
Faithful to him will he find us watching,
With our lamps all trimmed and bright?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Oh, can we say we are ready, brother?
Ready for the soul's bright home?
Say, will he find you and me still watching,
Waiting, waiting when the Lord shall come?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If at the dawn of the early morning,
He shall call us one by one,
When to the Lord we restore our talents,
Will he answer thee—Well done?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Have we been true to the trust he left us?
Do we seek to do our best?
If in our hearts there is naught condemns us,
We shall have a glorious rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blessed are those whom the Lord finds watching,
In his glory they shall share;
If he shall come at the dawn or midnight,
Will he find us watching there?

title: My soul, be on thy guard
author: George Heath

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My soul, be on thy guard,
Ten thousand foes arise:
The hosts of sin are pressing hard
To draw thee from the skies.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Ne'er think the vict'ry won
Nor lay thine armor down;
Thy arduous work will not be done
Till thou obtain thy crown.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Fight on, my soul, till death
Shall bring thee to thy God;
He'll take thee, at thy parting breath,
To his divine abode.

title: Soldiers of Christ! arise
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Soldiers of Christ! arise,
And put your armor on,—
Strong, in the strength which God supplies,
Through his eternal Son:—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Strong, in the Lord of hosts,
And in his mighty power;
Who in the strength of Jesus trusts,
Is more than conqueror.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Stand, then, in his great might,
With all his strength endued;
And take, to arm you for the fight,
The panoply of God:—

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
That, having all things done,
And all your conflicts past,
You may o'ercome through Christ alone,
And stand entire at last.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Still let the Spirit cry,
In all his soldiers, "Come,"
Till Christ, the Lord, descends from high,
And takes the conquerors home.

title: Arise, ye saints, arise
author: Thomas Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Arise, ye saints, arise!
The Lord our Leader is:
The foe before his banner flies,
And victory is his.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We soon shall see the day
When all our toils shall cease;
When we shall cast our arms away,
And dwell in endless peace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
This hope supports us here;
It makes our burdens light:
'Twill serve our drooping hearts to cheer,
Till faith shall end in sight:—

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Till, of the prize possessed,
We hear of war no more;
And ever with our Leader rest,
On yonder peaceful shore.

title: Am I a soldier of the cross
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Am I a soldier of the cross,
A follower of the Lamb?
And shall I fear to own his cause,
Or blush to speak his name?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Must I be carried to the skies
On flow'ry beds of ease,
While others fought to win the prize,
And sailed thro' bloody seas?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Are there no foes for me to face?
Must I not stem the flood?
Is this vile world a friend to grace,
To help me on to God?

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Thy saints in all this glorious war,
Shall conquer, though they die;
They see the triumph from afar,
By faith they bring it nigh.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
When that illustrious day shall rise,
And all thy armies shine
In robes of vict'ry through the skies,
The glory shall be thine.

title: Soldiers of Christ are we

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Soldiers of Christ are we
Marching to victory,
Marching to heaven;
In his bright armor dressed,
His cross our chosen crest,
And for our food and rest,
His word is given.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Tho' foes our path surround,
Tho' toils and cares abound,
Onward we tread;
We hear our Lord's command;
We grasp each shining brand,
And, like a banner grand,
Hope waves o'erhead.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Soldiers of Christ are we,
Light, Love, and Liberty
Our battle call!
Till truth shall win the day,
Till right shall gain the sway,
Till sin is driven away,
We fight or fall.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Stand up, stand up for Jesus,
Ye soldiers of the cross!
Lift high his royal banner,
It must not suffer loss;
From victory unto victory
His army shall he lead,
Till every foe is vanquished.
And Christ is Lord indeed.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5

title: God is my strong salvation
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God is my strong salvation;
What foe have I to fear?
In darkness and temptation,
My Light, my Help is near:
Though hosts encamp around me,
Firm to the fight I stand;
What terror can confound me,
With God at my right hand?

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Yield not to temptation
author: H.R. Palmer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Yield not to temptation,
For yielding is sin;
Each vict'ry will help you
Some other to win.
Fight manfully onward,
Dark passions subdue;
Look ever to Jesus,
He'll carry you through.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Ask the Savior to help you,
Comfort, strengthen, and keep you;
He is willing to aid you,
He will carry you through.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Shun evil companions,
Bad language disdain,
God's name hold in rev'rence,
Nor take it in vain;
Be thoughtful and earnest,
Kind-hearted and true;
Look ever to Jesus,
He'll carry you through.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: With stately towers and bulwarks strong
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With stately towers and bulwarks strong,
Unrivaled and alone,
Loved theme of many a sacred song;
God's holy city shone.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thus fair was Zion's chosen seat,
The glory of all lands;
Yet fairer and in strength complete,
The Christian temple stands.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The faithful of each clime and age
This glorious church compose;
Built on a Rock, with idle rage
The threat'ning tempest blows.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Fear not; though hostile bands alarm,
Thy God is thy defense;
And weak and powerless every arm
Against Omnipotence.

title: Oh! where are kings and empires now
author: Arthur Cleveland Coxe

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh! where are kings and empires now,
Of old that went and came?
But, Lord! thy church is praying yet,
A thousand years the same.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We mark her goodly battlements,
And her foundations strong;
We hear within the solemn voice
Of her unending song.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For, not like kingdoms of the world,
Thy holy church, O God!
Though earthquake shocks are threatening her,
And tempests are abroad;

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Unshaken as eternal hills,
Immovable she stands,
A mountain that shall fill the earth,
A house not made by hands.

title: Daughter of Zion, from the dust
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Daughter of Zion, from the dust
Exalt thy fallen head;
Again in thy Redeemer trust—
He calls thee from the dead.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Awake, awake, put on thy strength,
Thy beautiful array;
The day of freedom dawns at length—
The Lord's appointed day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Rebuild thy walls, thy bounds enlarge,
And send thy heralds forth;
Say to the South, Give up thy charge!
And, Keep not back, O North!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
