They come, they come; thine exiled bands,
Where'er they rest or roam,
Have heard thy voice in distant lands,
And hasten to their home.

title: Church of the ever-living God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Church of the ever-living God,
The Father's gracious choice,
Amid the voices of this earth
How feeble is thy voice!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Not many rich or noble called,
Not many great or wise:
They whom God makes his kings and priests
Are poor in human eyes.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But the chief Shepherd comes at length;
Their feeble days are o'er,
No more a handful in the earth,
A little flock no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text: H. Bonar, ab.

title: I love thy kingdom, Lord
author: Timothy Dwight

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I love thy kingdom, Lord!
The house of thine abode,
The church our blest Redeemer saved,
With his own precious blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I love thy church, O God!
Her walls before thee stand,
Dear as the apple of thine eye,
And graven on thy hand.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For her my tears shall fall,
For her my prayers ascend;
To her my cares and toils be given,
Till toils and cares shall end.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Beyond my highest joy
I prize her heavenly ways,
Her sweet communion, solemn vows,
Her hymns of love and praise.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Sure as thy truth shall last,
To Zion shall be given
The brightest glories earth can yield,
And brighter bliss of heaven.

title: Revive thy work, O Lord
author: Albert Midlane

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Revive thy work, O Lord!
Thy mighty arm make bare;
Speak, with the voice that wakes the dead,
And make thy people hear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Revive thy work, O Lord!
Disturb this sleep of death;
Quicken the smoldering embers now,
By thine almighty breath.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Revive thy work, O Lord!
Exalt thy precious name;
And, by the Holy Ghost, our love
For thee and thine inflame.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Revive thy work, O Lord!
And give refreshing showers;
The glory shall be all thine own,
The blessing, Lord! be ours.

title: Jesus shall reign where'er the sun
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus shall reign where'er the sun
Does his successive journeys run;
His kingdom spread from shore to shore,
Till moons shall wax and wane no more.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
From north to south the princes meet,
To pay their homage at his feet;
While western empires own their Lord,
And savage tribes attend his word.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To him shall endless prayer be made,
And endless praises crown his head;
His name, like sweet perfume, shall rise,
With every morning sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
People and realms of every tongue
Dwell on his love with sweetest song,
And infant voices shall proclaim
Their early blessings on his name.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Let every creature rise and bring
Peculiar honors to our King;
Angels descend with songs again,
And earth repeat the loud Amen!

title: Triumphant Zion! lift thy head
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Triumphant Zion! lift thy head
From dust, and darkness, and the dead;
Though humbled long, awake at length,
And gird thee with thy Savior's strength.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Put all thy beauteous garments on,
And let thy various charms be known;
The world thy glories shall confess,
Decked in the robes of righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
No more shall foes unclean invade,
And fill thy hallowed walls with dread;
No more shall hell's insulting host
Their vict'ry and thy sorrows boast.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Soon may the last glad song arise
author: Mrs. Voke

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Soon may the last glad song arise
Through all the millions of the skies—
That song of triumph which records
That all the earth is now the Lord's!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let thrones and powers and kingdoms be
Obedient, mighty God, to thee!
And, over land and stream and main,
Wave thou the scepter of thy reign!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, let that glorious anthem swell,
Let host to host the triumph tell,
That not one rebel heart remains,
But over all the Savior reigns!

title: Zion stands with hills surrounded
author: Thomas Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Zion stands with hills surrounded,
Zion kept by power divine!
All her foes shall be confounded,
Tho' the world in arms combine.
Happy Zion,
What a favored lot is thine!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Ev'ry human tie may perish,
Friend to friend unfaithful prove,
Mothers cease their own to cherish,
Heaven and earth at last remove;
But no changes
Can attend Jehovah's love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In the furnace God may prove thee,
Thence to bring thee forth more bright,
But can never cease to love thee—
Thou art precious in his sight:
God is with thee—
God, thine everlasting light.

title: On the mountain's top appearing
author: Thomas Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
On the mountain's top appearing,
Lo! the sacred herald stands,
Welcome news to Zion bearing—
Zion long in hostile lands:
Mourning captive!
God himself shall loose thy bands.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Has thy night been long and mournful?
Have thy friends unfaithful proved?
Have thy foes been proud and scornful?
By thy sighs and tears unmoved?
Cease thy mourning;
Zion still is well beloved.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Savior, visit thy plantation
author: John Newton

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Keep no longer at a distance;
Shine upon us from on high,
Lest, for want of thine assistance,
Every plant should droop and die.
Lord, revive us!
All our help must come from thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let our mutual love be fervent!
Make us prevalent in prayers;
Let each one, esteemed thy servant,
Shun the world's bewitching snares.
Lord, revive us!
All our help must come from thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Break the tempter's fatal power,
Turn the stony heart to flesh,
And begin, from this good hour,
To revive thy work afresh.
Lord, revive us!
All our help must come from thee.

title: Glorious things of thee are spoken
author: John Newton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Glorious things of thee are spoken,
Zion, city of our God!
He, whose word cannot be broken,
Formed thee for his own abode;
On the Rock of Ages founded,
What can shake thy sure repose?
With salvation's walls surrounded,
Thou mayest smile at all thy foes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
See! the streams of living waters,
Springing from eternal love,
Well supply thy sons and daughters,
And all fear of want remove;
Who can faint, while such a river,
Ever flows their thirst t' assuage?—
Grace, which, like the Lord, the Giver,
Never fails from age to age.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Round each habitation hovering,
See the cloud and tire appear,
For a glory and a covering,
Showing that the Lord is near!
Thus deriving from their banner,
Light by night, and shade by day,
Safe they feed upon the manna
Which he gives them when they pray.

title: Zion, dreary and in anguish
author: Thos. Hastings

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Zion, dreary and in anguish,
'Mid the desert hast thou strayed!
Oh, thou weary, cease to languish;
Jesus shall lift up thy head.
Still lamenting and bemoaning,
'Mid thy follies and thy woes!
Soon repenting and returning,
All thy solitude shall close.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Onward, onward, men of heaven
author: Mrs. Lydia H. Sigourney

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Onward, onward, men of heaven
Bear the gospel's banner high;
Rest not, till its light is given,
Star of every pagan sky:
Send it where the pilgrim stranger
Paints beneath the torrid ray;
Bid the red-browed forest-ranger
Hail it, ere he fades away.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Rude in speech, or grim in feature,
Dark in spirit, though they be,
Show that light to every creature—
Prince or vassal, bond or free:
Lo! they haste to every nation:
Host on host the ranks supply:
Onward! Christ is your salvation,
And your death is victory.

title: The heathen perish; day by day
author: J. Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The heathen perish; day by day,
Thousands on thousands pass away!
O Christians, to their rescue fly,
Preach Jesus to them ere they die!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Wealth, labor, talents freely give,
Yea, life itself, that they may live,
What hath your Savior done for you?
And what for him will ye not do?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, Spirit of the Lord! go forth,
Call in the South, wake up the North,
From every clime, from sun to sun,
Gather God's children into one!

title: Look from thy sphere of endless day
author: William C. Bryant

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Look from thy sphere of endless day,
O God of mercy and of might!
In pity look on those who stray,
Benighted, in this land of light.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In peopled vale, in lonely glen,
In crowded mart, by stream or sea,
How many of the sons of men
Hear not the message sent from thee!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Send forth thy heralds, Lord! to call
The thoughtless young, the hardened old,
A scattered, homeless flock, till all
Be gathered to thy peaceful fold.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Send them thy mighty word to speak,
Till faith shall dawn, and doubt depart,
To awe the bold, to stay the weak,
And bind and heal the broken heart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then all these wastes, a dreary scene,
That make us sadden as we gaze,
Shall grow with living waters green,
And lift to heaven the voice of praise.

title: Go, messenger of peace and love
author: A. Balfor

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Go, messenger of peace and love,
To people plunged in shades of night,
Like angels sent from fields above,
Be thine to shed celestial light.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Go to the hungry—food impart;
To paths of peace the wand'rer guide,
And lead the thirsty, panting heart,
Where streams of living water glide.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, faint not in the day of toil,
When harvest waits the reaper's hand:
Go, gather in the glorious spoil,
And joyous in his presence stand.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy love a rich reward shall find
From him who sits enthroned on high:
For they who turn the erring mind
Shall shine like stars above the sky.

title: Ascend thy throne, almighty King
author: Benjamin Beddome

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ascend thy throne, almighty King,
And spread thy glories all abroad;
Let thine own arm salvation bring,
And be thou known the gracious God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let millions bow before thy seat,
Let humble mourners seek thy face,
Bring daring rebels to thy feet,
Subdued by thy victorious grace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, let the kingdoms of the world
Become the kingdoms of the Lord!
Let saints and angels praise thy name,
Be thou through heaven and earth adored.

title: Arm of the Lord! awake, awake
author: William Shrubsole

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Say to the heathen, from thy throne,
"I am Jehovah—God alone!"
Thy voice their idols shall confound,
And cast their altars to the ground.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
No more let human blood be spilt,
Vain sacrifice for human guilt;
But to each conscience be applied
The blood, that flowed from Jesus' side.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Almighty God! thy grace proclaim
In every clime, of every name,
Till adverse powers before thee fall,
And crown the Savior—Lord of all.

title: Behold, the heathen waits to know
author: Voke

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold, the heathen waits to know
The joy the gospel will bestow;
The exiled captive to receive
The freedom Jesus has to give.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Come, let us, with a grateful heart,
In this blest labor share a part;
Our prayers and offerings gladly bring
To aid the triumphs of our King.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Our hearts exult in songs of praise,
That we have seen these latter days,
When our Redeemer shall be known
Where Satan long has held his throne.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Where'er his hand hath spread the skies,
Sweet incense to his name shall rise,
And slave and freeman, Greek and Jew,
By sovereign grace be formed anew.

title: Fling out the banner! let it float
author: George W. Doane

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Fling out the banner! let it float
Skyward and seaward, high and wide,
The sun that lights its shining folds,
The cross on which the Savior died.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Fling out the banner! angels bend
In anxious silence o'er the sign,
And vainly seek to comprehend
The wonder of the love divine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Fling out the banner! heathen lands
Shall see from far the glorious sight;
And nations, crowding to be born,
Baptize their spirits in its light.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Fling out the banner! sin-sick souls,
That sink and perish in the strife,
Shall touch in faith its radiant hem,
And spring immortal, into life.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Fling out the banner! let it float
Skyward and seaward, high and wide
Our glory, only in the cross,
Our only hope, the Crucified.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Yes, we trust the day is breaking
author: Thomas Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
While the foe becomes more daring,
While he enters like a flood
God, the Savior, is preparing
Means to spread his truth abroad,
Ev'ry language
Soon shall tell the love of God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, 'tis pleasant, 'tis reviving
To our hearts, to hear, each day,
Joyful news, from far arriving,
How the gospel wins its way,
Those enlight'ning
Who in death and darkness lay.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Great God! whose universal sway
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The heathen lands, that lie beneath
The shades of over-spreading death,
Revive at his first dawning light,
And deserts blossom at the sight.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The saints shall flourish in his days,
Dressed in the robes of joy and praise;
Peace, like a river, from his throne,
Shall flow to nations yet unknown.

title: From Greenland's icy mountains
author: Reginald Heber

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From Greenland's icy mountains,
From India's coral strand—
Where Afric's sunny fountains
Roll down their golden sand—
From many an ancient river,
From many a palmy plain—
They call us to deliver
Their land from error's chain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Shall we, whose souls are lighted
By wisdom from on high,
Shall we to man benighted
The light of life deny?
Salvation! oh, salvation!
The joyful sound proclaim,
Till earth's remotest nation
Has learned Messiah's name.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Waft, waft, ye winds, his story,
And you, ye waters, roll,
Till like a sea of glory
It spreads from pole to pole,
Till o'er our ransomed nature
The Lamb, for sinners slain,
Redeemer, King, Creator,
In bliss returns to reign.

title: Our country's voice is pleading
author: Mrs. G.W. Anderson

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our country's voice is pleading,
Ye men of God, arise!
His providence is leading,
The land before you lies;
Day gleams are o'er it brightening,
And promise clothes the soil;
Wide fields for harvest whitening,
Invite the reaper's toil.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Go where the waves are breaking
On California's shore,
Christ's precious gospel taking,
More rich than golden ore;
On Allegheny's mountains,
Through all the western vale,
Beside Missouri's fountains,
Rehearse the wondrous tale.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The love of Christ unfolding,
Speed on from east to west,
Till all, his cross beholding,
In him are fully blest.
Great Author of salvation,
Haste, haste the glorious day,
When we, a ransomed nation,
Thy scepter shall obey.

title: The morning light is breaking
author: Samuel F. Smith

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The morning light is breaking,
The darkness disappears:
The sons of earth are waking
To penitential tears.
Each breeze that sweeps the ocean
Brings tidings from afar
Of nations in commotion,
Prepared for Zion's war.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Rich dews of grace come o'er us,
In many a gentle shower,
And brighter scenes before us
Are opening every hour;
Each cry, to heaven going,
Abundant answers brings,
And heavenly gales are blowing,
With peace upon their wings.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
See heathen nations bending
Before the God we love,
And thousand hearts ascending
In gratitude above;
While sinners, now confessing,
The gospel call obey,
And seek the Savior's blessing,—
A nation in a day.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blest river of salvation!
Pursue thine onward way;
Flow thou to every nation,
Nor in thy richness stay:—
Stay not, till all the lowly
Triumphant reach their home;
Stay not, till all the holy
Proclaim "The Lord is come."

title: Go preach the blest salvation
author: Sidney Dyer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Go preach the blest salvation
To every sinful race,
And bid each guilty nation
Accept the Savior's grace;
But bear, oh, quickly bear it
Where thronging millions roam,
And bid them freely share it,
Who dwell with us at home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Where blooms the broad savanna,
Where mighty waters roll,
There let the gospel banner
Beam hope on every soul;
Go where the west is teeming,
And yet behold they come!
The fields all ripe are gleaming
For those who reap at home!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Our children there are dwelling,
Neglected and astray,
Whose hearts are often swelling
To learn of Zion's way.
Bear, bear to them the treasure
And bid the exiles come;
There is no sweeter pleasure,
Than preaching Christ at home.

title: See the flag of Jesus
author: Priscilla J. Owens

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
See the flag of Jesus
O'er the earth unfurled!
Sabbath-schools are singing,
All around the world;
Sunday-schools in China,
India and Japan,
Training souls for glory,
By the gospel plan.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Lift the cross of Jesus,
Bear the Bible on;
Soon the world will echo,
With the vict'ry won.
See the flag of Jesus,
O'er the earth unfurled!
Sunday-schools are singing,
All around the world.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Little Indian diamonds,
Precious island pearls;
Learning Bible lessons,
Happy boys and girls.
Afric's gold dust scattered,
Neath the feet of wrong,
Rises up in brightness,
From the darkness long.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sunday-schools are singing,
France and Spain and Rome;
Hear their joyous music,
Songs of heaven and home.
Where the martyrs suffered,
Holy seed is spread;
Gather up these rubies,
Dyed in life-blood red.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sunday-schools in Chili,
Reaching down the coast;
Mexico is leading,
Gallant little host.
Glad Brazilian children,
Praise to God shall sing;
Far-off Patagonia
Answers Christ is King.

title: How beauteous on the mountains

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How beauteous on the mountains,
The feet of him that brings,
Like streams from living fountains,
Good tidings of good things;
That publisheth salvation,
And jubilee release,
To ev'ry tribe and nation,
God's reign of joy and peace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lift up thy voice, oh, watchman!
And shout from Zion's towers,
Thy hallelujah chorus—
"The victory is ours!"
The Lord shall build up Zion
In glory and renown,
And Jesus, Judah's lion,
Shall wear his rightful crown.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text: Benjamin Gough, 186-.

title: Soldiers of the cross! arise
author: William Walsham How

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Guard the helpless, seek the strayed,
Soothe the troubled, banish grief;
With the Spirit's sword arrayed,
Scatter sin and unbelief.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Be the banner still unfurled,
Bear it bravely still abroad,
Till the kingdoms of the world
Are the kingdoms of the Lord.

title: With thine own pity, Savior, see
author: Ray Palmer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With thine own pity, Savior, see
The thronged and darkening way!
We go to win the lost to thee,
Oh, help us, Lord, we pray!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou bid'st us go, with thee to stand
Against hell's marshalled powers;
And heart to heart, and hand to hand,
To make thine honor ours.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Teach thou our lips of thee to speak,
Of thy sweet love to tell;
Till they who wander far shall seek
And find and serve thee well.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O'er all the world thy Spirit send,
And make thy goodness known,
Till earth and heaven together blend
Their praises at thy throne.

title: Oh! still in accents sweet and strong
author: S. Longfellow

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh! still in accents sweet and strong
Sounds forth the ancient word,—
"More reapers for white harvest fields,
More laborers for the Lord!"

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We hear the call; in dreams no more
In selfish ease we lie,
But girded for our Father's work,
Go forth beneath his sky.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Where prophet's word, and martyr's blood,
And prayers of saints were sown,
We, to their labors entering in,
Would reap where they have strown.

title: Pour out thy Spirit from on high
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Wisdom, and zeal, and faith impart,
Firmness with meekness from above,
To bear thy people on our heart,
And love the souls whom thou dost love;

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Then, when our work is finished here,
In humble hope, our charge resign;
When the chief Shepherd shall appear,
O God! may they and we be thine.

title: The solemn service now is done
author: Samuel F. Smith

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The solemn service now is done.
The vow is pledged, the toil begun;
Seal thou, O God! the oath above,
And ratify the pledge of love.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Here let the ardent prayer arise,
Faith fix its grasp beyond the skies.
The tear of penitence be shed,
And myriads to the Savior led.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Oh, happy day, that fixed my choice
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, happy day, that fixed my choice,
On thee, my Savior and my God!
Well may this glowing heart rejoice,
And tell its raptures all abroad.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Happy day, happy day,
When Jesus washed my sins away;
He taught me how to watch and pray,
And live rejoicing ev'ry day!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, happy bond, that seals my vows
To him who merits all my love!
Let cheerful anthems fill the house,
While to his altar now I move.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Now rest—my long-divided heart—
Fixed on this blissful center, rest;
Here have I found a nobler part,
Here heavenly pleasures fill my breast.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
High Heaven, that heard the solemn vow,
That vow renewed shall daily hear,
Till, in life's latest hour, I bow,
And bless in death a bond so dear.

title: Come in, thou blessed of the Lord
author: Thomas Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come in, thou blessed of the Lord!
Enter in Jesus' precious name;
We welcome thee, with one accord,
And trust the Savior does the same.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Those joys, which earth cannot afford,
We'll seek in fellowship to prove,
Joined in one spirit to our Lord,
Together bound by mutual love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And, while we pass this vale of tears,
We'll make our joys and sorrows known;
We'll share each other's hopes and fears,
And count a brother's case our own.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: How sweet, how heavenly is the sight
author: Joseph Swain

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How sweet, how heavenly is the sight,
When those who love the Lord,
In one another's peace delight,
And so fulfill his word!—

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
When, free from envy, scorn, and pride,
Our wishes all above,
Each can his brother's failings hide,
And show a brother's love:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When love, in one delightful stream,
Through every bosom flows;
When union sweet, and dear esteem,
In every action glows.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Love is the golden chain, that binds
The happy souls above;
And he's an heir of heaven, that finds
His bosom glow with love.

title: Come in, beloved of the Lord
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come in, beloved of the Lord,
Stranger nor foe art thou;
We welcome thee with warm accord,
Our friend, our brother, now.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The hand of fellowship, the heart
Of love, we offer thee:
Leaving the world, thou dost but part
From lies and vanity.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come with us,—we will do thee good,
As God to us hath done;
Stand but in him, as those have stood
Whose faith the victory won.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And when, by turns, we pass away,
And star by star grows dim,
May each, translated into day,
Be lost and found in him.

title: Witness, ye men and angels! now
author: Benjamin Beddome

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Witness, ye men and angels! now,
Before the Lord we speak;
To him we make our solemn vow,
A vow we dare not break;—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That, long as life itself shall last,
Ourselves to Christ we yield;
Nor from his cause will we depart,
Or even quit the field.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We trust not in our native strength,
But on his grace rely;
That, with returning wants, the Lord
Will all our need supply.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh! guide our doubtful feet aright,
And keep us in thy ways;
And, while we turn our vows to prayers,
Turn thou our prayers to praise.

title: Blest be the tie that binds
author: John Fawcett

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest be the tie that binds
Our hearts in Christian love!
The fellowship of kindred minds
Is like to that above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Before our Father's throne,
We pour our ardent prayers;
Our fears, our hopes, our aims are one,
Our comforts and our cares.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
When we asunder part,
It gives us inward pain;
But we shall still be joined in heart,
And hope to meet again.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
This glorious hope revives
Our courage by the way;
While each in expectation lives,
And longs to see the day.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
From sorrow, toil, and pain,
And sin we shall be free;
And perfect love and friendship reign
Through all eternity.

title: And let our bodies part
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And let our bodies part—
To diff'rent climes repair;
Inseparably joined in heart
The friends of Jesus are.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, let us still proceed
In Jesus' work below;
And following our triumphant Head,
To further conquests go.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The vineyard of the Lord
Before his laborers lies;
And lo! we see the vast reward
Which waits us in the skies.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, let our heart and mind
Continually ascend,
That haven of repose to find,
Where all our labors end.

title: And are we yet alive
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And are we yet alive,
And see each other's face?
Glory and praise to Jesus give,
For his redeeming grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Preserved by power divine
To full salvation here,
Again in Jesus' praise we join,
And in his sight appear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
What troubles have we seen!
What conflicts have we passed!
Fightings without, and fears within,
Since we assembled last!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But out of all the Lord
Hath brought us by his love;
And still he doth his help afford,
And hides our life above.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Let us take up the cross,
Till we the crown obtain;
And gladly reckon all things loss
So we may Jesus gain.

title: How blest the hour when first we gave
author: S.F. Smith

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How blest the hour when first we gave
Our guilty souls to thee, O God;
A cheerful sacrifice of love,
Bought with the Savior's precious blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How blest the vow we here record!
How blest the grace we now receive!
Buried in baptism with our Lord,
New lives of holiness to live.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How blest the solemn rite that seals
Our death to sin, our guilt forgiven;—
How blest the emblem that reveals
God reconciled and peace with heaven.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thus through the emblematic grave
The glorious, suffering Savior trod;
Thou art our pattern, through the wave
We follow thee, blest Son of God.

title: My God! and is thy table spread
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God! and is thy table spread?
And does thy cup with love o'erflow?
Thither be all thy children led,
And let them all its sweetness know.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hail! sacred feast, which Jesus makes!
Rich banquet of his flesh and blood;
Thrice happy he, who here partakes
That sacred stream, that heavenly food!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh! let thy table honored be,
And furnished well with joyful guests;
And may each soul salvation see,
That here its sacred pledges tastes.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Jesus, thou Joy of loving hearts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, thou Joy of loving hearts!
Thou Fount of life! thou Light of men!
From the best bliss that earth imparts,
We turn unfilled to thee again.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
We taste thee, oh, thou living Bread!
And long to feast upon thee still;
We drink of thee, the Fountain Head,
And thirst our souls from thee to fill.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Our restless spirits yearn for thee,
Where'er our changeful lot is cast;
Glad, when thy gracious smile we see,
Blest, when our faith can hold thee fast.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text: Lat., Bernard, of Clairvaux, 1140. Tr., Ray Palmer, 1833.

title: Bread of heaven, on thee we feed
author: Josiah Conder

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Bread of heaven, on thee we feed
For thy flesh is meat indeed;
Ever let our souls be fed
With this true and living bread.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Day by day with strength supplied,
Thro' the life of him who died,
Lord of life, oh, let us be
Rooted, grafted, built on thee.

title: 'Twas on that dark, that dreadful night
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
'Twas on that dark, that dreadful night,
When powers of earth and hell arose
Against the Son of God's delight,
And friends betrayed him to his foes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Before the mournful scene began
He took the bread, and blessed and brake;
What love thro' all his actions ran!
What wondrous words of grace he spake!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
"This is my body, broke for sin;
Receive and eat the living food;"
Then took the cup, and blessed the wine:
"'Tis the new cov'nant in my blood."

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"Do this," he cried, "till time shall end,
In mem'ry of your dying Friend;
Meet at the table, and record
The love of your departed Lord."

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus, thy feast we celebrate;
We show thy death, we sing thy name
Till thou return, and we shall eat
The marriage supper of the Lamb.

title: While, in sweet communion, feeding
author: Edward Denny

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
While, in sweet communion, feeding
On this earthly bread and wine,
Savior, may we see thee bleeding
On the cross, to make us thine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Now, our eyes forever closing
To this fleeting world below,
On thy gentle breast reposing,
Teach us, Lord, thy grace to know.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Though unseen, be ever near us,
With the still small voice of love,
Whisp'ring words of peace to cheer us,
Ev'ry doubt and fear remove.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Bring before us all the story
Of thy life, and death of woe;
And, with hopes of endless glory,
Wean our hearts from all below.

title: That dreadful night before his death

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
That dreadful night before his death,
The Lamb, for sinners slain,
Did, almost with his dying breath,
This solemn feast ordain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To keep the feast, Lord, we have met,
And to remember thee;
Help each poor trembler to repeat—
For me he died, for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy suff'rings, Lord, each sacred sign
To our remembrance brings;
We eat the bread and drink the wine,
But think on nobler things.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, tune our tongues, and set in frame
Each heart that pants for thee,
To sing, Hosanna to the Lamb,
The Lamb that died for me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: Joseph Hart, d. 1768

title: "Till he come!" oh, let the words
author: E.H.B. Bickersteth

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
"Till he come!" oh, let the words
Linger on the trembling chords,
Let the "little while" between
In their golden light be seen;
Let us think how heav'n and home
Lie beyond that "Till he come!"

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When the weary ones we love
Enter on that rest above,
When their words of love and cheer
Fall no longer on our ear,
Hush! be ev'ry murmur dumb,
It is only "Till he come!"

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Clouds and darkness round us press;
Would we have one sorrow less?
All the sharpness of the cross,
All that tells the world is loss,
Death, and darkness, and the tomb
Pain us only "Till he come!"

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
See, the feast of love is spread,
Drink the wine and eat the bread:
Sweet memorials, till the Lord
Call us round his heavn'ly board;
Some from earth, from glory some,
Severed only "Till he come!"

title: We long to move and breathe in thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We long to move and breathe in thee,
Inspired with thine own breath,
To live thy life, O Lord, and be
Baptized into thy death.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy death to sin we die below,
But we shall rise in love;
We here are planted in thy woe,
But we shall bloom above.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Above we shall thy glory share,
As we thy cross have borne;
E'en we shall crowns of honor wear,
When we the thorns have worn.

title: Our children, Lord, in faith and prayer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our children, Lord, in faith and prayer
We now devote to thee;
Let them thy covenant mercies share,
And thy salvation see.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In early days their hearts secure
From worldly snares, we pray;
And let them to the end endure
In every righteous way.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Grant us before them, Lord, to live
In holy faith and fear;
And then to heaven our souls receive
And bring our children there.

title: It is not death to die
author: George W. Bethune

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
It is not death to die,—
To leave this weary road,
And, midst the brotherhood on high,
To be at home with God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It is not death to close
The eye long dimmed by tears,
And wake, in glorious repose
To spend eternal years.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
It is not death to fling
Aside this sinful dust,
And rise, on strong exulting wing,
To live among the just.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, thou Prince of life!
Thy chosen cannot die;
Like thee, they conquer in the strife,
To reign with thee on high.

title: Servant of God, well done
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Servant of God, well done!
Thy glorious warfare's past;
The battle's fought, the race is won,
And thou art crowned at last;—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Of all thy heart's desire
Triumphantly possessed;
Lodged by the ministerial choir
In thy Redeemer's breast.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In condescending love,
Thy ceaseless prayer he heard,
And bade thee suddenly remove
To thy complete reward.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
With saints enthroned on high,
Thou dost thy Lord proclaim,
And still to God salvation cry,—
Salvation to the Lamb!

title: A few more years shall roll
author: Horatius Bonar

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A few more years shall roll,
A few more seasons come,
And we shall be with those that rest
Asleep within the tomb.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A few more suns shall set
O'er these dark hills of time,
And we shall be where suns are not,
A far serener clime.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A few more storms shall beat
On this wild rocky shore,
And we shall be where tempests cease,
And surges swell no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A few more struggles here,
A few more partings o'er,
A few more toils, a few more tears,
And we shall weep no more.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
'Tis but a little while
And he shall come again,
Who died that we might live, who lives
That we with him may reign.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Then, O my Lord, prepare
My soul for that great day;
Oh, wash me in thy precious blood,
And take my sins away.

title: Days and moments quickly flying

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Days and moments quickly flying
Blend the living with the dead;
Soon shall we who sing be lying,
Each within our narrow bed.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Soon our souls to God who gave them
Will have sped their rapid flight;
Able now by grace to save them,
Oh, that while we can we might.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, infinite Redeemer,
Maker of this mighty frame,
Teach, oh, teach us to remember
What we are, and whence we came:—

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Whence we came, and whither wending
Soon we must through darkness go,
To inherit bliss unending,
Or eternity of woe.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: Rev. Edward Caswell, 1849.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Jesus, while our hearts are bleeding
author: Thomas Hastings

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, while our hearts are bleeding
O'er the spoils that death has won,
We would at this solemn meeting,
Calmly say,—thy will be done.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Though to-day we're filled with mourning,
Mercy still is on the throne;
With thy smiles of love returning,
We can sing—thy will be done.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
By thy hands the boon was given,
Thou hast taken but thine own:
Lord of earth, and God of heaven,
Evermore,—thy will be done!

title: Asleep in Jesus! blessed sleep
author: Mrs. Margaret Mackay

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Asleep in Jesus! blessed sleep,
From which none ever wakes to weep;
A calm and undisturbed repose,
Unbroken by the dread of foes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Asleep in Jesus! peaceful rest,
Whose waking is supremely blest;
No fear, no woes, shall dim the hour,
Which manifests the Savior's power.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Asleep in Jesus! oh, for me
May such a blissful refuge be;
Securely shall my ashes lie,
And wait the summons from on high.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Asleep in Jesus! far from thee
Thy kindred and their graves may be;
But thine is still a blessed sleep,
From whence none ever wake to weep.

title: How blest the righteous when he dies
author: Mrs. A.L. Barbauld

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How blest the righteous when he dies!
When sinks a weary soul to rest!
How mildly beam the closing eyes!
How gently heaves the expiring breast!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
A holy quiet reigns around,
A calm which life nor death destroys;
And naught disturbs that peace profound
Which his unfettered soul enjoys.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Life's labor done, as sinks the clay,
Light from its load the spirit flies,
While heaven and earth combine to say,
How blest the righteous when he dies!

title: Unveil thy bosom, faithful tomb
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Unveil thy bosom, faithful tomb;
Take this new treasure to thy trust
And give these sacred relics room,
To slumber in the silent dust.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Nor pain, nor grief, nor anxious fear,
Invades thy bounds; no mortal woes
Can reach the peaceful sleeper here,
While angels watch the soft repose.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So Jesus slept; God's dying Son
Passed through the grave, and blest the bed;
Rest here, blest saint, till from his throne
The morning break, and pierce the shade.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: So fades the lovely, blooming flower
author: Anne Steele

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
So fades the lovely, blooming flower—
Frail smiling solace of an hour!
So soon our transient comforts fly,
And pleasure only blooms to die.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Is there no kind, no lenient art,
To heal the anguish of the heart?
Spirit of grace! be ever nigh,
Thy comforts are not made to die.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Bid gentle patience smile on pain,
Till dying hope shall live again;
Hope wipes the tear from sorrow's eye
And faith points upward to the sky.

title: Why do we mourn departing friends
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Why do we mourn departing friends,
Or shake at death's alarms?
'Tis but the voice that Jesus sends,
To call them to his arms.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Are we not tending upward, too,
As fast as time can move?
Nor would we wish the hours more slow,
To keep us from our love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Why should we tremble to convey
Their bodies to the tomb?
There the dear flesh of Jesus lay,
And scattered all the gloom.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The graves of all the saints be blessed,
And softened every bed;
Where should the dying members rest,
But with the dying Head?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thence he arose, ascending high,
And showed our feet the way;
Up to the Lord we, too, shall fly
At the great rising-day.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: And let this feeble body fail
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And let this feeble body fail,
And let it faint or die;
My soul shall quit the mournful vale,
And soar to worlds on high—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Shall join the disembodied saints,
And find its long-sought rest;
That only bliss for which it pants,
In the Redeemer's breast.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In hope of that immortal crown
I now the cross sustain;
And gladly wander up and down,
And smile at toil and pain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I suffer on my three-score years,
Till my Deliverer come,
And wipes away his servant's tears,
And takes his exile home.

title: Why should our tears in sorrow flow
author: Wm. H. Bathurst

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Why should our tears in sorrow flow
When God recalls his own,
And bids them leave a world of woe,
For an immortal crown?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Is not e'en death a gain to those
Whose life to God was given?
Gladly to earth their eyes they close
To open them in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Their toils are past, their work is done,
And they are fully blest!
They fought the fight, the victory won,
And entered into rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then let our sorrows cease to flow,—
God has recalled his own;
But let our hearts, in every woe,
Still say, "Thy will be done!"

title: I would not live alway; I ask not to stay
author: W.A. Muhlenburg

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I would not live alway; I ask not to stay
Where storm after storm rises dark o'er the way;
The few cloudy mornings that dawn on us here
Are enough for life's woes, full enough for its cheer.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I would not live alway; no, welcome the tomb!
Since Jesus has lain there, I dread not its gloom;
There sweet be my rest till he bid me arise,
To hail him in triumph descending the skies.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Who, who would live alway, away from his God,
Away from yon heaven, that blissful abode,
Where the rivers of pleasure flow o'er the bright plains,
And the noontide of glory eternally reigns;

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Where the saints of all ages in harmony meet,
Their Savior and brethren transported to greet;
While the anthems of rapture unceasingly roll,
And the smile of the Lord is the feast of the soul?

title: "Thy will be | done!" || In devious way
author: Sir. J. Bowring

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
"Thy will be | done!" || In devious way
The hurrying stream of | life may | run; ||
Yet still our grateful hearts shall say, |
"Thy will be | done."

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Thy will be | done!" || If o'er us shine
A gladdening and a | prosperous | sun, ||
This prayer will make it more divine— |
"Thy will be | done!"

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
"Thy will be | done!" || Tho' shrouded o'er
Our | path with | gloom, | one comfort, one ||
Is ours:—to breathe, while we adore, |
"Thy will be | done."

title: My days are gliding swiftly by
author: David Nelson

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My days are gliding swiftly by,
And I a pilgrim stranger,
Would not detain them as they fly,
Those hours of toil and danger.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
For, oh! we stand on Jordan's strand,
Our friends are passing over;
And, just before, the shining shore
We may almost discover.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We'll gird our loins, my brethren dear!
Our heav'nly home discerning;
Our absent Lord has left us word,—
"Let ev'ry lamp be burning."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Should coming days be cold and dark,
We need not cease our singing;
That perfect rest none can molest,
Where golden harps are ringing.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let sorrow's rudest tempest blow,
Each cord on earth to sever;
Our King says,—"Come!" and there's our home,
Forever, oh! forever!

title: Wayfarers in the wilderness
author: Alexander R. Thompson

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Wayfarers in the wilderness,
By morn, and noon, and even,
Day after day, we journey on,
With weary feet toward heaven.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
O land above! O land of love!
The glory shineth o'er thee;
O Christ, our King! in mercy bring
Us thither, we implore thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
By day the cloud before us goes,
By night the cloud of fire,
To guide us o'er the trackless waste,
To Canaan ever nigher.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The sea was riven from our feet,
And so shall be the river;
And, by the King's highway brought home,
We'll praise his name forever:

title: One sweetly solemn thought
author: Phoebe Cary

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
One sweetly solemn thought
Comes to me o'er and o'er;
I'm nearer home to-day
Than e'er I've been before.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I'm nearer my home, nearer my home,
Nearer my home to-day;
Yes, nearer my home in heav'n to-day,
Than ever I've been before.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Nearer the bound where we
Must lay our burdens down,
Nearer to leave the cross,
Nearer to gain the crown.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The waves of that deep sea
Roll dark before my sight,
But break, the other side,
Upon a shore of light.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Oh! if my mortal feet
Have almost gained the brink,
If I am nearer home
To-day than e'en I think,

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Father! perfect my trust,
That I may rest, in death,
On Christ, my Lord, alone,
And thus resign my breath.

title: There is no flock, however watched and tended
author: Henry W. Longfellow

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is no flock, however watched and tended,
But one dead lamb is there!
There is no fireside, howsoe'er defended,
But has one vacant chair!
The air is full of farewells to the dying,
And mournings for the dead;
The heart of Rachel for her children crying
Will not be comforted!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let us be patient, these severe afflictions
Not from the ground arise,
But oftentimes celestial benedictions
Assume this dark disguise.
We see but dimly thro' the mists and vapors,
Amid these earthly damps,
What seem to us but sad, funereal tapers,
May be heav'ns distant lamps.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
She is not dead, the child of our affection,
But gone unto that school
Where she no longer needs our poor protection,
And Christ himself doth rule.
In that great cloister's stillness and seclusion,
By guardian angels led,
Safe from temptation, safe from sin's pollution,
She lives whom we call dead.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And tho' at times, impetuous with emotion,
And anguish long suppressed,
The swelling heart heaves moaning like the ocean
That cannot be at rest:
We will be patient—and assuage the feeling
We cannot wholly stay,
By silence sanctifying, not concealing
The grief that must have way.

title: Peace, be still
author: Schiller

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, my God!
Give me grace, that I may be
Thy true child, and silently
Own thy scepter and thy rod;
Lord, my God!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Shepherd mine!
From thy fullness give me still
Faith to do and bear thy will
Till the morning light shall shine;
Shepherd mine!

title: Rest, weary pilgrim, thy journey is o'er
author: Maria Straub

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rest, weary pilgrim, thy journey is o'er,
Rest, sweetly rest, on the beautiful shore;
Safely at last thou hast reached the bright goal,
Fatherland, home of the soul.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Never again shall thy storm-beaten breast
Sigh, deeply sigh, for the sweet "land of rest;"
Gone to the Savior's bright mansion above,
Rest in the light of his love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Rest, weary pilgrim, thy journey is o'er,
Rest, sweetly rest, on the beautiful shore;
Dangers and troubles shall harm thee no more,
Rest on the beautiful shore.

title: As fade the stars at morn away

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
As fade the stars at morn away,
Their glory gone in perfect day,
So pass away the friends we love,
Their presence lost in worlds above,
While we o'er their slumbers are weeping.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
As sink the stars when night is o'er,
To rise upon some other shore,
So sink our precious ones from sight,
In other skies to walk in light,
While we sorrow's vigils are keeping.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text: J.E. Rankin, D.D.

title: Midst sorrow and care

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Midst sorrow and care
There's one that is near,
And ever delights to relieve us.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis Jesus, our Friend,
On whom we depend
For life and for all its rich blessings.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: When thou, my righteous Judge, shalt come
author: Mrs. Selina Shirley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When thou, my righteous Judge, shalt come,
To take thy ransomed people home,
Shall I among them stand?
Shall such a worthless worm as I,
Who sometimes am afraid to die,
Be found at thy right hand?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I love to meet thy people now,
Before thy feet with them to bow,
Though vilest of them all;
But—can I bear the piercing thought?—
What if my name should be left out,
When thou for them shalt call?

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
And when the final trump shall sound,
Among thy saints let me be found,
To bow before thy face;
Then in triumphant strains I'll sing,
While heaven's resounding mansions ring
With praise of sovereign grace.

title: Lo! on a narrow neck of land
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lo! on a narrow neck of land,
Between two boundless seas I stand,—
Yet how insensible!
A point of time—a moment's space—
Removes me to yon heavenly place,
Or shuts me up in hell!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O God! my inmost soul convert,
And deeply on my thoughtless heart
Eternal things impress;
Give me to feel their solemn weight,
And save me, ere it be too late!
Wake me to righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Be this my one great business here,
With holy trembling, holy fear,
To make my calling sure;
Thine utmost counsel to fulfill,
To suffer all thy righteous will,
And to the end endure!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then Savior! then my soul receive,
Transported from the earth, to live
And reign with thee above;
Where faith is sweetly lost in sight,
And hope, in full supreme delight,
And everlasting love.

title: That awful day will surely come
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
That awful day will surely come,
Th' appointed hour makes haste,
When I must stand before the Judge
And pass the solemn test.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou lovely Chief of all my joys,
Thou Sovereign of my heart,
How could I bear to hear thy voice
Pronounce the sound, "Depart!"

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, wretched state of deep despair,
To see my God remove,
And fix my dreadful station where
I must not taste his love!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, tell me that my worthless name
Is graven on thy hands;
Show me some promise in thy book
Where my salvation stands.

title: And must I be to judgment brought
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And must I be to judgment brought,
And answer in that day,
For every vain and idle thought,
And every word I say?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Yes, every secret of my heart
Shall shortly be made known,
And I receive my just desert
For all that I have done.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How careful then I ought to live!
With what religious fear,
Who such a strict account must give
For my behavior here.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou awful Judge of quick and dead,
The watchful power bestow;
So shall I to my ways take heed,
To all I speak or do.

title: Jerusalem, the golden
author: J.M. Neale

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jerusalem, the golden,
With milk and honey blest!
Beneath thy contemplation
Sink heart and voice oppressed:
I know not, oh, I know not,
What social joys are there,
What radiancy of glory,
What light beyond compare.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
They stand, those halls of Zion,
All jubilant with song,
And bright with many an angel,
And all the martyr throng;
The Prince is ever in them,
The daylight is serene;
The pastures of the blessed
Are decked in glorious sheen.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There is the throne of David;
And there, from care released,
The song of them that triumph,
The shout of them that feast;
And they who, with their Leader,
Have conquered in the light,
Forever and forever
Are clad in robes of white.

title: For thee, O dear, dear country
author: J.M. Neale

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
For thee, O dear, dear country,
Mine eyes their vigils keep;
For very love, beholding
Thy happy name, they weep.
The mention of thy glory
Is unction to the breast,
And medicine in sickness,
And love, and life, and rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, sweet and blessed country,
The home of God's elect!
Oh, sweet and blessed country,
That eager hearts expect!
Jesus, in mercy bring us
To that dear land of rest;
Who art, with God the Father,
And Spirit, ever blest.

title: The sands of time are wasting
author: Annie Ross Cousin

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The sands of time are wasting,
The dawn of heaven breaks;
The summer morn I've sighed for,
The fair, sweet morn awakes.
Oh, dark hath been the midnight,
But day-spring is at hand,
And glory, glory dwelleth
In Immanuel's land.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, Christ, he is the fountain,
The deep, sweet well of love;
The streams of earth I've tasted,
More deep I'll drink above.
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory, glory dwelleth
In Immanuel's land.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, I am my Beloved's,
And my Beloved's mine;
He brings a poor, vile sinner
Into his house divine.
Upon the Rock of Ages
My soul, redeemed, shall stand,
Where glory, glory dwelleth
In Immanuel's land.

title: Jerusalem, the glorious

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jerusalem, the glorious!
The glory of th' elect,—
O dear and future vision
That eager hearts expect!
Ev'n now by faith I see thee,
Ev'n here thy walls discern;
To thee my thoughts are kindled,
And strive, and pant, and yearn!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The cross is all thy splendor,
The Crucified, thy praise;
His laud and benediction
Thy ransomed people raise;—
Jerusalem! exulting
On that securest shore,
I hope thee, wish thee, sing thee,
And love thee evermore!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O sweet and blessed country!
Shall I e'er see thy face?
O sweet and blessed country!
Shall I e'er win thy grace?—
Exult, O dust and ashes!
The Lord shall be thy part;
His only, his forever,
Thou shalt be, and thou art!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Bernard of Cluny, 1145.
J.M. Neale, tr. 1757

title: There is a land of pure delight
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a land of pure delight,
Where saints immortal reign;
Infinite day excludes the night,
And pleasures banish pain.
There everlasting spring abides,
And never-withering flowers;
Death, like a narrow sea, divides,
This heavenly land from ours.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sweet fields beyond the swelling flood
Stand dressed in living green;
So to the Jews old Canaan stood,
While Jordan rolled between.
But timorous mortals start and shrink
To cross this narrow sea,
And linger, shivering on the brink,
And fear to launch away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O could we make our doubts remove,
Those gloomy doubts that rise,
And see the Canaan that we love,
With unbeclouded eyes—
Could we but climb where Moses stood,
And view the landscape o'er,
Not Jordan's stream, nor death's cold flood,
Should fright us from the shore.

title: When I can read my title clear
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When I can read my title clear
To mansions in the skies,
I'll bid farewell to every fear
And wipe my weeping eyes.
Should earth against my soul engage,
And fiery darts be hurled,
Then I can smile at Satan's rage.
And face a frowning world.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let cares like a wild deluge come
Let storms of sorrow fall—
So I but safely reach my home,
My God, my heaven, my all.
There I shall bathe my weary soul
In seas of heavenly rest,
And not a wave of trouble roll
Across my peaceful breast.

title: Jerusalem! my glorious home

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jerusalem! my glorious home!
Name ever dear to me!
When shall my labors have an end,
In joy, and peace, and thee?
When shall these eyes thy heaven-built walls
And pearly gates behold?
Thy bulwarks with salvation strong,
And streets of shining gold?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, when, thou city of my God,
Shall I thy courts ascend,
Where congregations ne'er break up,
And Sabbaths have no end?
There happier bowers than Eden's bloom,
Nor sin nor sorrow know:
Blest seats! through rude and stormy scenes
I onward press to you.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Why should I shrink at pain and woe?
Or feel at death dismay?
I've Canaan's goodly land in view,
And realms of endless day.
Jerusalem! my glorious home!
My soul still pants for thee;
Then shall my labors have an end,
When I thy joys shall see.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text: Francis Baker (?), 1801.

title: Oh, think of the home over there
author: Rev. D.W.C. Huntington

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, think of the home over there,
By the side of the river of light,
Where the saints all immortal and fair,
Are robed in their garments of white.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Over there, over there,
Oh, think of the home over there;
Over there, over there, over there,
Oh, think of the home over there.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, think of the friends over there,
Who before us the journey have trod,
Of the songs that they breathe on the air.
In their home in the palace of God.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Over there, over there,
Oh, think of the friends over there;
Over there, over there, over there,
Oh, think of the friends over there.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My Savior is now over there,
There my kindred and friends are at rest;
Then away from my sorrow and care,
Let me fly to the land of the blest.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Over there, over there,
My Savior is now over there;
Over there, over there, over there,
My Savior is now over there.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I'll soon be at home over there,
For the end of my journey I see;
Many dear to my heart, over there,
Are watching and waiting for me.

sections.label: Chorus

title: There's a land that is fairer than day
author: S.F. Bennett

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There's a land that is fairer than day
And by faith we can see it afar;
For the Father waits over the way,
To prepare us a dwelling-place there.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
In the sweet by and by,
We shall meet on that beautiful shore;
In the sweet by and by,
We shall meet on that beautiful shore.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We shall sing on that beautiful shore
The melodious songs of the blest,
And our spirits shall sorrow no more,
Not a sigh for the blessing of rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To our bountiful Father above
We will offer the tribute of praise,
For the glorious gift of his love.
And the blessings that hallow our days.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We shall rest on that beautiful shore,
In the joys of the saved we shall share;
All our pilgrimage toil will be o'er,
And the conqueror's crown we shall wear.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
We shall meet, we shall sing, we shall reign,
In the land where the saved never die;
We shall rest, free from sorrow and pain,
Safe at home in the sweet by and by.

title: In the Christian's home in glory
author: William Hunter

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In the Christian's home in glory,
There remains a land of rest;
There my Savior's gone before me
To fulfill my soul's request.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
There is rest for the weary,
There is rest for the weary,
There is rest for the weary,
There is rest for you.
On the other side of Jordan,
In the sweet fields of Eden,
Where the tree of life is blooming,
There is rest for you.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He is fitting up my mansion,
Which eternally shall stand.
For my stay shall not be transient,
In that holy, happy land.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Pain and sickness ne'er shall enter,
Grief nor woe my lot shall share;
But, in that celestial center,
I a crown of life shall wear.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Death itself shall then be vanquished
And his sting shall be withdrawn;
Shout for gladness, oh, ye ransomed
Hail with joy the rising morn

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Sing, oh! sing, ye heirs of glory
Shout your triumph as you go;
Zion's gate will open for you,
You shall find an entrance through.

title: This is not my place of resting
author: H. Bonar

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
This is not my place of resting,—
Mine's a city yet to come;
Onward to it I am hasting—
On to my eternal home.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
There the Lamb, our Shepherd, leads us
By the streams of life along—
On the freshest pastures feeds us,
Turns our sighing into song.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Soon we pass this desert dreary,
Soon we bid farewell to pain;
Never more are sad or weary,
Never, never sin again!

title: There is an hour of peaceful rest
author: Wm. B. Tappan

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is an hour of peaceful rest
To mourning wand'rers giv'n;
There is a joy for souls distressed,
A balm for ev'ry wounded breast—
'Tis found above—in heav'n.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There is a soft, a downy bed,
'Tis fair as breath of even;
A couch for weary mortals spread,
Where they may rest the aching head,
And find repose—in heav'n.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There is a home for weary souls,
By sin and sorrow driv'n;
When tossed on life's tempestuous shoals,
Where storms arise, and ocean rolls,
And all is drear—but heav'n.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There faith lifts up her cheerful eye,
To brighter prospects giv'n;
And views the tempest passing by,
The evening shadows quickly fly,
And all serene—in heav'n.

title: My heavenly home is bright and fair
author: Rev. William Hunter

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
sections.text:
I'm going home, I'm going home,
I'm going home to die no more,
To die no more, to die no more,
I'm going home to die no more.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Let others seek a home below,
Which flames devour, or waves o'erflow,
Be mine a happier lot, to own
A heavenly mansion near the throne.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then fail this earth, let stars decline,
And sun and moon refuse to shine
All nature sink and cease to be,
That heavenly mansion stands for me.

title: 'Mid scenes of confusion and creature complaints
author: David Denham

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
'Mid scenes of confusion and creature complaints,
How sweet to my soul is communion with saints;
To find at the banquet of mercy there's room,
And feel in the presence of Jesus at home.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Home! home! sweet, sweet home!
Prepare me, dear Savior, for glory, my home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sweet bonds that unite all the children of peace,
And thrice precious Jesus whose love cannot cease,
Tho' oft from thy presence in sadness I roam,
I long to behold thee in glory at home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I sigh from this body of sin to be free,
Which hinders my joy and communion with thee;
Tho' now my temptations like billows may foam,
All, all will be peace when I'm with thee at home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
While here in the valley of conflict I stay,
Oh, give me submission and strength as my day,
In all my afflictions to thee would I come,
Rejoicing in hope of my glorious home.

title: We shall meet beyond the river
author: Rev. John Atkinson

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We shall meet beyond the river,
By and by, by and by;
And the darkness shall be over,
By and by, by and by;
With the toilsome journey done,
And the glorious battle won,
We shall shine forth as the sun,
By and by, by and by.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We shall strike the harps of glory,
By and by, by and by;
We shall sing redemption's story.
By and by, by and by;
And the strains for evermore
Shall resound in sweetness o'er
Yonder everlasting shore,
By and by, by and by.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We shall see and be like Jesus,
By and by, by and by;
Who a crown of life will give us,
By and by, by and by;
And the angels who fulfill
All the mandates of his will
Shall attend, and love us still,
By and by, by and by.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There our tears shall all cease flowing,
By and by, by and by;
And with sweetest rapture knowing,
By and by, by and by;
All the blest ones who have gone
To the land of life and song,—
We with shoutings shall rejoin,
By and by, by and by.

title: I saw a way-worn trav'ler
author: J.B. Matthias

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I saw a way-worn trav'ler,
In tattered garments clad,
And struggling up the mountain,
It seemed that he was sad;
His back was laden heavy,
His strength was almost gone,
Yet he shouted as he journeyed,
Deliverance will come.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Then palms of victory, crowns of glory,
Palms of victory I shall wear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The summer sun was shining,
The sweat was on his brow,
His garments worn and dusty,
His step seemed very slow;
But he kept pressing onward,
For he was wending home;
Still shouting as he journeyed,
Deliverance will come.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The songsters in the arbor
That stood beside the way
Attracted his attention,
Inviting his delay;
His watchword being "Onward,"
He stopped his ears and run,
Still shouting as he journeyed,
Deliverance will come.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I saw him in the evening,
The sun was bending low,
He'd overtopped the mountain
And reached the vale below;
He saw the golden city,—
His everlasting home,—
And shouted loud, Hosanna,
Deliverance will come!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
While gazing on that city,
Just o'er the narrow flood,
A band of holy angels
Came from the throne of God;
They bore him on their pinions
Safe o'er the dashing foam,
And joined him in his triumph,—
Deliverance has come!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
I heard the song of triumph
They sang upon that shore,
Saying, Jesus has redeemed us
To suffer nevermore:
Then, casting his eyes backward
On the race which he had run,
He shouted loud, Hosanna,
Deliverance has come!

title: I will sing you a song of that beautiful land
author: Mrs. Ellen H. Gates

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I will sing you a song of that beautiful land,
The far away home of the soul;
Where no storms ever beat on the glittering strand,
While the years of eternity roll.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, that home of the soul, in my visions and dreams
Its bright jasper walls I can see;
Till I fancy but thinly the veil intervenes
Between the fair city and me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
That unchangeable home is for you and for me,
Where Jesus of Nazareth stands,
The King of all kingdoms forever is he,
And he holdeth our crowns in his hands.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, how sweet it will be in that beautiful land,
So free from all sorrow and pain;
With songs on our lips and with harps in our hands,
To meet one another again.

title: "Forever with the Lord!"
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
"Forever with the Lord!"
Amen, so let it be;
Life from the dead is in that word,
'Tis immortality.
Here in the body pent,
Absent from him I roam,
Yet nightly pitch my moving tent
A day's march nearer home;
Nearer home, nearer home,
A day's march nearer home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My Father's house on high,
Home of my soul, how near,
At times, to faith's aspiring eye
Thy golden gates appear.
Ah! then my spirit faints
To reach the land I love;
The bright inheritance of saints—
Jerusalem above;
Home above, home above,
Jerusalem above.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yet doubts still intervene,
And all my comfort flies;
Like Noah's dove, I flit between
Rough seas and stormy skies.
Anon the clouds depart,
The wind and waters cease,
While sweetly o'er my gladdened heart
Expands the bow of peace;
Bow of peace, bow of peace,
Expands the bow of peace.

title: On Jordan's stormy banks I stand
author: Samuel Stennett

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
On Jordan's stormy banks I stand,
And cast a wishful eye
To Canaan's fair and happy land,
Where my possessions lie.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
We will rest in the fair and happy land,
Just across on the evergreen shore,
Sing the song of Moses and the Lamb, by and by,
And dwell with Jesus evermore.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O'er all those wide-extended plains
Shines one eternal day;
There God the Son forever reigns
And scatters night away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When shall I reach that happy place,
And be forever blest?
When shall I see my Father's face,
And in his bosom rest?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Filled with delight, my raptured soul
Would here no longer stay;
Tho' Jordan's waves around me roll,
Fearless I'd launch away.

title: Shall we gather at the river
author: Robert Lowry

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Shall we gather at the river
Where bright angel feet have trod;
With its crystal tide forever
Flowing by the throne of God.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Yes, we'll gather at the river,
The beautiful, the beautiful river,—
Gather with the saints at the river
That flows by the throne of God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On the margin of the river
Washing up its silver spray,
We will walk and worship ever,
All the happy, golden day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ere we reach the shining river
Lay we ev'ry burden down;
Grace our spirits will deliver,
And provide a robe and crown.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
At the smiling of the river
Mirror of the Savior's face,
Saints whom death will never sever
Lift their songs of saving grace.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Soon we'll reach the silver river,
Soon our pilgrimage will cease;
Soon our happy hearts will quiver
With the melody of peace.

title: Oh, I often sit and ponder
author: Miss Jennie Stout

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh, I often sit and ponder,
When the sun is sinking low,
Where shall yonder future find me?
Does but God in heaven know?
Shall I be among the living?
Shall I be among the free?
Wheresoe'er my path be leading,
Savior, keep my heart with thee.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Oh, the future lies before me,
And I know not where I'll be;
But where'er my path be leading,
Savior, keep my heart with thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Shall I be at work, for Jesus,
Whilst he leads me by the hand,
And to those around be saying,
Come and join this happy band?
Come, for all things now are ready,
Come, his faithful foll'wer be;
Oh, where'er my path be leading,
Savior, keep my heart with thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But perhaps my work for Jesus
Soon in future may be done,
All my earthly trials ended,
And my crown in heaven won;
Then forever with the ransomed
Thro' eternity I'd be
Chanting hymns to him who bo't me
With his blood, shed on a tree.

title: The evening shades are falling
author: Rev. W. Gossett

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The evening shades are falling,
The sun is sinking fast;
The Holy One is calling,
We're going home at last.

sections.label: Chorus
Verse 2
sections.text:
The road's been long and dreary,
The toils came thick and fast;
In body weak and weary,
Were going home at last.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We now are nearing heaven,
And soon shall be at rest;
Our crowns will soon be given,
We're going home at last.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: I think when I read that sweet story of old
author: Mrs. Jemima Luke

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I think when I read that sweet story of old,
When Jesus was here among men,
How he called little children as lambs to his fold,
I should like to have been with them then.

sections.label: Chorus
Verse 2
sections.text:
I wish that his hands had been placed on my head,
His arms had been thrown around me,
And that I might have seen his kind look when he said,
"Let the little ones come unto me."

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
"Let the little ones come unto me,"
"Let the little ones come unto me,"
And that I might have seen his kind look when he said,
"Let the little ones come unto me."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yet still to his footstool in prayer I may go,
And ask for a share in his love;
And if I now earnestly seek him below,
I shall see him and hear him above.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I shall see him and hear him above,
I shall see him and hear him above,
And if I now earnestly seek him below,

title: By cool Siloam's shady rill
author: Reginald Heber

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
By cool Siloam's shady rill,
How fair the lily grows!
How sweet the breath, beneath the hill,
Of Sharon's dewy rose!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lo! such the child whose early feet
The paths of peace have trod,
Whose secret heart, with influence sweet,
Is upward drawn to God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By cool Siloam's shady rill
The lily must decay;
The rose that blooms beneath the hill
Must shortly fade away.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And soon, too soon, the wintry hour
Of man's maturer age
Will shake the soul with sorrow's pow'r.
And stormy passions rage.

title: God of the universe! to thee
author: Miss Mary O----

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of the universe! to thee
This sacred house we rear,
And now, with songs and bended knee,
Invoke thy presence here.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Long may this echoing dome resound
The praises of thy name,
These hallowed walls to all around
The Triune God proclaim.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
And, when the last long Sabbath morn
Upon the just shall rise,
May all who own thee here be borne
To mansions in the skies.

title: Arise, O King of grace, arise
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Arise, O King of grace, arise,
And enter to thy rest;
Lo! thy church waits, with longing eyes,
Thus to be owned and blest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Enter with all thy glorious train.
Thy Spirit and thy word;
All that the ark did once contain
Could no such grace afford.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here, mighty God, accept our vows,
Here let thy praise be spread;
Bless the provisions of thy house
And fill thy poor with bread.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here let the Son of David reign,
Let God's Anointed shine;
Justice and truth his court maintain
With love and power divine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Here let him hold a lasting throne,
And as his kingdom grows,
Fresh honors shall adorn his crown.
And shame confound his foes.

title: 'Tis thine alone, almighty Name
author: Edwin F. Hatfield

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
'Tis thine alone, almighty Name,
To raise the dead to life,
The lost inebriate to reclaim
From passion's fearful strife.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What ruin hath intemperance wrought,
How widely roll its waves!
How many myriads hath it brought
To fill dishonored graves!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And see, O Lord! what numbers still
Are maddened by the bowl,
Led captive at the tyrant's will,
In bondage heart and soul!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
